summary: Solar tower power plants provide dispatchable, renewable energy by concentrating sunlight with thousands of mirrors, called heliostats, onto a central receiver. Efficient operation requires accurate modeling of the optical path from each heliostat to the receiver and compensation for manufacturing imperfections, kinematic misalignment, and material degradation that distort the flux distribution. Conventional ray tracers predict the flux from an assumed plant model but are limited to forward simulation. They cannot recover unknown plant parameters from measured flux nor directly optimize plant operation. We present artist, an open-source, FAIR4RS-compliant Python package implementing a fully differentiable digital twin of solar tower power plants. By making the optical pipeline, comprising heliostat surface representation, kinematics, blocking, and ray tracing, end to end differentiable, artist turns the digital twin from a passive forward model into an active physics-based tool for inverse modeling and data-driven optimization. The resulting gradient-based framework unifies tasks usually handled by separate solutions, such as reconstructing heliostat surfaces and kinematics from operational flux images without costly deflectometry, predicting irradiance at the receiver, and optimizing aim points to realize a desired receiver flux density distribution. Built on PyTorch, artist scales to real plants through GPU acceleration, a structure-of-arrays memory layout, and nested data parallelism. It interfaces with open data sources such as the PAINT database. We describe the software architecture, physical models, and optimization framework, and demonstrate the workflow on representative tasks. By integrating modeling, prediction, and optimization into a single open, interpretable package, artist provides a principled foundation for data-driven research toward autonomous solar tower operation.

summary: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties from measurements. We develop a comprehensive suite of property identification tasks focused on hardware mechanisms relevant to Spectre-class attacks, covering speculative execution, branch prediction, memory dependence, and cache behavior. We evaluate ProcReverser on the XuanTie C910, the gem5 RISC-V O3 CPU model, and the SiFive P550. ProcReverser achieves Pass@1 and Pass@5 scores of 81.3% and 93.8%, respectively, on C910, and 83.0% and 100.0% on gem5 O3. On the SiFive P550, ProcReverser further characterizes microarchitectural properties covered by the proposed task suite. These findings highlight the potential of automated microarchitectural reverse engineering to support processor vulnerability analysis and defense evaluation.
title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis

summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models (LLMs) activate only a few experts per token while generally keeping all the experts in GPU memory for high efficiency. Expert pruning reduces this GPU memory footprint cost, yet discards the contribution of pruned experts. Existing remedies either rely on static substitutes, merge experts at the cost of altering their functions, or require costly recovery training. In this paper, we find that the functionalities of pruned experts can be efficiently reconstructed from the activated remaining experts. We propose GEAR (Gated Expert Activation Reuse), which reuses the scaled outputs of reliable activated experts without any training or additional expert computation. In addition, we propose GEAR$^2$ to further recover what reuse cannot express with an ultra-lightweight residual. On five MoE LLMs from 16B to 106B parameters with 25% and 50% of experts pruned, GEAR improves over its training-free counterparts in nearly every setting (up to 4 pp.) in terms of accuracy, and GEAR$^2$ outperforms baseline approaches (up to 2.75 pp.) in every setting on nine zero-shot benchmarks, with larger advantages (up to 2.72 pp. higher) under more aggressive pruning (up to 50%).
title: GEAR$^2$: Pruned Experts Live On through Gated Reuse of Activated Experts and a Missing-Mass Residual

summary: Speculative decoding reduces generation cost, but it stores two KV caches: one for the target model and one for the draft model. We reduce this extra memory by quantizing the draft cache. The target cache and verifier remain in BF16, so that compression cannot change the target model's final correction rule. We first study how to divide precision between keys and values. A naive per-token quantizer makes keys appear much more sensitive: splitting a 12-bit budget, K8V4 beats K4V8 in acceptance by 10.87pp. However, with grouped per-channel keys, the gap becomes -0.25pp. A controlled Qwen test confirms that changing only the key quantizer can erase or reverse the preferred bit split. Hence, following KIVI, we propose K4V4 quantization with per-channel keys and per-token values. Across six model pairs, our method reduces draft cache memory by 66.20%, and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%. Mean acceptance drops from 57.93% to 57.14%, only 1.36% relative. Overall, quantized draft caches can make speculative decoding more memory efficient; as a predictive principle for efficient AI design, key and value precision must be co-designed with the quantizer layout.
title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache

summary: Latent KV cache compression reduces memory footprint by mapping historical keys and values into compact representations. However, generic compressed key states require reconstruction to native dimension before applying RoPE and computing attention scores, adding sequence-scaling overhead to the decode path. We characterize when a latent KV representation can serve directly as the execution state of pretrained RoPE. For RoPE-based transformers, exact static linear execution of the rotary key path requires the latent-to-native map to preserve the pretrained RoPE action through an intertwining relation, restricting exact mixing to coordinates that share the same RoPE frequency. Guided by this characterization, we build GaugeRoPE, a training-free executable latent KV representation. It combines a RoPE-compatible carrier that preserves the rotary action with an approximate position-independent residual key--value (RKV) correction for complementary key and value information, both evaluated without per-token dense historical K/V reconstruction. On Mistral-7B, GaugeRoPE achieves $5.85\times$ KV compression while maintaining quality close to the full-cache baseline. Additional MHA results validate the construction beyond GQA. GaugeRoPE achieves up to $2.48\times$ the decode throughput of the vanilla uncompressed baseline through direct latent execution.
title: GaugeRoPE: RoPE-Compatible Executable Latent Attention

summary: Obesity is a growing public health issue in New Zealand, increasing the risk of chronic diseases and exacerbating health disparities. Mobile health (mHealth) initiatives, such as smartphone apps, have showed promise in improving weight management and physical exercise. FatSecret, a popular software for tracking nutrition and activity, may help people lose weight, but its efficacy across ethnic groups and areas in New Zealand is uncertain. The primary goal is to determine the efficacy of the FatSecret app in promoting weight loss and boosting physical activity among overweight and obese people in New Zealand. The secondary purpose is to investigate potential differences in intervention effectiveness based on ethnicity (European, Māori, Asian, and Pacific Islanders) and living place (urban or rural). A two-arm, parallel, randomized controlled trial design will be used. Adult volunteers (aged 18–65 years, BMI ≥25 kg/m²) from various ethnic groups and areas in New Zealand will be recruited and randomly assigned 1:1 to the intervention or control group, stratified by ethnicity and region. The intervention group will receive a 12-week weight management and physical activity program given via the FatSecret app, while the control group will not use the app and will continue with their usual lifestyle. The primary outcome is the change in body weight between baseline and 12 weeks. Secondary objectives include changes in body fat percentage, waist circumference, physical activity level measured using established methods, and health-related quality of life. This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the FatSecret app’s effectiveness in promoting weight loss and physical activity among New Zealand’s overweight and obese individuals. The study design allows for the evaluation of potential differences in intervention effectiveness across ethnic groups and residential locations, which will inform the creation of culturally appropriate and geographically targeted mHealth therapies for obesity control. If proven effective, the FatSecret app might be widely promoted and integrated into national health policies to combat the obesity pandemic and minimize health disparities. Potential limitations include self-reported data for some outcomes and the short intervention duration. summary: Modern AI assistants, agents, and decision-support systems increasingly rely on information beyond model parameters by retrieving documents, accessing memory, invoking tools, and combining external evidence. Retrieval-Augmented Generation is one prominent realization of this broader information-grounding paradigm. Yet external grounding does not by itself ensure trustworthiness. Systems can still fail under incomplete, noisy, conflicting, or misleading evidence, and these failures become harder to diagnose as retrieval, reasoning, memory, tool use, and generation interact. Existing evaluation frameworks measure important aspects of system quality, but do not necessarily ensure deliberate coverage of the conditions most likely to expose system vulnerabilities. We introduce PRISM as a methodology for systematic stress testing of retrieval-grounded AI through controlled synthetic data generation. Rather than treating evaluation data as a static benchmark, PRISM constructs and validates document and question-answer pairs designed to reproduce deployment-relevant failure conditions. Its 25 evaluation instruments are organized across ten diversity dimensions and eight thematic clusters, covering conditions such as fragmented or noisy evidence, lexical and semantic mismatch, unanswerable queries, and adversarial or epistemically unreliable content. Because these conditions are generated synthetically, they can reproduce relevant document and evidence characteristics without requiring access to proprietary or sensitive operational data. Stress conditions are also linked to concrete system choices to support targeted diagnosis. PRISM is expected to provide reproducible and traceable evaluation artifacts that help reveal vulnerabilities before deployment and distinguish failures originating from retrieval, evidence selection, generation, or abstention. Automated construction and validation are also intended to reduce the manual effort associated with human-curated evaluation sets while preserving the control, coverage, and consistency needed for systematic evaluation. More broadly, PRISM reframes evaluation as not only a measurement problem but also an experimental-design problem. By complementing existing metrics, human evaluation, observability, and post-deployment monitoring, it contributes toward more systematic pre-deployment assessment of increasingly agentic, retrieval-grounded AI systems.
title: Toward Trustworthy Retrieval-Grounded AI through Synthetic Stress Testing

summary: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 43 examines the governance and evidence requirements that arise when artificial intelligence influences consequential business decisions. The paper defines a decision chain of custody as a controlled, verifiable record connecting the information used, systems involved, applicable policies, delegated authority, approvals, execution and preserved evidence behind an AI-influenced decision. Its central operating test is independent reconstruction: an authorised reviewer should be able to determine what happened, which authority permitted the action and how the resulting business state was verified without relying on the original operator's memory. The analysis distinguishes decision custody from related concepts including accuracy, explainability, data lineage, observability and content provenance. It argues that these controls answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable forms of transparency. Content provenance might identify the history of a digital asset, for example, while providing no evidence that a user held authority to approve a payment or that the resulting transaction was correctly executed. The paper proposes eight linked evidence domains for consequential AI-influenced decisions: information received, intelligence used, rules applied, tools invoked, state changed, authority held, outcome approved and evidence preserved. These domains connect through a shared decision identifier and are intended to preserve relationships between initial inputs, policy evaluation, delegated authority, approval, execution and verified outcome. Particular attention is given to the moment of commitment, when an AI-generated recommendation becomes an external or financial business action. The paper argues that approvals must remain linked to the material terms ultimately executed. Changes to amount, recipient, purpose or other material conditions require a defined re-evaluation path rather than reliance on an earlier approval. The paper also addresses delegation across multiple agents and systems, retry behaviour, transaction reconciliation, evidence integrity, retention, human oversight and supplier evidence obligations. It distinguishes reconstruction from reproduction and outcome verification, noting that exact reproduction of stochastic model output is neither always possible nor necessary for reconstructing observable system behaviour. Three cases illustrate different dimensions of the argument. IBM provides company-reported evidence of reduced data-clearance processing time within an integrated governance programme. HSBC demonstrates large-scale financial-crime detection alongside explainable and auditable investigative outputs. AstraZeneca provides published evidence concerning the organisational scope and challenges of ethics-based AI auditing. None of these cases is presented as proof of a complete decision-custody architecture. The paper proposes consequence-based evidence requirements, independent reconstruction tests, explicit stop conditions for missing authority or mandatory evidence, supplier acceptance tests and measurable indicators including reconstruction pass rate, authority coverage, approval match, outcome reconciliation and preservation verification. The chapter concludes that auditability after an AI-influenced decision is becoming as important as intelligence before the decision. Enterprises expanding autonomous authority should first demonstrate that completed consequential decisions can be independently reconstructed from preserved evidence with clear ownership, valid authority and verified outcomes. The eight-domain decision record, consequence-based evidence model, reconstruction tests and associated management controls are author-developed conceptual frameworks informed by established provenance, AI governance, legal and assurance sources. They are not externally validated standards or universal legal requirements.
title: The 2026 AI Inflection Series, Chapter 43: Every AI Decision Needs a Chain of Custody

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: for 1 < p < 2 this paper finds the exact Schatten-norm constant for sums of matrix moduli when there are at least as many matrices as the matrix size, gives a new general upper bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , and certifies in exact arithmetic that rank-one matrices do not give the answer to Lee’s two-matrix problem. The question. For numbers, |a+b| ≤ |a|+|b|. A matrix A has a natural absolute value |A| = (A*A) 1/2 , but for matrices the size of a sum can exceed the size of the sum of the absolute values. Measuring size by the Schatten p-norm (p = 1 is the trace norm, p = 2 the Frobenius norm), one asks for the smallest constant c with ‖A 1 +…+A m ‖ p ≤ c ‖|A 1 |+…+|A m |‖ p . What was known. Eun-Young Lee (2010, 2012) asked for the best constant for two matrices. Lin and Zhang (2022) settled p = 2; Tang and Zhang extended the question to m matrices and conjectured a formula; Qiu (2026) proved it for p ≥ 2; below p = 2 the formula fails, by counterexamples of Zeng, Liu and Ratnavelu, of Pang and of Qiu, all built from rank-one matrices. The survey of Bourin and Zhang (2026) lists the range 1 < p < 2 as open. Results (1 < p < 2, n-by-n matrices). (1) When m ≥ n the best constant is an explicit one-variable maximum D p,n ; it depends only on the rank of the sum of the moduli, every equality case is classified, and for m < n the constant is strictly smaller. Consequently the best constant for rank-one summands is D p,min(m,n) in every dimension. (2) The best constant is log-convex in 1/p, so interpolating between p = 1 and p = 2 gives the dimension-free bound ((1+√m)/2) 1−1/p , better than the previous m (p−1)/(2p) for every m ≥ 2 (for two matrices at p = 3/2: 1.0648 instead of 1.1225, while the true value is at least 1.0364). (3) For two 3-by-3 matrices a computer-assisted proof in exact rational and interval arithmetic shows that the best rank-one value is beaten at nine exponents between 11/10 and 17/10. How. The sum is written as a product of two block matrices and Hölder’s inequality is applied; the problem reduces to comparing two Rényi entropies of the spectrum, whose extremal shape is one large eigenvalue and the rest equal. This extends T. Zhang’s Frobenius-norm argument; the matching examples are Pang’s, with a re-tuned parameter. Limits. The exact constant for two matrices of arbitrary size (Lee’s problem) for 1 < p < 2 remains open, as does the case m < n; the interpolation bound is not sharp; the certified excess over the rank-one value is tiny (about 10 −5 to 10 −7 ) and covers nine specific exponents, not an interval. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF) with Figure 1; the certificate script certify_rank_gap.py with its exact rational witnesses; verify_schatten.py (128 numerical checks of the scalar constant, equality families, adversarial searches, the bounds table and asymptotics, with negative controls); the figure script; recorded outputs; the bibliography from registry records; a machine-readable index; a research-gate record; a rating-free review summary; a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Assurance. Written proofs, except one computer-assisted proof in exact arithmetic (Proposition 2.5). summary: The Brina Gap measures the difference between the growth a company can self-finance and the growth its market price already assumes.  Its fundamental arm is the sustainable-growth ceiling,  g f  = ROIC × Reinvestment Rate; its pricing arm is the market-implied growth  g *, recovered from a reverse discounted-cash-flow on enterprise value. Both come from public filings, so the Gap makes the market's embedded growth expectation explicit — mechanically, reproducibly, and without an analyst's private valuation. Stated in growth units, it is the only kind of valuation claim that can be checked against what firms later deliver —  and it checks out. On the complete point-in-time S&P 500 (2010–2024, survivorship-free), the market-implied growth  g * genuinely tracks the growth firms subsequently realize (correlation ≈ 0.4–0.5, nearly unbiased at the 10-year horizon) and is robust across independent recovery methods (Spearman 0.73–1.00).  The Brina Gap is a detector of over-extrapolated growth expectations:  the market systematically over-extrapolates growth — the calibration slope sits below one at every horizon — and the median firm priced for high growth under-delivers what its price implies (≈ 26% priced in vs ≈ 22% realized).  Head-to-head against the classical Margin of Safety, the Gap is mechanical and falsifiable where the Margin of Safety is not, nearly orthogonal to it in cross-section, and more accurate on the one directional test both can take (+3.9 points, p ≈ .004; the Gap's expensive-side calls were correct 58.9% of the time on the full universe).  Among all pure valuation metrics tested — book-to-market, earnings yield, EPV, the Margin of Safety — the Brina Gap ranks first, and it is the only one whose central claim can be verified at all.  Its practical form is the  Brina Matrix , which crosses the Gap's pricing read with fundamental quality and yields one rule that survives every specification tested:  "cheap" is only a bargain when quality is high — cheap plus low quality is the value trap, the worst-performing cell in the sample. summary: Unrefereed research candidate. Proof of the Mogilnykh–Vorob’ev–Valyuzhenich conjecture, the exact Rényi minimum for sampling without replacement, and the hypergeometric tail problem from n = 4k. The question. Pick k of n given real numbers at random, without replacement, and add them. How concentrated can that random sum be? The paper answers three classical forms of this question exactly: how often the sum can be exactly zero, how small its entropy can be, and how rarely it can be nonnegative. Results. (1) Zero sums. If the numbers add up to zero and are not all zero, at least 2·C(n−2, k−1) of the k-subsets have a nonzero sum whenever k ≥ 5 and n ≥ 2k+1, and only the pattern (1, −1, 0, …, 0), up to scaling and reordering, attains this. This is the smallest support of an eigenfunction in the first nontrivial eigenspace of the Johnson graph, and proves Conjecture 1 of Mogilnykh, Vorob’ev and Valyuzhenich (2018), who had checked it by computer for n ≤ 600. A formula with all equality cases is given for every n and k, including the case (1, 1, −1, −1, 0) at n = 5, k = 2 that earlier classifications missed (Theorem 1.1). (2) Entropy. The minimum Rényi entropy of the sum is found for every finite order, answering a question of Ai, Kuželka and Pelekis (2026): one outlier is optimal except at half-sampling (n = 2k), where two outliers win above an explicit order α k (α 2 = 2, about 1.386k for large k). So the universal Bernoulli lower bound holds exactly for orders up to 2 (Theorems 1.2 and 1.3, Corollary 1.4). (3) Tails. For two-valued populations, the probability that the sum is at least its mean is at least k/n whenever n ≥ 4k, with a single outlier the unique minimiser for n > 4k (Theorem 1.5); Ai and Pelekis (2026) had n ≥ 8k. The proof uses a 2026 lemma of Ai, Karagiannis, Kuželka and Pelekis. Consequently the Aydinian–Blinovsky conjecture (that two-valued populations are the worst case) would imply the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture for all n ≥ 4k. This does not prove the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture, and below 4k a single outlier is not always the worst case. (4) Exact analogues over Abelian groups, where elements of order two change the answer at half-sampling (Theorem 1.6), and a small-ball inequality for sampling without replacement; a known incidence-rank result is re-derived. Limits. Real numbers only for the zero-sum theorem (it fails over Z 2 , Z 3 and Z 5 ); first Johnson eigenspace only; the tail problem below n = 4k is open. Finite computer checks corroborate but do not replace the written proofs. Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF); five standard-library Python scripts of exact finite checks (each runs in seconds and exits nonzero on any failure, also under python -O) with their recorded outputs; a claim ledger and prior-art note; the bibliography from registry records; a machine-readable index; a research-gate record; a rating-free review summary; a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Assurance. Complete written proofs for every result. summary: Supplementary note to arXiv:2611.08310 and arXiv:2610.19779. A fingerprint of coherent noise built from a stabilizer code is only as informative as the recovery gates that produce it, and every fixed choice of those gates is blind somewhere. This note isolates what can nevertheless be guaranteed, and states it as a worst-case floor rather than an average improvement. Two elementary facts about Fisher information make the guarantee exact. Because information matrices add, the identifiable set of a collection of designs is the union of theirs, so running several designs in parallel can never cost a direction that any member sees. Because the inverse of a sum is Loewner-dominated by the inverse of any summand, splitting a fixed shot budget over S designs can never cost more than sqrt(S) in standard deviation, that is, S in shots. The premium is therefore fixed in advance and independent of the working point, while the gain is not. Both statements are certified over the 64-design space of the three-qubit repetition code, under the 48- and 112-component fingerprints: the Loewner inequality is evaluated rather than assumed at every point tested, the worst case over 300 working points is 1.25 against the certified sqrt(2) = 1.4142, the bound is attained to five figures at one structured point, and at the worst points of the individual designs the parallel pair sits below the better single design by factors of 2.6 to 9.5. Two three-gate placements suffice; a third adds 3.5 to 11.5 per cent. The floor buys recoverability and worst-case precision, and it buys nothing else: it does not buy accuracy under common-mode calibration bias, and it does not repair a model degeneracy that no design can see. Contents: the two propositions with proofs, the cost corollary, the numerical certification (five tables, one figure), the relation to the two companion papers, and a reproduction map. The archive repro_v1.0.zip in this record contains the seven scripts, four data files, the figure and a self-test that re-derives every quoted number; run python scripts/selftest.py from the archive root and compare against MANIFEST.sha256. Companion papers: arXiv:2611.08310 (recovery gates as a resource) and arXiv:2610.19779 (coherent-noise identifiability).

summary: Contemporary speculative fiction unsettles anthropocentric assumptions about language, intelligence and the production of knowledge. This article compares Laline Paull’s The Bees (2014) to Ray Nayler's The Mountain in the Sea (2022) and The Tusks of Extinction (2024), exploring how the novels represent the conditions under which non-human knowledge is produced, recognized and transmitted. Drawing on biosemiotics and critical posthumanism in conversation with Andrew Lopez's account of epistemic injustice towards non-human animals, it develops a comparative framework based on recognition, access and continuity. The key argument is that the novels depict epistemic harm not merely as a failure to interpret non-human signs but as the institutional restriction of the very environments and social relations through which practical knowledge can flow. In Paull's hive caste is the source of authority which controls access to sensory information; in Nayler's oceanic enclave corporate power turns scientific attention into a potential tool of appropriation; and in the de-extinction narrative, biological restoration is simply not enough without the recovery of the skills that are socially transmitted. The novels are not being read as descriptions of actual animal species. Rather they are being used as a lens through which to examine the political and ethical dimensions of human authority over other ways of knowing. The article makes a contribution to contemporary literary studies by linking multispecies representation to the distribution and preservation of epistemic goods.

summary: Enterprise database systems face data-loss risks that come from operational errors, system failures and security incidents. MySQL binary logs give tools for data replication and point-in-time recovery, yet many organizations do not use them fully for recovery. This study proposes an automated, schema-aware MySQL binary-log recovery framework that integrates log discovery, dependency-aware recovery planning, database reconstruction, and validation into a unified enterprise restoration pipeline. The framework explains how to read binary-log formats, how to run recovery steps automatically and how to use performance-boosting tactics learned from well-known recovery models such as ARIES write-ahead logging, log-structured storage and event sourcing. In those tests, the recovery time dropped by about 65%, meaning the framework needed only about one-third of the baseline time. summary: Publishing a model or method does not finish the work of applied mathematics. Turning a mathematical idea into a reliable operational tool requires translation: assessment of how well a method behaves in theory and under real domain constraints, adaptation of both the mathematical formulation and the software to modern computing architectures, and adoption into sustained community use. Because every simplified model leaves a gap between idealized assumptions and reality, it carries applicability debt that an overlapping web of skills—uniting applied mathematicians, statisticians, domain specialists, and research software engineers—must manage. Generative AI and multi-agent harnesses have upset that balance. Large language models and coding agents make it cheap to generate candidate derivations, simulation code, and machine-checked proofs while leaving problem formulation and concrete domain verification tied to scarce human judgement. When automated generation outpaces translation, applicability debt goes unmanaged and pushes adoption toward unverified shortcuts, risking a crisis of application. At the same time, Australian science and innovation policy largely equates translation with commercial intellectual property and private data centres while overlooking research software and verification capacity inside public agencies, national facilities, and universities. Picking up in 2006—the fiftieth anniversary of the Australian Mathematical Society (Counting Australia In) and the birth year of the National Collaborative Research Infrastructure Strategy (NCRIS) and the ACCESS Earth-system partnership—this monograph contrasts that post-war public compact at the Society's seventieth anniversary in 2026 against Ambitious Australia and Science 2035, where research software disappears from policy view and the 2016–2025 mathematical-sciences decadal plan has expired without a successor. Written for both public policymakers and working quantitative practitioners, this book examines how translation succeeds or short-circuits across two centuries of computational history, a twenty-year citation census of 112 works applying the EQ algorithm for equal-area sphere partitions, Research Software Engineer workforce audits, Earth-system and biomedical case studies, and invariants-first software verification (PyEQSP and GluCat). Benchmarking Australia against Canada, Europe, the United Kingdom, the United States, and New Zealand across 18 chapters, 3 empirical appendices, and 750 verified primary sources (188 pages), it outlines practical, trade-off-aware opportunities across university assessment, service teaching, research software careers, scientific societies, sovereign infrastructure, and public-interest model verification ahead of the 2026–2028 national research and infrastructure renewals.
title: What does it take to apply mathematics in Australia today?

summary: Emissions figures in ship weather routing rest on regulatory and market data that change with new legal acts and markets. Maintaining them by hand is slow and prone to plausible errors. This paper presents the Data Steward, an agent built on a large language model that maintains these data in EcoRouter, a workbench for ship weather routing. The agent changes a value that calculations use only through an approved proposal. Deterministic tools take over the tasks that the model performs unreliably, such as reading area boundaries from legal texts, and checks run as workflows of small steps with an outcome for every item. The contribution to artificial intelligence is the design of an agent that maintains regulatory reference data under human control, together with a method for evaluating such an agent. The engineering application is the maintenance of the regulatory data on which a ship-routing tool computes emissions and regulatory costs. In a controlled test with 40 errors injected into the data that a full check covers, the Steward corrected 36 to 38 in three runs, against 20 to 28 for the same model alone with web search. In three full checks of the live data, 96 to 99 % of judged items were correct. A person who took no part in building EcoRouter found 57 of the 59 approved values correct. The results show that a commercial language model can maintain regulatory reference data with few errors once the tasks it performs unreliably are moved into deterministic code. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. Version 1. The records of the tests are published as a dataset: 10.5281/zenodo.24251511. In one sentence: the greedy row-selection rule built into every linear-algebra library, column-pivoted QR, can lose against the best possible choice by a factor of about exp(C√k), with an exact constant C, and never by the 2 k allowed by the textbook guarantee. Context. Many simulation and data methods keep only k of N coordinates of an N×k matrix Q with orthonormal columns (for example the interpolation points of the discrete empirical interpolation method, DEIM). The quality of a choice I is γ = ‖Q(I,:) −1 ‖ 2 , the factor by which interpolation from the chosen coordinates can be worse than the best approximation; some choice always has γ ≤ √(k(N−k+1)). The rule used in practice is column-pivoted QR (QRCP) on Q * , which repeatedly picks the coordinate least explained by those already chosen. Drmač and Gugercin (SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 2016) proved a bound that grows like 2 k . Damle and Kressner asked whether QRCP meets the existence scale on orthonormal rows (Problem 4.3 of Amsel et al., arXiv:2602.05394). Chen, Liu, He and Dong (arXiv:2606.02484) gave the first answer, negative: their examples exceed every polynomial multiple of the existence scale, and their construction already gives growth of order exp(c√k) with a small c. summary: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. summary: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.
title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon

summary: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. Orc6, the only non-AAA+ family protein within the origin recognition complex (ORC), has diverged significantly in function, sequence, and structure across eukaryotes, all while remaining necessary for proper genome maintenance and DNA replication in most species. This preprint investigates several differences between human and fruit fly ( Drosophila melanogaster ) Orc6 (HsOrc6 and DmOrc6, respectively), namely the behavior of the conserved C-terminal α-helix that tethers Orc6 to ORC. Here, the authors postulate that the mechanism of Orc6 association varies substantially between the species: in D. melanogaster , the C-terminal α-helix of DmOrc6 forms a high affinity interaction with DmORC reliant on a sulfur-aromatic interaction between M232 and the highly conserved W228. Meanwhile, HsOrc6 has lower affinity for HsORC, but the authors believe this is compensated for by utilizing a strong nuclear localization sequence (NLS) to increase the local concentration of HsOrc6 in the nucleus to allow for binding. The authors utilize several orthogonal methods to evaluate the effects of specific Orc6 mutations and human-fly Orc6 chimeras on ORC-Orc6 association, genome maintenance, and viability. While the general claim the authors make about the differences in nuclear localization and conserved regions of the Orc6 C-terminal α-helix are sensible and backed up by the presented data, there are several points of feedback provided regarding the in vivo experiments and mutant Drosophila lines. These aim to strengthen the scientific rigor of the manuscript and raise alternative explanations for conflicting results in the mutant Orc6 experiments. With these considerations, the manuscript could provide insight into the evolution and differing behavior of Orc6 amongst metazoans. Major comments: 1. MTT assay has appreciably different cell proliferation values between experiments for the same groups (WT, CTR, NA) and appears to use technical triplicates rather than biological replicates (p. 6, 11, Fig. 6B), making it difficult to compare mutants. The authors could carry out additional biological replicates and run all MTT assay trials in the same experiment to account for this and could confirm the authors' statement that the I239M substitution in HsOrc6 is not detrimental. If these replicates cannot be carried out, the authors could comment on their decision to use technical triplicates. 2. No controls were mentioned for rescue protein expression (p. 9-10 "Methods", Fig. 4), and the number of transgenic lines used per mutant was not stated. The cassette randomly integrates into the genome, meaning expression/integration of the Orc6 mutant genes may vary between lines. The authors could state the number of transgenic lines per mutant used and confirm there are multiple transgenic lines for each, then quantify both expression rates and protein concentration using RT-qPCR and total GFP fluorescence, respectively, to allow for better one-to-one comparisons between mutants. 3. Numeric per-genotype rescue counts of Orc6 mutants and ratios are not provided (p. 4-6, 10, Fig. 2-3). Instead, the authors state that rescue efficiency ranged from 10-30% and do not state whether this range is an arbitrary cutoff for being rescued or rather was the range of rescue efficiencies seen throughout all mutants. Providing raw rescue counts and expected number of rescues for each mutant along with a chi-squared test would offer a more robust viability comparison between mutants. 4. summary: Toda táctica del manejo integrado de plagas y enfermedades (MIP) cuesta algo cada semana —mano de obra, producto, recorrido del lote— menos una: la que se decidió antes de sembrar. Este artículo examina la resistencia varietal como fundamento del sistema, con las magnitudes medidas en campo y sus condiciones impresas. En Yunnan, China, entre 1998 y 1999, las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes —material convencional, sin modificación transgénica— presentaron una severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor que en monocultivo, a escala de miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios, y los agricultores abandonaron el fungicida contra esa enfermedad (Zhu et al., 2000). Ese caso sostiene el titular: es resistencia disponible, sembrable y medida a escala de paisaje. El contraste opuesto lo aporta el banano frente a la marchitez por *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* raza tropical 4 (Foc TR4): en el ensayo australiano de cinco ciclos, la incidencia acumulada fue de 84 % en el testigo 'Williams' y de 66 % en 'Grand Nain', frente a 2 % en la línea QCAV-4 portadora del gen *MamRGA2* (Harding et al., 2025). Su estatuto es el contrario: QCAV-4 es un banano transgénico aprobado solo en Australia y no es sembrable hoy en Colombia; se cita como evidencia de cuánto puede valer una resistencia cuando existe, no como material disponible para el productor colombiano. Entre ambos extremos, el artículo recorre la durabilidad —que se mide en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva y depende del fondo del paisaje, no de la ficha del cultivar—, el material limpio como decisión separada de la genética, y el injerto como forma de trasplantar la resistencia en tomate. La resistencia es la primera línea porque es la única decisión irreversible dentro del ciclo, y por eso mismo es la que más verificación exige antes de comprar. **Palabras clave:** resistencia varietal; mezclas de cultivares; añublo del arroz; *Magnaporthe oryzae*; Foc TR4; QCAV-4; durabilidad de la resistencia; material limpio; manejo integrado de plagas ## 1. Introducción: la decisión que se toma antes de que exista el problema Hay una decisión de manejo integrado que se toma antes de que el cultivo exista: la elección del material que se siembra. Cuando el productor compra semilla, encarga estacas, aparta tubérculos de su propia cosecha o contrata plántulas de vivero, ya decidió —aunque no lo sepa— qué fracción de la presión de plagas y enfermedades enfrentará el lote durante todo el ciclo. Ninguna aplicación posterior devuelve lo que se perdió por sembrar susceptible en un suelo con historia del patógeno. Esa anterioridad le da una propiedad que ninguna otra táctica tiene en el mismo grado: trabaja gratis toda la temporada, sin recorrido ni aplicación, desde la emergencia hasta la cosecha. Y comparte una segunda propiedad, menos amable: es irreversible dentro del ciclo. Si el monitoreo falla, se corrige la semana siguiente; si el material sembrado era el equivocado, el error dura lo que dura el cultivo —en perennes, años—. La tesis es medible, no retórica: donde se ha comparado material resistente contra susceptible, la diferencia típica es de decenas de puntos porcentuales de incidencia, y a veces equivale a eliminar una línea entera de gasto —el fungicida que deja de aplicarse—. Pero sería deshonesto quedarse en la celebración: el material vegetal es también el terreno de las promesas más frágiles de la sanidad tropical —tolerancias que se quiebran al tercer ciclo, resistencias que el patógeno rodea con razas nuevas, materiales «resistentes» que llegan infectados con otra enfermedad y resistencias enormes que existen únicamente como transgénico aprobado en otro continente—. ## 1. Introducción: la decisión que se toma antes de que exista el problema

Hay una decisión de manejo integrado que se toma antes de que el cultivo exista: la elección del material que se siembra. Cuando el productor compra semilla
aparta tubérculos de su propia cosecha o contrata plántulas de vivero

ya decidió —aunque no lo sepa— qué fracción de la presión de plagas y enfermedades enfrentará el lote durante todo el ciclo. Ninguna aplicación posterior devuelve lo que se perdió por sembrar susceptible en un suelo con historia del patógeno.

Esa anterioridad le da una propiedad que ninguna otra táctica tiene en el mismo grado: trabaja gratis toda la temporada
desde la emergencia hasta la cosecha. Y comparte una segunda propiedad
menos amable: es irreversible dentro del ciclo. Si el monitoreo falla
si el material sembrado era el equivocado

## 2. Tres decisiones distintas bajo una misma palabra

En el lenguaje de finca
«buen material» mezcla tres cosas que la evidencia separa

porque cada una falla y se verifica de una manera distinta.

La primera decisión es **genética**: sembrar un genotipo que resiste o tolera al organismo dañino. Resistencia y tolerancia no son sinónimos: la resistencia reduce la infección o el desarrollo del patógeno —o la alimentación y reproducción de la plaga—
la tolerancia permite que el organismo esté presente pero limita el daño en el rendimiento. Un material tolerante puede verse enfermo y rendir bien
y uno con resistencia parcial puede verse limpio en un año de baja presión y colapsar en uno de alta. Importa también distinguir la resistencia de uno o pocos genes de efecto mayor —potente
pero expuesta a que una sola mutación del patógeno la vuelva inútil— de la cuantitativa
repartida en muchos genes de efecto menor
menos espectacular y más duradera. Antes de aceptar la palabra «resistente» hay que preguntar resistente a qué

durante cuántos ciclos y contra qué población del patógeno.

La segunda decisión es **sanitaria**: sembrar material limpio
libre —o tan libre como el sistema permite— de los patógenos que viajan dentro de la semilla
el tubérculo o la plántula. En cultivos de propagación vegetativa —yuca
batata— pesa tanto como la genética
porque el material de siembra es el vehículo principal de virus
bacterias y hongos sistémicos: un genotipo excelente con estacas infectadas es un programa condenado desde el primer día

como demuestra la sección 7.

La tercera decisión es **de arquitectura**: injertar la variedad productiva sobre un portainjerto que aporta la resistencia que la variedad no tiene
típicamente contra patógenos del suelo. El injerto no crea resistencia nueva
y su costo es operativo: vivero capaz

mano de obra entrenada y un portainjerto probado bajo condiciones locales. Las tres decisiones se compran y se verifican por separado.

## 3. Yunnan: la mezcla que llevó el titular

El ensayo de Yunnan sigue siendo la demostración más grande de que la composición genética del lote es una variable de manejo. Las variedades de arroz susceptibles al añublo (*Magnaporthe oryzae*

sin. *Pyricularia oryzae*) sembradas en mezcla con variedades resistentes presentaron una **severidad 94 % menor y un rendimiento 89 % mayor** que en monocultivo. El efecto no se quedó en parcelas: se mantuvo al escalar a miles de hectáreas en 5 a 10 municipios de Yunnan
y su consecuencia práctica fue que los agricultores abandonaron la aplicación de fungicida contra el añublo (Zhu et al.
2000). La fuente es primaria y leída con sus condiciones: es la magnitud mejor sostenida de este artículo

y por eso lleva el titular.

Tres precisiones gobiernan su lectura. La primera es la naturaleza del material: variedades convencionales
obtenidas por mejoramiento clásico y combinadas por diseño de siembra

nada en Yunnan exige aprobación transgénica ni espera regulatoria —la táctica estaba disponible en la misma temporada en que se midió—. La segunda es el mecanismo: la resistencia funcionó mejor repartida en mezcla que concentrada
porque la mezcla reduce a la vez la densidad de tejido susceptible y la velocidad de propagación entre plantas
la unidad de la táctica no fue el gen aislado sino la composición del lote. La tercera es económica: el ahorro no fue un porcentaje de una aplicación
y su comparación correcta es contra la suma de todas las temporadas en que la mezcla siga funcionando —lo que depende de la durabilidad

el tema de la sección 6—.

El caso enseña además qué significa que una resistencia sea «disponible»: que el material existe
que su uso es legal donde se siembra
que el productor puede obtenerlo y que su efecto fue medido en condiciones comparables. Yunnan cumple las cuatro
el banano cumple la última con la mayor magnitud de este artículo

para Colombia— las tres primeras.

## 4. La resistencia a escala de país: el contraste de la roya del café

Entre la parcela y el paisaje hay un punto intermedio: el país. En Colombia
la roya del café (*Hemileia vastatrix*) separa con nitidez los dos mundos de este artículo: **incidencia de 20 % o más en variedades susceptibles frente a 6 % o menos en resistentes**
con pérdidas de 30 a 80 % en las susceptibles cuando el manejo no compensa la susceptibilidad

y más de 84 % del área cafetera nacional sembrada ya con variedades resistentes. La clase de evidencia se imprime con la cifra: es una fuente institucional —la Federación Nacional de Cafeteros de Colombia y Cenicafé—
cuya fuerza es la escala de observación
se lee como balance nacional sostenido
no como comparación experimental entre parcelas

y se cita como magnitud de contexto dentro del tema de la resistencia.

El dato cumple dos funciones: confirma el orden de magnitud —decenas de puntos de incidencia y pérdidas de un tercio a cuatro quintos de la cosecha en el material equivocado— y advierte: la misma fuente reporta seis razas nuevas de roya y nueve variantes más virulentas recientes. La resistencia cafetera colombiana es un éxito en vigilancia permanente

no un problema archivado.

## 5. TR4 del banano: la magnitud mayor y la vía que hoy no está disponible

Frente a la marchitez por *Fusarium oxysporum* f. sp. *cubense* raza tropical 4 (Foc TR4)
el ensayo de campo más largo publicado —cinco ciclos
de planta madre a cuarto rebrote

en el Territorio del Norte de Australia— comparó testigos Cavendish susceptibles con líneas portadoras del gen *MamRGA2*. La incidencia acumulada fue de **66 % en el testigo 'Grand Nain' y de 84 % en 'Williams'
frente a un rango de 2 % —la línea QCAV-4— a 36 % en las líneas con el gen** (Harding et al.
2025). La fuente es primaria y abierta
con testigo susceptible en el mismo campo y los mismos ciclos: con testigos en 66 % y 84 %
el 2 % de QCAV-4 es interpretable como lo que es

la separación entre un lote condenado y un lote viable.

Y aquí el marco obligatorio
impreso sin rebaja: **QCAV-4 es un banano genéticamente modificado
aprobado para producción comercial y consumo solo en Australia. No es sembrable hoy en Colombia.** Para el productor colombiano de banano o de plátano

esta resistencia no existe como opción de siembra: no hay material que comprar ni registro que lo ampare. Por eso la arquitectura de este artículo es deliberada: la mitad del titular —la táctica que el lector sí puede ejecutar— la lleva el arroz de Yunnan
con variedad convencional y mezcla de cultivares
la mitad del TR4 se enmarca como lo contrario

la demostración de cuánto vale la vía transgénica y la constatación de que esa vía hoy no está disponible para el productor colombiano. Citar el 2 % como evidencia de la magnitud del efecto «resistencia» es legítimo

presentarlo como recomendación de siembra sería vender como presente lo que para casi todo el trópico es todavía futuro.

## 6. La durabilidad: hectáreas-año

no ficha de cultivar

Si el artículo terminara en la tabla anterior

el lector saldría con una regla simple y falsa: «siembre resistente y el problema queda resuelto». La evidencia obliga a examinar cómo y por qué la resistencia deja de funcionar.

La unidad honesta de la durabilidad no es el año calendario ni la frase «resistencia durable» de un catálogo: es la **hectárea-año de protección efectiva** —cada hectárea sembrada con el material
multiplicada por cada año en que la protección se mantiene bajo presión real—. Leída así
la durabilidad **no es una propiedad de la ficha del cultivar: depende del fondo del paisaje** —de cuánta superficie comparte el mismo genotipo
de cómo se mueve el inóculo entre fincas y regiones—. La mezcla de Yunnan es

una tecnología de durabilidad además de una de control: repartir la resistencia baja la severidad de la temporada y reduce la recompensa que el patógeno obtiene por adaptarse a cualquiera de los genotipos.

El primer mecanismo de quiebre es la **evolución del patógeno**: un genotipo resistente en grandes extensiones ejerce la selección más intensa posible

y sobreviven las variantes capaces de atacarlo. Las seis razas nuevas y las nueve variantes más virulentas de roya reportadas en Colombia son la respuesta esperable del hongo a décadas de resistencia desplegada. La consecuencia de manejo: toda resistencia se siembra junto con su plan de quiebre —diversidad de genotipos

vigilancia de la incidencia en el material «resistente» como alarma temprana y ruta de reemplazo pensada antes de necesitarla—.

El segundo mecanismo no requiere evolución alguna: **la tolerancia anunciada que nunca fue lo que el ensayo corto sugería**. El caso de advertencia permanente es la variante somaclonal GCTCV-218

desplegada en Filipinas como Cavendish tolerante a Foc TR4. Su estatuto de evidencia debe quedar impreso: las cifras favorables que circulan provienen de páginas comerciales y de literatura secundaria
sin fuente primaria abierta que las respalde en la búsqueda verificada del libro fuente
y por tanto no se imprimen aquí como magnitud. Lo que sí está verificado es lo contrario de la promesa: en el ensayo extendido de tres años discutido por Harding et al. (2025)
2025). Había mostrado resistencia moderada en planta madre y primer rebrote

la protección se desvaneció.

La regla de interpretación vale para todo el artículo: **una tolerancia medida en uno o dos ciclos es una compra de tiempo
y debe planearse como tal —monitoreo ciclo a ciclo
el lote tolerante como activo que se deprecia
y sin desmontar las demás capas del programa—. Quien siembra un tolerante sabiendo que compra tiempo decide legítimamente

quien lo siembra creyendo que compró inmunidad ha sido engañado por la propaganda.

El tercer límite no es quiebre sino **ausencia**: frente al rayado pardo de la yuca (CBSD)
la fuente primaria más reciente declara que no existe ninguna variedad con resistencia duradera (Casinga et al.
2025). Donde la genética no ofrece la herramienta
el programa se construye con las demás —material limpio
manejo del vector y roguing—: el hueco declarado orienta el esfuerzo

la resistencia imaginaria lo desperdicia.

## 7. Material limpio: la decisión que la resistencia no reemplaza

En los cultivos de propagación vegetativa
la pregunta «¿de dónde salió este material?» vale tanto como «¿qué genotipo es?»: los virus
las bacterias sistémicas y algunos hongos viajan dentro de la estaca

y el material de siembra es a la vez primera víctima y primer vehículo. La degeneración de la semilla vegetativa —la acumulación de infecciones cuando el productor resiembra su propio material— es el proceso que la estrategia integrada de salud de semilla busca interrumpir con tres componentes que no se sustituyen entre sí: resistencia varietal
manejo en finca y reemplazo estratégico de los lotes (Thomas-Sharma et al.
derrotada por la estaca.** El ensayo de Kabare
en Kivu del Sur (República Democrática del Congo)
sembró dos variedades resistentes al mosaico —'Nabana' (MM 96/4653) y 'Sawasawa' (MM 96/3920)— con estacas sanas y con estacas infectadas por los virus del rayado pardo. Con estacas infectadas
el rendimiento de raíz fresca cayó **44 % a los 9 meses y 86 % a los 12 meses en 'Nabana'
frente a las mismas variedades con estacas sanas
mientras el material sano rindió 5 % más a los 12 meses que a los 9
2025). La resistencia al mosaico era real en ambas parcelas
porque el problema venía dentro de la estaca y era otra enfermedad —una frente a la cual
no existe resistencia duradera: en ese patosistema el material limpio es

casi toda la estrategia disponible—.

**Papa: la selección positiva como tecnología sin laboratorio.** Donde no hay semilla certificada al alcance
la herramienta verificada es marcar en el ciclo anterior las plantas sanas y vigorosas y cosechar de ellas —y solo de ellas— la semilla siguiente. En Uganda
a lo largo de tres generaciones
la selección positiva redujo la incidencia de virus (PVY
PLRV y otros) generación tras generación frente a la selección habitual y la aleatoria
porque al PLRV la literatura le atribuye reducciones de rendimiento de hasta 90 % (*Potato Research*
el análisis por ELISA dio la fotografía complementaria: en los lotes de selección positiva no se detectaron PVY
mientras en los de selección aleatoria se detectaron PVS en 78 %
PLRV en 16 % y PVM en 9 % de los tubérculos (Okeyo et al.
2018). La selección positiva no esteriliza un lote infectado

es frenar la degeneración y ganar ciclos de semilla aceptable.

El criterio práctico es uno solo: **«limpio» y «resistente» se compran por separado y se verifican por separado** —con certificación formal donde existe

renovación periódica y la disciplina de no sembrar jamás material de un lote con síntomas sistémicos visibles—.

## 8. Injertos y portainjertos: trasplantar la resistencia

Hay cultivos en los que la variedad que el mercado quiere no es la que el suelo permite. El injerto separa los dos trabajos: la copa produce lo que se vende y el portainjerto enfrenta lo que el suelo trae. La evidencia tropical más sólida está en tomate contra la marchitez bacteriana (*Ralstonia solanacearum*)

replicada en tres países con el mismo patrón.

En Benín (Abomey-Calavi y Sékou)

el informe técnico del World Vegetable Center comparó la variedad 'Tounvi' autoinjertada —el testigo sin portainjerto resistente— contra la misma variedad sobre dos portainjertos. La incidencia del testigo fue de **65
el rendimiento del injertado fue aproximadamente tres veces el del testigo (Zohoungbogbo et al.
los portainjertos 'EG203' —de berenjena— y 'Hawaii 7796' redujeron la marchitez en **49
0 %** en promedio y mejoraron el rendimiento en **57
injerto con riego reducido llevó la reducción a **76 %** en promedio
6 veces el del testigo (Msabila et al.
el injerto sobre berenjena suprimió la incidencia en más de 20 % y aumentó el rendimiento de dos cultivares en 30 % (*Sustainability*

con menor detalle en la fuente disponible.

Tres lecturas se imponen. La magnitud: pasar de 65–82 % de plantas marchitas a 0–10 % es la diferencia entre un cultivo inviable y uno comercial. La condición: el efecto depende del portainjerto y del sitio —la regla no es «injerte» sino «injerte sobre el portainjerto que haya demostrado resistencia bajo presión comparable a la de su suelo»—. Y el costo oculto: el injerto exige vivero con capacidad técnica y disciplina sanitaria. Queda una advertencia declarada: la rentabilidad comparada del injerto para el pequeño productor no está medida en la literatura abierta
el rendimiento tres veces mayor la sugiere

pero «sugiere» no es «mide».

## 9. Verificar antes de comprar: el interrogatorio del material

Entre la evidencia y la finca hay un mostrador: el del proveedor de semilla

el vivero o el vecino que vende estacas. La mayoría de las decisiones malas de material se toman aceptando en ese mostrador palabras sin precisiones. El interrogatorio que sigue las convierte en preguntas aplicables a cualquier oferta de material «resistente»
exactamente?** La respuesta aceptable nombra el organismo y

es un adjetivo publicitario. Segunda: **¿medido dónde y contra qué testigo?** Una incidencia de 5 % no significa nada sin el testigo susceptible en el mismo ensayo: el dato de TR4 es interpretable porque 'Grand Nain' y 'Williams' marcaron 66 % y 84 % en el mismo campo y los mismos ciclos (Harding et al.
2025). Tercera: **¿durante cuántos ciclos?** Es la pregunta que desarma el caso 'Formosana': en perennes
una resistencia sin al menos tres ciclos bajo presión real es una hipótesis. Cuarta: **¿qué pasa cuando se quiebre?** Genotipos alternos
lo inválido no es el material sino la dependencia exclusiva de él. Y quinta
para material de origen biotecnológico: **¿su uso está aprobado donde yo siembro?** —la pregunta que separa a QCAV-4

de cualquier cultivar convencional—.

Para el material limpio se verifica la procedencia
no el genotipo: ¿de qué lote madre salió —en selección positiva bien hecha
de plantas marcadas como sanas el ciclo anterior—?

¿el lote madre tenía síntomas? —un lote cosechado en un campo con síntomas sistémicos no se «mejora» eligiendo los órganos de mejor aspecto: el ensayo keniano encontró PVS en 78 % de los tubérculos de selección aleatoria (Okeyo et al.
la verificación es del proceso: portainjerto con nombre y respaldo local —'Hawaii7996' y 'Padma F1' en Benín
2024)— y un vivero capaz de mostrar su disciplina sanitaria: sin desinfección

el vivero se convierte en distribuidor del patógeno que el injerto pretendía evitar.

## 10. Conclusiones: la regla de la primera línea

La primera decisión fitosanitaria del programa es el material
antes de sembrar: (1) el genotipo —resistente o tolerante al problema dominante del lote
(2) el estado sanitario —limpio por certificación o por selección positiva verificada—
y (3) la arquitectura —injerto sobre portainjerto demostrado donde un patógeno del suelo limita el cultivo y existe vivero capaz—. Si alguna falla
el programa se rediseña alrededor de ese límite antes de sembrar

no después.

Las magnitudes quedan con sus condiciones y su estatuto. Yunnan —94 % menos severidad
miles de hectáreas en 1998–1999— es evidencia primaria de una táctica convencional y ejecutable. La roya del café —20 % o más frente a 6 % o menos

con fuente institucional— confirma el orden de magnitud y la obligación de vigilar. El TR4 —84 % en 'Williams' y 66 % en 'Grand Nain' frente a 2 % en QCAV-4— mide el techo de una resistencia y delimita la vía transgénica hoy no disponible en Colombia: QCAV-4 está aprobado solo en Australia. Y la durabilidad no se lee en la ficha del cultivar sino en hectáreas-año de protección efectiva sobre el fondo del paisaje.

Tres huecos delimitan la regla: no existe variedad de yuca con resistencia duradera al rayado pardo
las cifras favorables de los somaclonales tipo 'Formosana' carecen de verificación en fuente primaria abierta —solo está verificado su colapso en ensayo largo—
y la rentabilidad del injerto para el pequeño productor no está medida en serie abierta. Los huecos no debilitan la regla: la delimitan
que es lo que distingue una regla de decisión de un eslogan. Sembrar resistente sigue siendo la única táctica que trabaja gratis toda la temporada —siempre que lo sembrado sea

limpio y sembrable donde se siembra—.

summary: Data and code from the second case of a larger study, within the project Disrupting Digital Monolingualism 2 (DDM2), on the state of language metadata in Spanish and Latin American research infrastructures. The study follows language metadata along the Spanish open access aggregation chain: repositories and journals → RECOLECTA, the national aggregator operated by FECYT with REBIUN (225 registered resources) → the Spanish node ( ES ) of LA Referencia (1,478,369 records). It asks where language metadata are declared, transformed and lost, and with what effects on Spain's co-official languages (Catalan/Valencian, Galician, Basque, Aranese) and on Asturian. The deposit includes the RECOLECTA list of resources and endpoints; an OAI-PMH harvest at origin (34,186 records from 111 resources, in oai_dc and oai_openaire ); counts of records with and without language for each of the 96 repositories in the Spanish node, with their language facets; a repository-level contrast between levels; resources absent from LA Referencia; the language facet of the RECOLECTA portal and the provenance of its labels; and tests of selection by resource type. The study is exploratory. Samples were designed for exploration rather than estimation, and the data describe a single snapshot of live systems taken on 11 November 2026. The cases documented illustrate what can happen to language metadata along an aggregation chain; they are not general or causal claims about the infrastructures, institutions or repositories involved. See README.md and codebook.md for sources, method, files and limitations. Data: CC BY 4.0. Code: MIT.
title: Language metadata in RECOLECTA and the Spanish node of LA Referencia: Snapshot, 11 November 2026

summary: Capital markets open and close windows capriciously, and an issuer who must act once, irreversibly, has a different problem from a trader who may act continuously. This paper formalises an instrument built to decide the first problem: an admission clock that states, at any date, whether the window for placing a new instrument is open, how far open, and what dose that grade permits. The instrument is a conjunction of three gates — internal readiness, market regime, and a veto list — and not a weighted index, a design choice we defend on the ground that averaging allows an open gate to compensate a closed one, which is precisely the error an irreversible act cannot absorb. The regime gate is driven by a latent-factor engine whose identification rests on a point we believe has been underweighted in practice: an index assembled exclusively from indicators endogenous to the crypto market measures a single factor that is itself a transformation of the price level, and therefore carries no information about the future willingness of capital to finance an unseasoned instrument. We show that the primary equity issuance market supplies an exogenous and leading measurement of that same latent variable, and that the relevant measurement is the count and receptivity of small deals rather than aggregate proceeds — a distinction the 2026 data make vivid, with record United States proceeds accompanied by a thirty-four per cent fall in the number of deals priced. The paper's technical core converts the tacit knowledge of a daily operator into testable propositions. We obtain three results worth isolating. First, under a margin buffer set proportionally to the prevailing volatility level, the probability that a carry position breaches its buffer is exactly invariant to the level of volatility and depends, to second order, only on the volatility of volatility; the dependence is strictly increasing when the buffer exceeds √2 standard deviations and reverses below it. This gives the lockability gate a defensible threshold variable and explains why a carry bid withdraws in unstable markets without any change in the mean level of risk. Second, the rotation cascade that carries capital from bitcoin outward to the market's tail is asymmetric in its lag structure, not merely in sign: in expansion it propagates head-to-tail with a positive and tier-increasing lag, which is what makes it exploitable and what gives an issuer warning; in contraction it propagates at lag zero with amplification greater than one, which gives no warning and dries the tail first. Third, the equity of a company holding a leveraged bitcoin treasury is not a levered claim on bitcoin but a levered claim on the regime factor, with elasticity β = λ (1 + ε _m) decomposing into a balance-sheet channel and a premium-elasticity channel, both of which reverse sign together; the accretion identity Δ q/q = ( Δ V/SN)(1 − 1/m) shows the issuance loop inverting exactly at a multiple of one, which the 2025–2026 compression of these multiples and the observable conversion of such companies from net buyers into net sellers appear to bear out. A fourth result was added in this version and is negative. The whole architecture presupposes that the admission window is exogenous — that assent must be obtained from a party the issuer does not control. Where the issuer can operate its own venue, the predicate degenerates into a preference, and three identities follow: in a constant-product pool the marginal price is the ratio of seeded reserves, so the opening price is declared rather than discovered; slippage depends on the fraction of the pool reserve transacted and not on circulating float, so depth decouples from the float arithmetic; and the liquidity position is concave in price, so the issuer who seeds his own pool writes a continuous strip of options on his own instrument — the precise arrangement the dose parameters
title: Timing the Window: A gated regime engine for issuance and rotation in crypto-asset markets — architecture, calibration from operator heuristics, and conditional derivations for cascade rotation and treasury-levered equity exposure

summary: The ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo community benchmark for discriminating physiological from non-physiological protein–protein interfaces (Schweke et al., Proteomics 2023) contains 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 PDB entries. We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The benchmark is described with Bioschemas/schema.org JSON-LD: every interface is annotated with its label, chains, structural features, sequence-cluster assignment, provenance and licence, and linked to the PDB structure files and to snapshots of the RCSB PDB metadata. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the source repository, and the errors found were corrected. A lightweight design removed the need for Git LFS and for duplicated metadata. The post-publication curation of the labels (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces, compared with 836 and 841 in the publication) is documented, and three entries superseded in the PDB are linked to their replacements. A reference machine-learning script with cluster-aware cross-validation is included. Data, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, with full attribution to the original work.
title: FAIRification of the ELIXIR 3D-Bioinfo Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark

summary: SparkEviTune v1.0.1 — SoftwareX Corrective Release SparkEviTune is an evidence-aware, human-controlled software framework for Apache Spark configuration guidance. It combines deterministic configuration rules, Spark event-log analysis, optional machine-learning components subject to data-readiness gates, constrained optimization, and optional explanations. Version 1.0.1 incorporates software corrections prepared during the SoftwareX major revision, including: Improved FastAPI workload input-row handling. Profile Guard validation and associated regression tests. ModelRegistry multiprocessing-related corrections and targeted tests. Updates to dashboard, detection, machine-learning, pipeline, and validation components. Software verification The corrective release passed 61 automated tests under Windows Python 3.12 and Python 3.14. Ruff checks passed in both environments, and dependency consistency checks passed under Python 3.12. These checks establish correctness only within the tested scope and do not demonstrate general multi-worker deployment correctness or unrestricted concurrency safety. Scientific evidence and limitations Historical Spark benchmark results remain associated with their original experimental implementations and execution environments. The historical publication corpus comprises 81 clean runs covering 16 distinct scenarios, below the 20-scenario threshold required for publication-model training. A separate retrospective audit of 90 Learning01 executions found agreement for 90/90 event-log-derived durations, successful completion of 342/342 Spark jobs, and no mismatches across 1,128 shared configuration-property comparisons. Independent duration prediction yielded MAE = 8.9637 s and R² = -0.0621. General predictive accuracy or universal performance improvement is therefore not claimed. Historical Table 3 reconstruction remains incomplete. The A-03 LZ4 provenance and A-04 acceptance-criterion traceability issues remain unresolved. AQE-01 and Lot C experiments are not claimed as validated. SparkEviTune does not automatically apply proposed configurations. Users must review and benchmark recommendations before deployment. This archive represents the corrective software version and does not constitute a new experimental benchmark dataset.

summary: The ELIXIR Single Cell Omics community benchmark experiment 1 (BE1; Arigoni et al., Scientific Data 2024) is a 10x Genomics single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset that provides a controlled heterogeneous environment: seven lung cancer cell lines characterised by seven different driver genes, together with a PBMC population, were multiplexed with CellPlex oligonucleotides and sequenced. The data comprise 29,128 cells from the cell lines and 478 PBMC (GEO series GSE243665). We describe the FAIRification of this benchmark, carried out by the University of Bologna ELIXIR node within the ELIXIR Tools Platform. The experiment is described with the Single Cell Schema (version 0.4), in a machine-readable file that validates against the schema and links the samples, libraries, sequencing and processing steps to the public identifiers of GEO, SRA, BioProject and figshare. A query tool retrieves expression profiles from the public count matrices. The first version of the package was audited against the publication and the public records, and the errors found, among them a wrong article DOI, wrong cell counts, an incorrect creator record and unsupported statements, were corrected. Metadata, scripts and a web portal are available on GitHub, with full attribution to the original work.

summary: DMDO DMDO (Distributed Multidisciplinary Design Optimization) solves coupled, multidisciplinary engineering design problems by decomposing them into subproblems, one per discipline, and coordinating them with nonhierarchical analytical target cascading (NHATC). Documentation, theory, tutorials and benchmarks:  ahmed-bayoumy.github.io/DMDO Version 2612.0 Why DMDO Design the whole system, let every discipline keep its own tools.  Aircraft, vehicles, turbines and energy systems are designed by teams that each own an analysis: aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, controls, cost. Optimizing them as one monolithic problem needs a multidisciplinary analysis that converges at every design point, one optimizer that suits every discipline, and every code in one process. DMDO needs none of that. No converged multidisciplinary analysis.  Each subproblem keeps its own copies of the variables it shares with the others, and an augmented Lagrangian coordinator drives the copies to agreement. Coupled analyses never have to be iterated to convergence inside the optimizer. Measured on the classic MDO benchmarks.  On the Sellar problem with derivative-free MADS subproblems, DMDO reaches  f = 3.2042, 0.65 % from the best known solution 3.18339  [3], with the disciplines consistent to  1.3 × 10⁻⁶ . In all six recorded benchmark runs (Sellar, Golinski's speed reducer, a geometric program and a basic two-discipline problem), the inconsistency between disciplines falls  below 10⁻³ within 6 to 16 outer iterations . The right optimizer for each discipline.  A subproblem built on a noisy or failing simulation uses derivative-free Mesh Adaptive Direct Search ( OMADS ); a smooth analytical one uses SciPy's SLSQP, in the same run. Any other optimizer plugs in as a small strategy class. Serial, parallel or distributed, with the same answer.  Solve the subproblems one after the other (Gauss–Seidel) or all at once (Jacobi), in-process, in a pool of worker processes, or on remote machines. Jacobi results do not depend on which worker finishes first: the test suite checks that in-process, out-of-order, process-pool and remote runs give bit-identical designs. An API, not just a script.  Build a problem from YAML, a dictionary or Python objects, then  run()  it, drive it one outer iteration at a time with  step() , or solve the subproblems yourself with  ask() / tell() . Observers stream progress, registries and entry points add solvers, executors and analyses, and an optional HTTP service exposes runs to any language. Results you can reproduce.  Runs are seeded; every benchmark run is checked against a recorded history that the code must reproduce bit for bit; interrupted runs resume from their checkpoint to exactly the same result; the test suite runs on Linux, Windows and macOS in continuous integration.   Maximum inconsistency between the copies held by different subproblems, at each outer iteration of the six recorded benchmark runs. Details in the  benchmarking documentation . summary: The PlanckPlay is a 3D-printed representation of the 16 three-dimensional tetrahedra that make up the Planck’s Hexadecachoron—a metamodel (model of models) of physics. Mathematically, a hexadecachoron is the four-dimensional polytope dual to the hypercube, or tesseract. Just as the tetrahedron and cube are three-dimensional Platonic solids, the hexadecachoron and tesseract are their four-dimensional analogues. The hexadecachoron is composed of 16 regular tetrahedra in four-dimensional space. When projected into three dimensions, these tetrahedra appear distorted—much like how the square faces of a cube are distorted in a two-dimensional drawing. PlanckPlay was developed within the Hypercube of Physics (HoP) project, part of the Cluster of Excellence Matters of Activity. In HoP, we explore models that classify physical theories in relation to the four fundamental physical constants: Newton's gravitational constant (G), the inverse speed of light (c -1 ), Planck’s constant (h), and the Boltzmann constant (k B ). In 1899, Max Planck used these constants to define natural units for length, time, mass, and temperature—foundational to modern physics. Within the HoP consortium, we envision PlanckPlay as both a research object and an educational tool, harnessing its gamified structure to make abstract physical concepts tangible and engaging.
title: PlanckPlay - Planck's Hexadecachoron Puzzle
