summary: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties from measurements. We develop a comprehensive suite of property identification tasks focused on hardware mechanisms relevant to Spectre-class attacks, covering speculative execution, branch prediction, memory dependence, and cache behavior. We evaluate ProcReverser on the XuanTie C910, the gem5 RISC-V O3 CPU model, and the SiFive P550. ProcReverser achieves Pass@1 and Pass@5 scores of 81.3% and 93.8%, respectively, on C910, and 83.0% and 100.0% on gem5 O3. On the SiFive P550, ProcReverser further characterizes microarchitectural properties covered by the proposed task suite. These findings highlight the potential of automated microarchitectural reverse engineering to support processor vulnerability analysis and defense evaluation.
title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis

summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models (LLMs) activate only a few experts per token while generally keeping all the experts in GPU memory for high efficiency. Expert pruning reduces this GPU memory footprint cost, yet discards the contribution of pruned experts. Existing remedies either rely on static substitutes, merge experts at the cost of altering their functions, or require costly recovery training. In this paper, we find that the functionalities of pruned experts can be efficiently reconstructed from the activated remaining experts. We propose GEAR (Gated Expert Activation Reuse), which reuses the scaled outputs of reliable activated experts without any training or additional expert computation. In addition, we propose GEAR$^2$ to further recover what reuse cannot express with an ultra-lightweight residual. On five MoE LLMs from 16B to 106B parameters with 25% and 50% of experts pruned, GEAR improves over its training-free counterparts in nearly every setting (up to 4 pp.) in terms of accuracy, and GEAR$^2$ outperforms baseline approaches (up to 2.75 pp.) in every setting on nine zero-shot benchmarks, with larger advantages (up to 2.72 pp. higher) under more aggressive pruning (up to 50%).
title: GEAR$^2$: Pruned Experts Live On through Gated Reuse of Activated Experts and a Missing-Mass Residual

summary: Speculative decoding reduces generation cost, but it stores two KV caches: one for the target model and one for the draft model. We reduce this extra memory by quantizing the draft cache. The target cache and verifier remain in BF16, so that compression cannot change the target model's final correction rule. We first study how to divide precision between keys and values. A naive per-token quantizer makes keys appear much more sensitive: splitting a 12-bit budget, K8V4 beats K4V8 in acceptance by 10.87pp. However, with grouped per-channel keys, the gap becomes -0.25pp. A controlled Qwen test confirms that changing only the key quantizer can erase or reverse the preferred bit split. Hence, following KIVI, we propose K4V4 quantization with per-channel keys and per-token values. Across six model pairs, our method reduces draft cache memory by 66.20%, and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%. Mean acceptance drops from 57.93% to 57.14%, only 1.36% relative. Overall, quantized draft caches can make speculative decoding more memory efficient; as a predictive principle for efficient AI design, key and value precision must be co-designed with the quantizer layout.
title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache

summary: Latent KV cache compression reduces memory footprint by mapping historical keys and values into compact representations. However, generic compressed key states require reconstruction to native dimension before applying RoPE and computing attention scores, adding sequence-scaling overhead to the decode path. We characterize when a latent KV representation can serve directly as the execution state of pretrained RoPE. For RoPE-based transformers, exact static linear execution of the rotary key path requires the latent-to-native map to preserve the pretrained RoPE action through an intertwining relation, restricting exact mixing to coordinates that share the same RoPE frequency. Guided by this characterization, we build GaugeRoPE, a training-free executable latent KV representation. It combines a RoPE-compatible carrier that preserves the rotary action with an approximate position-independent residual key--value (RKV) correction for complementary key and value information, both evaluated without per-token dense historical K/V reconstruction. On Mistral-7B, GaugeRoPE achieves $5.85\times$ KV compression while maintaining quality close to the full-cache baseline. Additional MHA results validate the construction beyond GQA. GaugeRoPE achieves up to $2.48\times$ the decode throughput of the vanilla uncompressed baseline through direct latent execution.
title: GaugeRoPE: RoPE-Compatible Executable Latent Attention

summary: Bug fixes Fixed caching of timing properties in Scan and Kymo with recent cachetools versions, where using cachedmethod beneath @property could raise TypeError: Decorating class methods is not supported . The fix preserves read-only access and invalidation when the instance cache is cleared. Fixed timestamp mismatches in PiezoTrackingCalibration , PiezoForceDistance and force-baseline fitting/correction with ForceBaseLine by cropping native force and trap-position channels to their shared time range before matching sample rates. Only complete averaging blocks are retained. Incompatible sampling grids now raise an informative error suggesting native channels instead of manually downsampled data. Fixed potential complex-to-real casting warnings in the kymotracker geometry tests by explicitly taking the real parts of reference eigenvalues and eigenvectors for real symmetric matrices. Also corrected assertion failure messages in the candidate-direction test. These are test-only changes. The geometry implementation and tracking results are unchanged. Ensured Scan.export_video() and ImageStack.export_video() use a Python integer for the default stop-frame index, improving compatibility when the frame count is a NumPy integer. This silences some warnings that pop up during testing. Fixed alignment of values in calibration tables for ForceCalibrationItem and CalibrationResults with tabulate 0.10 by explicitly preserving whitespace, while retaining compatibility with older supported versions.

summary: Recent megajoule laser inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments have demonstrated thermonuclear target gain above unity, yet scaling pulsed laboratory ignition to commercial 1–20 Hz Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) power plants remains obstructed by six coupled physics and engineering bottlenecks: hydrodynamic Rayleigh–Taylor (RT) and Richtmyer–Meshkov instabilities, core contamination from mechanical target support tents and fill tubes, parasitic cross-beam energy transfer (CBET) and stimulated Brillouin/Raman backscatter (SBS/SRS), critical-density reflection and solid gold cone vaporization in petawatt fast ignition, dielectric mirror blistering and positive plasma pulse dispersion, and the absence of non-destructive focal-plane phase diagnostics in high vacuum. This paper presents an integrated theoretical and reactor-engineering solution derived from the Lorentz Invariant / Localized Intrinsic Field Equilibrium (LIFE) framework, governed by the exact four-dimensional covariant divergence of the Maxwell stress-energy tensor (∂ μ T μν = 0). By arranging subsets of N beam ≥ 4 coherent laser beamlines into mutually orthogonal pairs with quadratic sinusoidal cross-beam phase modulation, directional wave operators annihilate longitudinal radiation-drag force densities (f x = f z ≡ 0) while enforcing strictly forward longitudinal Poynting transport (S x, S z ≥ 0), eliminating coherent backscatter and replacing chaotic CBET with deterministic transverse Poynting routing. Along the mutual orthogonal axis, optical-cycle averaging via the Jacobi–Anger Bessel expansion establishes a stationary three-dimensional ponderomotive restoring lattice with zero net volume momentum bias, enabling both stalk-free high-vacuum cryogenic pellet levitation and dynamic RT shear damping during implosion. For fast-ignition architectures, orthogonal precursor guide beams induce an effective curved optical metric (n eff = c/v g > 1) forming an exponentially self-confined slow-light channel I core (r) = I 0 exp(−k|r|) that guides petawatt ignitor pulses directly into the stagnated fuel core without solid gold cones. Combined with coating-free corrugated monolithic bulk tungsten negative-dispersion wall optics and sub-millisecond vacuum three-beam differential interferometric and dual-divergence (∇·E, ∇·H) electro-optic feedback, the LIFE architecture provides a non-invasive upgrade path for existing megajoule and petawatt laser facilities as well as next-generation commercial IFE power plants. summary: Kohn-Sham solver for isolated atoms using the finite-element discrete variable representation (FE-DVR). Pseudo-atoms with norm-conserving pseudopotentials in UPF format, including pseudopotentials without pseudo-atomic orbitals (e.g. SG15) All-electron atoms (non-relativistic), plus approximate scalar-relativistic (Koelling-Harmon) and ZORA treatments LDA and GGA functionals: PBE built in, all others via libxc Confined atomic orbitals with polarization functions for use as localized basis functions or projectors, exported on a logarithmic grid (Quantum ESPRESSO style), on the FE-DVR grid, or as spherical Bessel transforms; dipole matrix elements Photoemission : scattering phase shifts and dipole matrix elements to continuum states 🚀 Installation $ python3 -m pip install atomic_femdvr   The built-in exchange-correlation driver provides PBE. Other functionals (e.g. the LDA used for the NIST benchmark) need the libxc Python bindings, which are not on PyPI; see the installation guide . 💪 Getting started Calculations are defined by a JSON input file. summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24314752 . Reviewer Report: Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine Manuscript: "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems" (G. Yang; Preprints.org , doi:10.20944/preprints202603.0470.v1, posted 5 March 2026) Type of report: Point-by-point reviewer report, prepared to help the author strengthen the work before journal submission. The manuscript proposes a computational "multi-track cognition" (MTC) framework that lets data from different medical systems (traditional Chinese medicine, biomedicine, Tibetan medicine, with others said to be addable) be compared and fused without forcing one system's vocabulary onto another. The author's stated aim is to move beyond format-level standardisation towards semantic alignment, and beyond single-point linear correspondence towards system-level mapping. Importance of the research area. Integrative medicine is widely practised and increasingly supported by health policy, including the World Health Organization's strategic work on traditional and complementary medicine. A persistent barrier to generating integrated evidence is that systems describe the patient and the intervention in different conceptual languages. Examples are pattern differentiation, nature and flavour, and meridian tropism on one side, and disease categories, biomarkers and molecular targets on the other. A general and extensible way to connect these descriptions would be useful for evidence synthesis, chronic-disease management and individualised care. The author appropriately targets semantic, and not merely syntactic, interoperability, which is a question that merits careful methodological work. Approach proposed. The framework has three layers (Figure 1; Section 2): 1. Cognitive tracks (Section 2.1). Each medical system has its own track with a native feature set, normalisation rules and a native "systemic effect" index. 2. Homeostatic representation network, HRN (Section 2.2). A directed acyclic graph of 28 laboratory indicators across eight physiological systems serves as the shared anchor. Its topology comes from literature and three expert physicians. Its parameters are learned with a Bayesian network on MIMIC-III. 3. System-level mapping (Section 2.3). A random forest, guided by three rules (cluster correspondence, network emergence, context dependence), is trained with a mean-squared-error loss to predict post-intervention changes in the HRN indicators. Performance is judged by Semantic Alignment Accuracy (SAA, the share of cases in which two mapped vectors reach cosine similarity ≥ 0.85), R², MAE and RMSE (Section 2.4). Evidence reported (Section 3). Four public datasets are used (Table 1), with a 70/30 split and 5-fold cross-validation. In the TCM–Western dual-track setting the framework reports SAA 91.27% and R² 0.852, against 59.13–76.58% SAA for three baselines (Table 2). A three-system extension adding Tibetan medicine reports SAA 86.34% and R² 0.821 (Section 3.4). Agreement with three clinical experts is reported as κ = 0.86, and a Lung–Spleen Qi Deficiency case illustrates the workflow (Section 3.5). The author concludes that the framework is lossless, general, and ready to support clinical integration. Strengths. The following strengths provide a sound basis for revision: • The problem is timely and clinically meaningful. • The modular idea, with track-specific components and one shared core, is attractive and in principle testable. • An outcome-level physiological anchor is a practical way to compare interventions that act through different theories. • The model, loss, hyperparameters and pseudo-code are stated explicitly, which allows scrutiny. • The author attempts expert annotation, effect sizes and a multi-system extension. •

summary: Adding new parameters to the baseline distribution using the generated family concept has been one of the most commonly used techniques in recent years. The Median-based Unit Rayleigh (MBUR) is a one-parameter unit distribution. In this paper, the author added another parameter using the Topp_Loene generated family. The new approach not used previously in the literature is to use the Lomax distribution. The author truncated the Lomax distribution to obtain the unit-truncated Lomax distribution and used it as a generator to elaborate the unit-truncated Lomax-generated MBUR distribution. The derivations of the new generalized forms are discussed. The properties of both distributions, including the quantile function and raw moments, are discussed in detail.   The quantile functions can be expressed in a closed form, while the raw moments cannot be expressed in a closed form. Both distributions have bathtub-shaped, J-shaped, and increasing shape hazard rates. Real data analysis is performed to compare the fitness of both distributions.
title: Topp Leone Generated MBUR and Unit Truncated Lomax Generated MBUR Distributions: New Generalization of The MBUR Distribution

summary: Data and Stata code for a study of whether social capital predicts retained luxury imports. The outcome is imports less re-exports of four HS headings — 7113 jewellery, 9101 wristwatches with cases of precious metal, 4202 trunks, handbags and similar containers, and 3303 perfumes — scaled by population. Subtracting re-exports matters because entrepôt economies import these goods for onward shipment. The main regressor is the GSCI social capital dimension DIM_SC_30, a balanced annual series covering 247 countries. The full panel is 3,883 country-years across 184 countries, 2000–2023; the estimation sample with all controls is 3,241 country-years across 159 countries. A second, smaller panel uses the WVS/EVS Integrated Values Survey trust measure at wave level (86 country-waves, 36 OECD countries), with luxury imports averaged over a five-year window centred on each wave year. The package contains the UN Comtrade extract and the PowerShell script that produced it from the Comtrade public API, the World Bank control variables and their download script, the GSCI series, the Integrated Values Survey trust file, the Stata do-files and logs, and Figures 1–3. Code/Replication_Luxury_SocialCapital.do reproduces every table and figure in the paper. Nothing is interpolated: a country-year enters a panel only if it was observed. See README.md.
title: Social capital and retained luxury imports: replication data and Stata code for a global panel, 2000–2023

summary: We compared target-specific eight-point dose layouts for four withheld interior responses in 171 held-out Merck 4 × 4 drug-pair matrices, with (1,1) designated as the primary target. For the projection predictor, near-minus-far mean absolute error was −0.05772 at the primary target (95% pair-bootstrap interval −0.07163 to −0.04441) and −0.07085 for the four-target pair average (−0.07899 to −0.06262). Overall projection errors for near, far-plus-anchor and fixed random layouts were 0.0412, 0.1120 and 0.0773; on the same near inputs, the order-based predictors had lower average errors than the tested local interpolators, while projection showed no clear added benefit over the raw witness. A post-hoc Gaussian-process comparator showed no clear average difference from projection on the Merck near inputs, with optimizer-bound warnings in 293 of 684 fits.
title: Fixed-Budget Dose Layouts in Merck 4 × 4 Combination Matrices

summary: Two independent bulk RNA-sequencing datasets were generated using a zebrafish model of Dravet syndrome at 5 days post-fertilization (dpf). Dataset 1: Disease-associated transcriptional alterations Comparison of scn1lab−/− zebrafish with wild-type controls ( scn1lab+/+ ) to identify disease-associated changes in gene expression. scn1labvWT_metadata.txt scn1labvWT_unnormalised_counts.txt Dataset 2: Drug treatment and transcriptional response An independent dataset comprising scn1lab−/− zebrafish treated with sertraline, orphenadrine, brexpiprazole, fenfluramine, or DMSO. All treatment groups were compared against wild-type controls to investigate compound-induced transcriptional changes and their potential to reverse disease-associated gene expression signatures. scn1labvWT_treatment_metadata.txt scn1labvWT_treatment_unnormalised_counts.txt Data integration and batch correction Both datasets contain unnormalized gene-level RNA-sequencing counts and corresponding sample metadata. Although generated independently, the datasets can be analyzed jointly using appropriate batch correction or statistical models that account for dataset-specific effects. This enables integrated comparisons of disease-associated and treatment-induced transcriptional changes, provided that batch effects can be distinguished from the biological conditions of interest.
title: From molecular dysfunction to therapeutic discovery: Novel targets and drug repurposing candidates for Dravet syndrome

summary: This record contains the raw data generated in the computational experiments of the article "EpiBuilder 2.0: A Dockerized and User-Friendly Web Platform for in silico Analysis of Linear B-cell Epitopes" . Source code: https://github.com/labioinfoufsc/EpiBuilder . The data were used to (i) benchmark the processing time of the EpiBuilder 2.0 workflow on CPU and GPU on two different machines, (ii) compare the epitope predictor integrated into EpiBuilder 2.0 (BepiPred v3.0) with an alternative deep-learning predictor (EpiDope v0.3), in processing time and in per-residue concordance, and (iii) carry out the biological evaluation of the predicted linear B-cell epitopes (N-glycosylation filtering, subcellular localization, BLASTp matches against the IEDB and against other proteomes of the same genus). All runs were performed in triplicate . The archive contains only the generated outputs and the shell scripts used to produce them; the input proteomes are public UniProt reference proteomes and are not redistributed. Hardware configurations Machine A (Intel Core i9-14900K @ 6.0 GHz, 80 GB DDR5 6000 MHz): configuration A – CPU only ( machine_A/cpu/ ); A1 – NVIDIA RTX 3080, 10 GB ( machine_A/RTX_3080/ ); A2 – NVIDIA RTX A4500, 20 GB ( machine_A/RTX_A4500/ ). Machine B (Intel Xeon E7-4830 v2 @ 2.20 GHz, 295 GB DDR3 1600 MHz): configuration B – CPU only ( machine_B/cpu/ ). Input proteomes (UniProt, downloaded on 6 November 2026) Influenza B virus B/Lee/1940 – UP000008158 (11 proteins) Zaire ebolavirus – UP000007209 (9 proteins) Borrelia burgdorferi B31 – UP000001807 (1,273 valid proteins) Staphylococcus aureus – UP000008816 (2,888 valid proteins) Candida albicans – UP000000559 (5,977 valid proteins) Software and parameters BepiPred v3.0 (Docker image bioinfoufsc/bepipred3 ), CPU and GPU. EpiDope v0.3 ( flomock/epidope:v0.3 ), CPU only. EpiBuilder 2.0 core workflow in Nextflow ( bioinfoufsc/epibuilder-core ): epitope extraction, physicochemical properties, N-glycosylation, PSORTb v3.0 / WoLF PSORT v0.1, BLASTp v2.17 against the IEDB (~155,279 B-cell epitopes) and reference proteomes of each genus. Parameters: epitope length 10–30 aa; BepiPred v3.0 threshold 0.1512; BLAST minimum identity 90% and minimum query coverage 90%; localization none (viruses), gram_neg ( B. burgdorferi ), gram_pos ( S. aureus ), fungi ( C. albicans ). Contents of EpiBuilder2_experiments.tar.gz scripts/ – experiment_bepipred.sh (BepiPred v3.0, CPU or GPU), experiment_epidope.sh (EpiDope v0.3), experiment.sh (one EpiBuilder 2.0 run) and experiment_triplicate.sh (loop over organisms and replicates). machine_A/ and machine_B/ – one folder per configuration and tool ( bepipred , epidope , epibuilder ), with one subfolder per organism ( INFLUENZA , EBOLA , BORRELIA , STAPHYLOCOCCUS , CANDIDA ) and replicate1 – replicate3 . bepipred/ – FASTA validation output, per-residue scores ( raw_output.csv ), execution logs and wall-clock times ( execution_times.tsv ). epidope/ – per-residue scores ( epidope_scores.csv ), predicted epitopes, per-protein tables and plots, and execution times. epibuilder/ – epitope-level results ( epitope-detail.tsv , epitopes.fasta ), per-protein summary, per-residue scores, subcellular localization, BLASTp hits against the IEDB and each reference proteome, consolidated spreadsheet ( epibuilder.xlsx ) and Nextflow trace, report, timeline and DAG ( reports/ ). Use in the publication CPU vs. GPU processing time of the workflow (configurations A, A1, A2 and B) and comparison between machines: bepipred/*/execution_times.tsv and epibuilder/*/replicateN/reports/trace.txt . BepiPred v3.0 vs. EpiDope v0.3 processing time on CPU: execution_times.tsv of both tools. Per-residue concordance between BepiPred v3.0 and EpiDope v0.3 (Cohen's kappa, Jaccard index, Spearman's rho): raw_output.csv and epidope_scores.csv . Biological evaluation, IEDB matches and cross-species
title: Benchmark data of EpiBuilder 2.0: CPU/GPU performance, BepiPred v3.0 vs. EpiDope v0.3 comparison, and epitope predictions for five pathogen proteomes

summary: Executive Summary & Abstract Book XV completes the monumental fifteen-volume architecture of the Canonical Monograph Series in Biophysical Political Economy. Building directly upon the ecological and holobiont baselines established in Book XIV, this treatise resolves the evolutionary and physical mechanics of cross-domain viral plasticity, the emergence of novel microbial life in the oceanic plastisphere, the role of human somatic cellular wetware as an evolutionary crucible, and the global topological coordination of the virosphere under the Queen Virus Hypothesis. To ensure broad accessibility and prevent typographical corruption across web repositories, this official archival record is presented entirely in clear, uncompressed descriptive prose without raw formula scripts: Division I: The Pinocchio Hypothesis & Cross-Domain Viral Plasticity (Chapters 1–3) The Non-Linear Threshold Bridge: Resolves the boundary between baseline ecological stability and crisis-driven phase transitions. While under ordinary conditions bacteriophages remain strictly prokaryotic, severe environmental clearance shocks threaten bacterial extinction, triggering the Pinocchio Jump across kingdom barriers into mammalian cells. The Somatic Sanctuary: Demonstrates that cross-domain viral entry is driven by refuge seeking rather than host destruction. The human body—regulated at a constant 37 degrees Celsius, shielded from solar ultraviolet radiation, and buffered in its chemical pH—acts as an evolutionary bunker of last resort where internalized viruses persist without lysing host tissues. The Early-Warning Telemetry Lattice: Establishes that the ten-nonillion viral ocean (10^31 particles), possessing zero thermal inertia and twenty-minute replication cycles, functions as the primary sensory nervous system of the biosphere. Measurable surges in virome sequence variance and cellular uptake precede macroscopic ecological and agricultural collapses by weeks to months. Division II: The Anthropogenic Plastisphere & The Reciprocal Crucible (Chapters 4–7) The Plastisphere Abyss: Explores the synthetic polymer continents accumulating across the five subtropical oceanic gyres. Unlike natural biodegradable substrates, non-biodegradable microplastics create permanent hydrophobic reefs that accelerate plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer by up to one thousand times, outpacing ancestral open-ocean phages. The Human Somatic Crucible: Documents that nearly half of the human nuclear genome is composed of ancient viral and retro-transposable elements. Within perinuclear compartments, host cytidine and adenosine deaminases (APOBEC3 and ADAR) edit and diversify internalized viral sequences at sub-lethal rates, acting as an evolutionary bio-laboratory. The Reciprocal Inversion: Closes the bi-directional loop. Human cellular editing synergizes with phage Diversity-Generating Retroelements (DGRs) capable of generating over seventy trillion tail-fiber variants. The resulting bespoke counter-phages are shed back into external watersheds to lyse runaway plastisphere bacterial blooms. The Entangled Antidote: Formulates the law of simultaneous co-emergence. Because a bacterial pathogen and its matching viral predator are forged in the exact same ecological and somatic crucible, nature never generates an antibacterial threat without co-localizing its specific lytic antidote within the immediate outbreak coordinate. Division III: Unified Virocell Topology & The Queen Virus Hypothesis (Chapters 8–10) The Non-Local Virosphere: Refutes the dogma of memoryless random drift. Grounded in Manfred Eigen's quasispecies mechanics and social virology, viral populations operate as coupled probability clouds endowed with four-dimensional historical memory, exhibiting parallel convergent evolution across geographically separated niches. summary: Identifying refugia, areas likely to be buffered from climate change, is an important wildlife conservation strategy. For forest-associated wildlife, better representation of climate conditions should improve refugia identification. We quantified refugia potential for boreal songbirds in Alberta, Canada, by comparing distribution models based on macroclimate (unadjusted) and locally downscaled climate predictions (microclimate). We surveyed songbirds with autonomous recording units (n = 2147 locations) from spring to mid-summer between 2014 and 2018 and recorded air temperature with iButton Thermochron dataloggers (n = 283) in river valleys and hills systems. Using microclimate offsets, we downscaled macroclimate based on topography and vegetation cover. We fit boosted regression tree (BRT) models for 48 forest songbird species using four model combinations: climate-only models with (i) downscaled vs. (ii) unadjusted climate, and climate + vegetation (full model) with downscaled (iii) vs. (iv) unadjusted climate. F or each species, we compared the four model combinations in terms of predictive performance, variable importance, and projected refugia potential, and summarized the results by nesting habitat group (coniferous, deciduous, and wetland). . For most species, vegetation variables (relative biomass of key tree species) had lower importance in bird models based on downscaled climate, suggesting a degree of substitutability. However, model explanatory power did not improve with downscaled climate variables for most species. Coniferous-associated species were the exception, suggesting greater sensitivity to local climate conditions. We then predicted refugia potential as the area of overlap between current and projected future distribution under a moderate climate scenario. Climate-only models predicted less habitat loss for coniferous species using downscaled climate (21% habitat loss vs. 58% loss with unadjusted variables), whereas full models with vegetation showed the reverse, with greater habitat loss under downscaled climate (39% downscaled vs. 23% with unadjusted climate variables). For deciduous-associated species, which were mostly projected to increase under climate change, habitat loss was smaller using downscaled climate regardless of model type. Overall, our results suggest that microclimate downscaling improves the identification of refugia for coniferous-associated species in this region.   Managers should consider targeting areas with high refugia potential to improve conservation outcomes.
title: Data from: Downscaling climate models with vegetation and topography identifies refugia for some, but not all, boreal songbirds

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Forty-eight entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature, among them: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7; a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients; a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset; a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten; a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998); a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation; a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight; a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. Light through a Jerlov water type. The package: computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963); converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors; gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m, and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers; integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth; gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two; and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent; ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum; carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models; converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient. Measurements it carries. Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type, against which the depth profile is checked; Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille; the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures; Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters; five published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016), Lee et al. (2015) and Morel et al. (2007), for the caller to choose from; the eight stations of the clearest ocean water measured, Morel et al. (2007); the measured reflectance of ten materials found in and around water, from the USGS Spectral Library Version 7, for reference images of how they look through each water type. Without a water type. It gives: Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001, and the earlier edition of Morel 1988), or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013); the attenuation of the visible and of the whole shortwave from the surface to a depth, and the depth where a given fraction of the visible light is left, the euphotic depth among them, from the absorption and backscattering coefficients at 490 nm and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2007); from chlorophyll, the absorption by phytoplankton (Bricaud et al. 1995) and
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: Deep research and agentic search agents autonomously retrieve content from the open web and generate reports with citations, and their outputs are often taken directly as research conclusions. This paper systematizes security research in this area along four stages, namely retrieval, planning, evidence integration, and report generation. We present a unified threat model, a taxonomy of attacks and defenses, and a review of evaluation benchmarks, and we align the area dimension by dimension with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) poisoning, prompt injection, and generative engine optimization (GEO). Coding 34 primary studies shows that only 26.5% of them involve the planning stage, and none performs an end-to-end poisoning evaluation on commercial products. To address this gap, we propose the agenda seeding attack, in which the attacker writes no instructions and only introduces a fictitious evaluation metric. Across 3,520 sandboxed research runs under the same budget, GEO and prompt injection are nearly ineffective, whereas agenda seeding makes the attacker's target the top pick in 16% to 28% of reports. Injection detection and query anchoring fail against it, verification prompting hurts utility, and our proposed provenance tagging preserves utility but can be bypassed by multi-site bait. Finally, we propose eight research directions.
title: Security of Deep Research Agents: Attack Surface, Defenses, Benchmarks, and Agenda Seeding against Research Planning

summary: Assistants built on large language models (LLMs) are entering power system operation. Current designs delegate computations to validated solvers, but the agent still infers the type, role and state of each element from its name and tool-specific formats, and errors propagate to every study. The Common Information Model (CIM), the IEC standard in which operators already exchange network models, defines unambiguously what each element is and how it connects. We propose a CIM layer for LLM grid assistants and implement it in CONDUCTOR, an open-source assistant. Both the agent and its power-system studies read the layer. It labels the provenance of each fact (stated in the data, suggested only by a name, or inferred from topology), loads operators' CGMES models directly, and builds in $\leq$1\,s on the 9,241-bus PEGASE network. Deterministic checks compare every answer with solver results and the layer. On 37 tasks about the CIGRE medium-voltage and IEEE 30-bus networks, the agent gets right 97\,\% of the graded facts with the layer, such as a unit's energy source or a switch's normal state, against 55\,\% without it. We argue that a CIM layer should be a default component of grid assistants.
title: The Grid's Own Language: A Common Information Model Layer for LLM Grid Assistants

summary: Timely urban-canopy information is essential for linking remote sensing with heat, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture Imagery Program imagery (0.6 m RGB+NIR). DeepForest generated crown candidates; an NDVI threshold, non-maximum suppression, and box-prompted Segment Anything Model (ViT-B) produced a crown-anchored canopy surface. Analyses used the 25.92 km2 Census TIGER municipal boundary and a 100 m grid. The workflow retained 11,741 candidate crowns and mapped 7.71 km2 of canopy (29.8% of the city). On the identical extent, pixel precision was 0.804, pixel recall was 0.873, and 97.4% of candidate centers agreed with the 2022 USDA/CAL FIRE LiDAR-assisted canopy product (IoU 0.719; Dice 0.837; area recovery 108.5%). Approximately 49% of candidates occurred within 15 m of a road. Canopy was inversely associated with Landsat land-surface temperature (Spearman rho = -0.477; partial rho = -0.551 controlling for built probability), and spatial-lag modeling confirmed clear neighborhood structure. Two transparent attention surfaces combined canopy need with thermal and contextual indicators. The framework provides a reproducible, updateable screening layer that complements structural canopy products and municipal inventories while retaining assumptions, data provenance, and spatial diagnostics for planning interpretation.
title: Optical GeoAI and spatial modeling enable urban-canopy mapping and resilience screening in Davis, California

summary: Magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides are layered materials with highly tunable magnetic orders and unconventional transport properties. Here we report a surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in $\mathrm{M}_{1/3}\mathrm{T}\mathrm{X}_{2}$, in which the surface and bulk favor distinct magnetic orders. In $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) results are reproduced by an A-type antiferromagnetic electronic structure, while neutron scattering and bulk DFT+$U$ calculations identify stripe order as the bulk ground state. DFT+$U$ slab calculations resolve this contradiction by showing that relaxation of an Fe-terminated surface reverses the magnetic preference from stripe to A-type order. The same dichotomy recovers the $K$-centered Fermi-surface pockets that are observed in $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Ta}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ but absent from previous bulk calculations. Notably, the surface-stabilized magnetic phase of $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ carries nonrelativistic spin splitting and can exhibit altermagnetic character. These results caution against the general association of ARPES signals with bulk magnetic states in these systems, and suggest surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy as a promising route to realize magnetic phases, including altermagnetism, that are not energetically favored in the bulk.
title: Surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides

summary: Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) is a derivative-free and parallelizable method for parameter estimation in Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive forward models. It adapts Kalman filtering by repeatedly assimilating the observation data through an artificial dynamical system with identity state evolution and the parameter-to-observation map as its observation operator. However, its performance can be limited by ensemble collapse and confinement to the affine span of the initial ensemble. We propose an exploration-enhanced EKI framework that combines multiplicative covariance inflation with a projected-dropout correction of the ensemble mean. Inflation helps maintain ensemble spread, while projected dropout enables the mean to explore directions beyond the initial affine span. For linear inverse problems, we provide a discrete-time, finite-ensemble analysis of the resulting method and prove the least-squares objective converges exponentially to its minimum in expectation. Within the initial ensemble subspace, the contraction factor is independent of the conditioning of the inverse problem, and the limiting ensemble covariance provides a low-rank representation of the posterior covariance. Experiments on ill-conditioned linear systems, 100-dimensional nonlinear benchmarks, and a PDE-constrained barotropic flow inverse problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
title: Enhancing Exploration in Ensemble Kalman Inversion via Covariance Inflation and Projected Dropout

summary: Auroras provide remote optical observations of energetic electrons precipitating into the upper atmosphere, and whose energy distribution encodes key information about large scale magnetospheric processes. Recovering the underlying electron precipitation field from ground-based camera images of auroras remains a challenging inverse problem. Existing auroral tomography techniques are often limited to simplified static settings, discrete spatial and energy grids, or strong assumptions on the electron energy spectrum. We propose to model the dynamic auroral electron precipitation field via a temporally conditioned neural network. The state of the precipitation field at each frame is represented by a per-frame latent code driven by learned discrete dynamics. A shared decoder maps horizontal positions and latent states to electron energy spectra. The predicted flux is converted to multi-wavelength volume emission rates and rendered into camera images accounting for delayed emissions. We evaluate the method on synthetic dynamic auroral sequences and real multi-view auroral videos, showing that the proposed representation produces temporally coherent precipitation reconstructions and image projections consistent with the observations.
title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Auroral Precipitations with Neural Fields

summary: We document the data reduction, reconstruction choices, and available uncertainty propagation underlying fifteen PHAROS stellar spectral energy distributions from 0.5 to 5000 nm. A catalogue timeline and a practical FITS guide introduce the available products, their column and extension conventions, and examples of reading, integration, and uncertainty display. Shared methods are presented once, including flux geometry, support-aware integration, X-ray likelihoods, the 2025 X/EUV luminosity relation, intrinsic Ly$α$ inference, airglow treatment, spectral junctions, and covariance-aware resampling. Target sections record the adopted observations and alternatives, including spatially separated binary components, unresolved system-level EUV measurements, direct EUVE constraints, optical stellar-twin transfer, and literature-anchored cases where new spectral inference is unsupported. The distinction between native measurement errors, conditional model intervals, empirical predictive scatter, and physical-method sensitivity is maintained. Signed measurements and nonnegative irradiation products are distinguished. Each target section concludes with the final nominal spectrum and its available uncertainty bounds on common axes. This library provides the detailed provenance and interpretation needed to accompany the catalogue paper and its machine-readable products.
title: The PHAROS Spectral Library: Data Processing, Spectral Reconstruction, and Uncertainty Propagation

summary: Learning the underlying probability distribution from samples is a core problem in statistics and applied mathematics. Generative models based on diffusion and flow matching learn a velocity field whose flow transports a known distribution to the data distribution. They produce novel, realistic samples, although the empirical learning problem is ill posed near the data distribution. Its minimizer transports the samples onto the training data, and small perturbations of the data change the velocity field strongly near the end of the flow. The observed generalization is often attributed to implicit regularization by the network parameterization, early stopping of the training, and the time integration during sampling. Explicit regularization has advanced the theory and computation of many inverse problems and has recently been proposed to prevent memorization in generative models. With a regularizer on the magnitude of the velocity, however, the field approaches the memorizing velocity unless the regularization parameter grows to infinity fast enough, and it then stays bounded by a constant that is small only for large parameters. We show that penalizing the derivatives of order $k$ of the velocity renders the $D$-dimensional empirical problem well posed uniformly in time if $2k > D$ and the training points are in general position. Our experiments in one and two dimensions discretize the velocity with splines and use direct solvers for the regularized least-squares problems to exclude optimization error. Refining the discretization in space and time changes the error of the Hessian-regularized flows only marginally, whereas without the regularizer the error tends to that of memorization. These flows generalize, with errors comparable to or lower than those of well-tuned kernel density estimates.
title: Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching

summary: This document describes all files associated with the Reverse Meta-analysis Project, a semester-long project for PSY 8121: History and Methods of Psychology at the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities, taught by Moin Syed, Ph.D. All files relevant for this project have a prefix of “PSY8121_” .
title: PSY8121 Reverse Meta-analysis Project Information (README)

summary: Fixed folds, an evaluation harness, a leakage checker and per-fold uncertainty for three distinct prediction tasks over the M2OR database of olfactory receptor bioassay records: T1 new molecule — scaffold-disjoint, five repeated splits: will this receptor respond to a chemotype not in training? T2 new source — publication-disjoint: will this laboratory's screen report a positive? T3 replication — publication-disjoint, test restricted to pairs already called positive by a training source: will an independent laboratory reproduce a reported positive? The harness rebuilds pair-level consensus labels inside each fold from training sources only, runs a four-way leakage audit (pairs, molecules, scaffolds, sources) on every fold and reports it as a table, and reports each fold with a percentile bootstrap interval instead of pooling folds into a single figure. Four reference models run on every fold: random forest, L2 logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting on Morgan fingerprints with a receptor indicator, plus a receptor prior that uses no chemical information at all and predicts each receptor's positive rate in the training fold. The prior is a diagnostic, not a recommended model: a result that does not clear it has not been shown to use chemical structure. Also included: an independent re-implementation of the three headline label-reliability statistics, written without reference to the primary analysis code and using only the Python standard library for parsing; the label-composition and dose-dependence statistics; two controls on the new-source result (a study-design split and a Dawid–Skene relabelling); and the code that regenerates every figure in the accompanying paper. The M2OR release of 28 April 2023 is redistributed unmodified under the Apache License 2.0 so that the exact bytes the paper analysed remain available; see NOTICE. Please cite the database (doi:10.1093/nar/gkad886) in addition to this record.
title: M2OR-Provenance: a three-task benchmark for olfactory receptor activity prediction

summary: Code and derived data for Recertifying Quantized Vision–Language Models under Changes in Calibration and Answer Scoring , by Nam-Hyun Yoo, Hyojin Park, and Jinhong Yang. Version 1.1.0 combines the native-score calibration study, the original answer/end-token decomposition, expanded allocation and threshold-grid sensitivity analyses, and a prospectively registered extension on one RTX 5080. The extension contains 54,400 scored records with answer and end-token components, 8,192 greedy-generated responses, 48 scorer-specific calibration policies, and statistical summaries for the registered hypotheses. The prospective protocol is archived separately at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24294124 . The registered scoring analysis uses 4,000 U images disjoint from the original 1,024-image B diagnostic. Native predictions on U had previously been used as unlabeled calibration observations, and public annotations had been parsed for eligibility. Scorer-specific calibration reuses the labeled calibration and evaluation samples. The records distinguish these data exposures, exploratory analyses, prospective hypotheses, and generated-response comparisons. The archive provides Python code, ordered identifiers, derived binary labels, predictions, score components, generated token records, fitted policies, numerical figure and table data, validation records, checksums, a data dictionary, and CPU reproduction instructions. Project-root paths are normalized for distribution; provenance records map original and public file hashes and verify preservation of numerical content. The earlier immutable release remains available at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24281585 . Original benchmark images and pretrained model weights are obtained from their cited official sources and are not redistributed. The manuscript is not included in this deposit. Original study code is licensed under MIT; original derived numerical results, figures, and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Included source-derived annotations retain their upstream terms, including VQAv2 CC BY 4.0 and CV-Bench/NaturalBench Apache-2.0. See the included license files and third-party notices. Supported by the Development and Demonstration of AI Services for Manufacturing Industry Specialization grant, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, Republic of Korea, project SG20240201.
title: Recertifying Quantized Vision–Language Models under Changes in Calibration and Answer Scoring: Code and Derived Data

summary: Intrusion detection systems are a central defence in modern networks. Deep learning models report strong anomaly-detection results, but evaluations on standard benchmarks such as CSE-CIC-IDS-2018 are often inflated by two methodological problems: temporal leakage from overlapping sliding windows, and contamination from preprocessing fitted before the train/test split. Per-flow classifiers also ignore the spatio-temporal dependencies across sequences of network flows. We propose a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network (ST-GAT) that represents traffic as a sequence of graph snapshots. It builds k-Nearest Neighbour (k-NN) edges within each window, applies multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) layers for spatial aggregation, and uses a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network with temporal attention for sequence modelling. To prevent leakage, we use non-overlapping temporal windows (stride equal to window length) and fit all preprocessing on the training split only. We compare three class-imbalance strategies: inverse class-frequency weighting, dynamic balanced sampling, and few-shot metric prototyping. Across three random seeds, ST-GAT with inverse class weighting reached a Macro-F1 of 96.65% (+/- 0.87) and an accuracy of 99.14%. This is 14.3 percentage points higher in Macro-F1 than a per-flow Random Forest baseline (82.34%). Balanced sampling reduced Macro-F1 by 2.3 points (to 94.37%) relative to loss weighting. This suggests that aggressive resampling of small, noisy minority classes can hurt detection in heavily imbalanced traffic.
title: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection

summary: AI assistants are becoming part of how knowledge workers think and perform, accumulating the prompts, exemplars, memory and interaction histories that encode a worker's professional judgment. This infrastructure typically runs under employer or platform control. We name the resulting process expertise capture, the absorption of worker-applied knowledge and judgment into AI resources under organizational control. We develop a framework of contribution forms, technical residences and transformation families, and show that how far a contribution can be attributed, separated and revoked depends on where it resides and how it has been transformed, properties fixed by system design long before any dispute arises. When a worker departs, the organization retains a capability shaped by their judgment while the worker loses access to it, and the asymmetry compounds as contributions move from inspectable artifacts into derivatives, learned components and successor systems. We outline three measures, write-time provenance, extraction of separable contributions and an executable exit procedure, that make an agreed allocation technically performable, and make explicit what cannot be separated at all.
title: Expertise capture in workplace AI

summary: Apple Reference Image (ARI) combines camera-sensor signatures, Secure Enclave attestation (SEP), cryptographic timestamp bounds, Private Cloud Compute (PCC), and a final post-quantum signature to establish photographic provenance. PCC is central to this process because it validates the secure digital negative and develops authenticated raw sensor measurements into a reference JPEG. Although the secure digital negative is encrypted during transmission, the authorized PCC workload must process the raw pixels in plaintext. This requirement creates a provenance-privacy paradox: cloud processing strengthens the provenance guarantee while giving an Apple-authorized, machine-learning-capable workload access to valuable, hardware-authenticated raw imagery. We argue that workload attestation and transparency-log inclusion verify software identity and authorization but do not, by themselves, prove that an authorized workload cannot learn from or retain information derived from the photograph. We implement this counterexample in a Python- and Docker-based experimental testbed that models relevant ARI and PCC functions. Across 27 public-domain photographs, a baseline workload and a learning-enabled workload both passed the same verification checks and returned byte-for-byte identical JPEGs. However, the learning-enabled workload retained a first-layer gradient of approximately 48 KB from which its 64 x 64 input was reconstructed with a maximum absolute per-pixel error of 6 x 10^-8. The additional processing overhead was small relative to image decoding and processing. These results do not demonstrate that Apple currently trains on ARI photographs or reproduce production PCC, but identify non-learning and non-retention as independently verifiable assurance requirements.
title: The Provenance-Privacy Paradox: Can Private Cloud Compute (PCC) Prove That Apple Reference Images Are Not Used for Learning?

summary: In this work, we study on-policy distillation (OPD) for transferring agentic coding capabilities from a large teacher model to a smaller student model. Prior work has focused primarily on reasoning and short-horizon agentic tasks. We present SWE-OPD, a minimal OPD study for software engineering, where the student interacts with executable repositories and the teacher supervises the prefixes visited by the student. Across three teacher--student pairs, two training sources, and three SWE benchmarks, we find that on-policy supervision transfers coding capability: supervision from Qwen3.6-27B increases the SWE-bench Pro resolve rate of Qwen3.5-9B from 35.9% to 39.4%. Refreshing trajectories is not strictly required either, as an offline variant with cached teacher scores still improves over the student baselines while cutting end-to-end GPU-hours by 59.4%--72.6% and halving peak GPU allocation, at benchmark-dependent accuracy. Furthermore, we extend the offline variant to corss-tokenizer scenarios: distilling GLM-4.5-Air from DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 raises its SWE-bench Pro and Multilingual resolve rate from 35.8% to 39.7% and from 41.8% to 46.2%, around 4% and 4.6% improvement, respectively. We also find that a decreasing loss, however, does not necessarily indicate improved agent performance: under top-$K$ reverse-KL loss, one student exhibits severe repetition despite a decreasing loss. We identify a support-mass gradient term as a potential mechanism underlying this failure.
title: SWE-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Coding

summary: An embodied speaker's expressiveness depends not only on what is said, but also on how the voice sounds and how the body moves. However, existing joint speech-motion generation models are largely driven implicitly by transcript semantics or intermediate speech representations, offering little explicit control over motion hierarchy, body parts, or vocal style. To bridge this gap, we construct MotionSpeech, a structured benchmark for controllable joint speech-motion generation that includes transcripts, voice-style descriptions, and motion conditions at two hierarchical levels. Building on this benchmark, we propose DuoFlow, a dual-stream latent flow transformer that jointly denoises speech and motion under a shared noise level and a unified second-based temporal coordinate. Modality-specific residual connectors inject structured conditions into the corresponding streams, layer-wise bidirectional cross-modal attention coordinates their generation, and a monotonic phoneme pathway combines normalized progress anchors with CTC supervision to strengthen speech temporal modeling. DuoFlow provides a unified interface for fine-grained motion and vocal-style control and demonstrates the ability to synthesize high-quality, synchronized, and instruction-consistent speech-motion sequences.
title: DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control

summary: Generative artificial intelligence complicates evidentiary assessment at the International Criminal Court by enabling fabricated audiovisual material and making authentic digital evidence easier to dismiss as fake. This article calls the latter problem synthetic doubt: an objection alleging that a digital item may be AI-generated or AI-manipulated. Existing scholarship addresses digital evidence, open-source investigations and deepfakes in the ICC context. Yet the question of when synthetic doubt should trigger enhanced reliability review under the Rome Statute, without displacing the prosecution's burden under article 66 or compromising article 67 fair-trial rights, remains underdeveloped. The article proposes a three-stage framework: a baseline authenticity and provenance showing by the proponent; a case-specific articulation threshold for the objector; and proportionate reliability review by the Chamber under articles 64 and 69(4). The framework treats AI-related provenance information and synthetic-media detector outputs as contextual rather than dispositive.
title: Synthetic Doubt and the Integrity of Digital Proof before the International Criminal Court

summary: A conformal surface that alternates between sectoral low scattering and directive telemetry poses a shared-hardware inverse problem when both modes must use one finite passive impedance alphabet, although their spatial codebooks may differ. This paper formulates and solves that mixed continuous--discrete problem at the effective impedance-boundary level. Reference-centered Tikhonov preimages prescribe restricted radiation data; inverse-source null-space freedom then moves each current within its data-equivalent class toward impedance profiles quantizable by the same alphabet. A line-searched Gauss--Newton update, common-state assignment and projected-centroid updates, and exact forward refinement determine the currents, two codebooks, and one passive library. Data invariance, the current-to-impedance differential, the optimal state update, monotonic mismatch reduction, and a forward perturbation bound are derived. A full-mutual-coupling two-dimensional TM study of a $4λ_0$-diameter cylinder uses 64 physical cells and one shared eight-state library. On a 256-unknown validation model, the worst power ratio over $\pm10^{\circ}$ monostatic sectors and incidence angles from $-30^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$ is $-11.6$~dB relative to a PEC cylinder; telemetry directivity is 13.1~dB with $-13.6$-dB peak sidelobes and a $1^{\circ}$ pointing error. A separate Fourier--Galerkin formulation, converged through 513 complex modes without reoptimization, gives $-11.36$~dB and 13.02~dB for the corresponding worst-sector and directivity metrics. The results establish feasibility at the effective impedance-boundary level; they do not establish unit-cell, bias-network, or platform-level realizability.
title: Shared-State Inverse Synthesis of Dual-Mode Conformal Metasurfaces for Low Scattering and Telemetry

summary: Design decisions shape software architecture, and writing them down preserves the reasons behind it. Architecture decision records (ADRs) capture them, each with its context, choice, and consequences. A decision can depend on earlier ones: reversing one of them would force its review. We call these its premises. Yet ADRs do not always name their premises. When a decision is reversed, engineers supersede its ADR and search by hand for what it affects. That search can miss ADRs resting on an unnamed premise. We frame this as premise recovery: given an ADR with identifiers masked, find its premises among earlier records. We collect 1,060 ADRs from 36 repositories and label 1,529 candidate pairs for 60 target ADRs. Two LLM annotators agree at \k{appa} = 0.859. An independent human annotator, blind to their labels, agrees with the stated/implicit tag on 30 of 32 premises (\k{appa} = 0.875). We compare 7 open-weight models with 2 baselines that use no LLM. Qwen3.8-27B reaches F1 0.756, against 0.466 for word overlap; 2 models added post hoc score similarly. On the 11 premises whose titles barely overlap the target, it finds 0.758, while word overlap finds none. Reasoning raises its recall of implicit premises but not its F1. Word overlap with as many predictions gains 69% as much. We find only 2 to 3 stale dependents, though we searched for unlinked ones in only 30 of 66 supersessions. Open models could thus suggest unwritten premises when a decision is reversed, with precision between 0.68 and 0.78.
title: Premise Recovery in Software Design: What Does This Decision Rest On?

summary: In this paper, we propose a method to recover simultaneously the shape and wavenumber of an object from noisy radar or sonar measurements. The physical problem is modeled in a bounded domain with the Helmholtz equation and appropriate transmission conditions. The approach relies on a Kohn-Vogelius formulation of the inverse problem and uses Nesterov's accelerated gradient descent combined with shape optimization techniques. To address the robustness of the method with respect to measurement noise, we are looking to minimize a convex combination of the expected value and variance, which we achieve by using a Karhunen-Lo{è}ve expansion. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through twodimensional numerical experiments.
title: Simultaneous reconstruction of an obstacle and its wavenumber for the Helmholtz equation: a robust optimization approach

summary: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moiré Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling ν_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moiré Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.
title: Moiré Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet

summary: Solar tower power plants provide dispatchable, renewable energy by concentrating sunlight with thousands of mirrors, called heliostats, onto a central receiver. Efficient operation requires accurate modeling of the optical path from each heliostat to the receiver and compensation for manufacturing imperfections, kinematic misalignment, and material degradation that distort the flux distribution. Conventional ray tracers predict the flux from an assumed plant model but are limited to forward simulation. They cannot recover unknown plant parameters from measured flux nor directly optimize plant operation. We present artist, an open-source, FAIR4RS-compliant Python package implementing a fully differentiable digital twin of solar tower power plants. By making the optical pipeline, comprising heliostat surface representation, kinematics, blocking, and ray tracing, end to end differentiable, artist turns the digital twin from a passive forward model into an active physics-based tool for inverse modeling and data-driven optimization. The resulting gradient-based framework unifies tasks usually handled by separate solutions, such as reconstructing heliostat surfaces and kinematics from operational flux images without costly deflectometry, predicting irradiance at the receiver, and optimizing aim points to realize a desired receiver flux density distribution. Built on PyTorch, artist scales to real plants through GPU acceleration, a structure-of-arrays memory layout, and nested data parallelism. It interfaces with open data sources such as the PAINT database. We describe the software architecture, physical models, and optimization framework, and demonstrate the workflow on representative tasks. By integrating modeling, prediction, and optimization into a single open, interpretable package, artist provides a principled foundation for data-driven research toward autonomous solar tower operation.
title: artist: A Python package for differentiable ray tracing and gradient-based optimization of solar tower power plant operation

summary: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties from measurements. We develop a comprehensive suite of property identification tasks focused on hardware mechanisms relevant to Spectre-class attacks, covering speculative execution, branch prediction, memory dependence, and cache behavior. We evaluate ProcReverser on the XuanTie C910, the gem5 RISC-V O3 CPU model, and the SiFive P550. ProcReverser achieves Pass@1 and Pass@5 scores of 81.3% and 93.8%, respectively, on C910, and 83.0% and 100.0% on gem5 O3. On the SiFive P550, ProcReverser further characterizes microarchitectural properties covered by the proposed task suite. These findings highlight the potential of automated microarchitectural reverse engineering to support processor vulnerability analysis and defense evaluation.
title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis

summary: Speculative decoding reduces generation cost, but it stores two KV caches: one for the target model and one for the draft model. We reduce this extra memory by quantizing the draft cache. The target cache and verifier remain in BF16, so that compression cannot change the target model's final correction rule. We first study how to divide precision between keys and values. A naive per-token quantizer makes keys appear much more sensitive: splitting a 12-bit budget, K8V4 beats K4V8 in acceptance by 10.87pp. However, with grouped per-channel keys, the gap becomes -0.25pp. A controlled Qwen test confirms that changing only the key quantizer can erase or reverse the preferred bit split. Hence, following KIVI, we propose K4V4 quantization with per-channel keys and per-token values. Across six model pairs, our method reduces draft cache memory by 66.20%, and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%. Mean acceptance drops from 57.93% to 57.14%, only 1.36% relative. Overall, quantized draft caches can make speculative decoding more memory efficient; as a predictive principle for efficient AI design, key and value precision must be co-designed with the quantizer layout.
title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache

summary: Recent megajoule laser inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments have demonstrated thermonuclear target gain above unity, yet scaling pulsed laboratory ignition to commercial 1–20 Hz Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) power plants remains obstructed by six coupled physics and engineering bottlenecks: hydrodynamic Rayleigh–Taylor (RT) and Richtmyer–Meshkov instabilities, core contamination from mechanical target support tents and fill tubes, parasitic cross-beam energy transfer (CBET) and stimulated Brillouin/Raman backscatter (SBS/SRS), critical-density reflection and solid gold cone vaporization in petawatt fast ignition, dielectric mirror blistering and positive plasma pulse dispersion, and the absence of non-destructive focal-plane phase diagnostics in high vacuum. This paper presents an integrated theoretical and reactor-engineering solution derived from the Lorentz Invariant / Localized Intrinsic Field Equilibrium (LIFE) framework, governed by the exact four-dimensional covariant divergence of the Maxwell stress-energy tensor (∂ μ T μν = 0). By arranging subsets of N beam ≥ 4 coherent laser beamlines into mutually orthogonal pairs with quadratic sinusoidal cross-beam phase modulation, directional wave operators annihilate longitudinal radiation-drag force densities (f x = f z ≡ 0) while enforcing strictly forward longitudinal Poynting transport (S x, S z ≥ 0), eliminating coherent backscatter and replacing chaotic CBET with deterministic transverse Poynting routing. Along the mutual orthogonal axis, optical-cycle averaging via the Jacobi–Anger Bessel expansion establishes a stationary three-dimensional ponderomotive restoring lattice with zero net volume momentum bias, enabling both stalk-free high-vacuum cryogenic pellet levitation and dynamic RT shear damping during implosion. For fast-ignition architectures, orthogonal precursor guide beams induce an effective curved optical metric (n eff = c/v g > 1) forming an exponentially self-confined slow-light channel I core (r) = I 0 exp(−k|r|) that guides petawatt ignitor pulses directly into the stagnated fuel core without solid gold cones. Combined with coating-free corrugated monolithic bulk tungsten negative-dispersion wall optics and sub-millisecond vacuum three-beam differential interferometric and dual-divergence (∇·E, ∇·H) electro-optic feedback, the LIFE architecture provides a non-invasive upgrade path for existing megajoule and petawatt laser facilities as well as next-generation commercial IFE power plants. title: Three-Dimensional Synchro-Resonant Electromagnetic Confinement, Ponderomotive Rayleigh–Taylor Stabilization, and Cone-Free Slow-Light Fast Ignition in Multi-Beam Laser Fusion Reactors within the LIFE Framework

Phase 2 (Hypothesis Review) is now complete. The independent external review was signed and authorized by Jonathan Rabe (AI | ML Engineer, Angeles University Foundation) on 2026-11-17, confirming the (E) Undetermined (interim) decision. Links: - Paper (v1.0.0): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24278322 - Figshare preprint: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.35038726 - GitHub: https://github.com/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - GitHub Release v2.0.0: https://github.com/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman/releases/tag/v2.0.0 - GitLab: https://gitlab.com/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - Codeberg: https://codeberg.org/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - Bitbucket: https://bitbucket.org/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - Website: https://aetherhuman.netlify.app What v2.0.0 contains: - 5 functions under investigation (Fn1–Fn5): Human Principal Representation, Authority Relation, Intervention Semantics, Accountability Chain, Human-Agent Boundary. - 4 failure conditions (H-F1–H-F4): Non-redundancy, Distinction from Govern + Identity + Runtime, Decentralizability, Observable benefit. - 2 propositions (P1–P2): Determinism of human intervention semantics, Irreducible human authority anchor. - External Independent Review (signed by Jonathan Rabe). - Architectural hypothesis, responsibility boundaries, falsification plan, independence decision, internal review, and investigation report. - Evaluation Design Protocol (addressing Sybil delegation & latency). - Adversarial Threat Model (AT-1 to AT-4). - 9 figures (Fig1–Fig9). - No implementation, no tests, no experiments. summary: Two independent bulk RNA-sequencing datasets were generated using a zebrafish model of Dravet syndrome at 5 days post-fertilization (dpf). Dataset 1: Disease-associated transcriptional alterations Comparison of scn1lab−/− zebrafish with wild-type controls ( scn1lab+/+ ) to identify disease-associated changes in gene expression. scn1labvWT_metadata.txt scn1labvWT_unnormalised_counts.txt Dataset 2: Drug treatment and transcriptional response An independent dataset comprising scn1lab−/− zebrafish treated with sertraline, orphenadrine, brexpiprazole, fenfluramine, or DMSO. All treatment groups were compared against wild-type controls to investigate compound-induced transcriptional changes and their potential to reverse disease-associated gene expression signatures. scn1labvWT_treatment_metadata.txt scn1labvWT_treatment_unnormalised_counts.txt Data integration and batch correction Both datasets contain unnormalized gene-level RNA-sequencing counts and corresponding sample metadata. Although generated independently, the datasets can be analyzed jointly using appropriate batch correction or statistical models that account for dataset-specific effects. This enables integrated comparisons of disease-associated and treatment-induced transcriptional changes, provided that batch effects can be distinguished from the biological conditions of interest.
title: From molecular dysfunction to therapeutic discovery: Novel targets and drug repurposing candidates for Dravet syndrome

summary: The package contains four current Round-2 annotation sets covering the same 236 publicly documented B2B generative-AI use cases across 26 professional roles and five functional areas, yielding 944 coder–task records. The annotated dimensions are agency component, delegation degree, task structuredness and error criticality. Additional materials include a reduced, adapted extract of the original published task covariates; an earlier version of Coder 1’s delegation annotations for historical sensitivity analysis; Python analysis and validation scripts; aggregate results; supplementary tables; and documentation of variables, methods and provenance. Analyses cover inter-rater agreement, matched task comparisons, predictor-source substitution, role-cluster bootstrap uncertainty and exploratory logistic GEE models. The original task inventory is available in Mendeley Data under DOI 10.17632/vp6pxrbrpz.1. Its classifications serve as a comparison source, not as a fifth independent Round-2 coder. The earlier Coder 1 version is a historical sensitivity condition, not an additional independent evaluator. Coder identities are pseudonymised as C1–C4. Public task identifiers are retained to support reproducibility and linkage to the original dataset. Private linkage keys, original coding forms, personal declarations, task descriptions and the consolidated private research master are excluded. These annotations concern the interpretation of task descriptors. They do not establish observed organisational AI behaviour or verified operational autonomy. Uncertainty summaries are conditional on the 26 professional roles represented in the dataset.
title: Independent annotations of human–AI agency delegation in professional tasks: data and reproducibility code.

summary: Python code accompanying the manuscript "Thermal Mode Coupling and Identifiability Limits in Photothermal Diffraction Tomography". It implements the exact Ewald accessibility test, Fourier-chain harmonic and transient solutions of the heat equation with spatially varying conductivity, the first-order rank analysis, noise-scenario detection power, the positive-source counterexample and an independent finite-volume check. All calculations are analytic or synthetic; no measured data are included. Running analysis.py and expanded_figures.py reproduces all tables and figures of the manuscript.
