Hence, following KIVI, we propose K4V4 quantization with per-channel keys and per-token values. Across six model pairs, our method reduces draft cache memory by 66.20%, and combined memory across both caches by 23.95%. Mean acceptance drops from 57.93% to 57.14%, only 1.36% relative. Overall, quantized draft caches can make speculative decoding more memory efficient; as a predictive principle for efficient AI design, key and value precision must be co-designed with the quantizer layout.
title: Memory-Efficient Speculative Decoding with Quantized Draft KV Cache

summary: Latent KV cache compression reduces memory footprint by mapping historical keys and values into compact representations. However, generic compressed key states require reconstruction to native dimension before applying RoPE and computing attention scores, adding sequence-scaling overhead to the decode path. We characterize when a latent KV representation can serve directly as the execution state of pretrained RoPE. For RoPE-based transformers, exact static linear execution of the rotary key path requires the latent-to-native map to preserve the pretrained RoPE action through an intertwining relation, restricting exact mixing to coordinates that share the same RoPE frequency. Guided by this characterization, we build GaugeRoPE, a training-free executable latent KV representation. It combines a RoPE-compatible carrier that preserves the rotary action with an approximate position-independent residual key--value (RKV) correction for complementary key and value information, both evaluated without per-token dense historical K/V reconstruction. On Mistral-7B, GaugeRoPE achieves $5.85\times$ KV compression while maintaining quality close to the full-cache baseline. Additional MHA results validate the construction beyond GQA. GaugeRoPE achieves up to $2.48\times$ the decode throughput of the vanilla uncompressed baseline through direct latent execution.
title: GaugeRoPE: RoPE-Compatible Executable Latent Attention

summary: Kohn-Sham solver for isolated atoms using the finite-element discrete variable representation (FE-DVR). Pseudo-atoms with norm-conserving pseudopotentials in UPF format, including pseudopotentials without pseudo-atomic orbitals (e.g. SG15) All-electron atoms (non-relativistic), plus approximate scalar-relativistic (Koelling-Harmon) and ZORA treatments LDA and GGA functionals: PBE built in, all others via libxc Confined atomic orbitals with polarization functions for use as localized basis functions or projectors, exported on a logarithmic grid (Quantum ESPRESSO style), on the FE-DVR grid, or as spherical Bessel transforms; dipole matrix elements Photoemission : scattering phase shifts and dipole matrix elements to continuum states 🚀 Installation $ python3 -m pip install atomic_femdvr   The built-in exchange-correlation driver provides PBE. Other functionals (e.g. the LDA used for the NIST benchmark) need the libxc Python bindings, which are not on PyPI; see the installation guide . 💪 Getting started Calculations are defined by a JSON input file. A pseudo-atom with a confinement potential and polarization orbitals ( examples/Si_Pseudo.json ): { "control" : { "storage_dir" : " ./Si_pseudo " }, "sysparams" : { "element" : " Si " , "file_upf" : " ../tests/data/Si/Si.oncvpsp.upf " , "lmax" : 2 , "nmax" : 1 }, "dft" : { "xc_functional" : " PBE " , "mixing_scheme" : " anderson " , "alpha_mix" : 0.5 }, "confinement" : { "type" : " SoftStep " , "rc" : 20.0 , "ri_factor" : 0.5 , "polarization_mode" : " SoftCoul " }, "output" : { "output_wfc_qe" : true , "output_wfc_bessel" : true } }   $ cd examples $ atomic_femdvr pseudoatomic Si_Pseudo.json -t scf,nscf out   This solves the Kohn-Sham equations self-consistently ( scf ), computes two confined radial functions each for s, p and d ( nscf ), and writes them to out/ . All energies are in Hartree and all lengths in bohr. The all-electron solver is run with atomic_femdvr atomic (see examples/Ne_full.json ). See the documentation for the input reference, the method and the output formats. ✅ Validation All-electron : LDA eigenvalues agree with the NIST atomic reference data (Ne, to 2e-6 Ha). Pseudo-atoms : eigenvalues reproduce the all-electron reference energies stored by ONCVPSP in the UPF file to about 0.5 meV (Mo, Si). The scalar-relativistic and ZORA options are approximate and have not been benchmarked. summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24314752 . Reviewer Report: Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine Manuscript: "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems" (G. Yang; Preprints.org , doi:10.20944/preprints202603.0470.v1, posted 5 March 2026) Type of report: Point-by-point reviewer report, prepared to help the author strengthen the work before journal submission. The manuscript proposes a computational "multi-track cognition" (MTC) framework that lets data from different medical systems (traditional Chinese medicine, biomedicine, Tibetan medicine, with others said to be addable) be compared and fused without forcing one system's vocabulary onto another. The author's stated aim is to move beyond format-level standardisation towards semantic alignment, and beyond single-point linear correspondence towards system-level mapping. Importance of the research area. Integrative medicine is widely practised and increasingly supported by health policy, including the World Health Organization's strategic work on traditional and complementary medicine. A persistent barrier to generating integrated evidence is that systems describe the patient and the intervention in different conceptual languages. Examples are pattern differentiation, nature and flavour, and meridian tropism on one side, and disease categories, biomarkers and molecular targets on the other. A general and extensible way to connect these descriptions would be useful for evidence synthesis, chronic-disease management and individualised care. The author appropriately targets semantic, and not merely syntactic, interoperability, which is a question that merits careful methodological work. Approach proposed. The framework has three layers (Figure 1; Section 2): 1. Cognitive tracks (Section 2.1). Each medical system has its own track with a native feature set, normalisation rules and a native "systemic effect" index. 2. Homeostatic representation network, HRN (Section 2.2). A directed acyclic graph of 28 laboratory indicators across eight physiological systems serves as the shared anchor. Its topology comes from literature and three expert physicians. Its parameters are learned with a Bayesian network on MIMIC-III. 3. System-level mapping (Section 2.3). A random forest, guided by three rules (cluster correspondence, network emergence, context dependence), is trained with a mean-squared-error loss to predict post-intervention changes in the HRN indicators. Performance is judged by Semantic Alignment Accuracy (SAA, the share of cases in which two mapped vectors reach cosine similarity ≥ 0.85), R², MAE and RMSE (Section 2.4). Evidence reported (Section 3). Four public datasets are used (Table 1), with a 70/30 split and 5-fold cross-validation. In the TCM–Western dual-track setting the framework reports SAA 91.27% and R² 0.852, against 59.13–76.58% SAA for three baselines (Table 2). A three-system extension adding Tibetan medicine reports SAA 86.34% and R² 0.821 (Section 3.4). Agreement with three clinical experts is reported as κ = 0.86, and a Lung–Spleen Qi Deficiency case illustrates the workflow (Section 3.5). The author concludes that the framework is lossless, general, and ready to support clinical integration. Strengths. The following strengths provide a sound basis for revision: • The problem is timely and clinically meaningful. • The modular idea, with track-specific components and one shared core, is attractive and in principle testable. • An outcome-level physiological anchor is a practical way to compare interventions that act through different theories. • The model, loss, hyperparameters and pseudo-code are stated explicitly, which allows scrutiny. • The author attempts expert annotation, effect sizes and a multi-system extension. •
title: PREreview of "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems"

summary: Adding new parameters to the baseline distribution using the generated family concept has been one of the most commonly used techniques in recent years. The Median-based Unit Rayleigh (MBUR) is a one-parameter unit distribution. In this paper, the author added another parameter using the Topp_Loene generated family. The new approach not used previously in the literature is to use the Lomax distribution. The author truncated the Lomax distribution to obtain the unit-truncated Lomax distribution and used it as a generator to elaborate the unit-truncated Lomax-generated MBUR distribution. The derivations of the new generalized forms are discussed. The properties of both distributions, including the quantile function and raw moments, are discussed in detail.   The quantile functions can be expressed in a closed form, while the raw moments cannot be expressed in a closed form. Both distributions have bathtub-shaped, J-shaped, and increasing shape hazard rates. Real data analysis is performed to compare the fitness of both distributions.
title: Topp Leone Generated MBUR and Unit Truncated Lomax Generated MBUR Distributions: New Generalization of The MBUR Distribution

summary: Data and Stata code for a study of whether social capital predicts retained luxury imports. The outcome is imports less re-exports of four HS headings — 7113 jewellery, 9101 wristwatches with cases of precious metal, 4202 trunks, handbags and similar containers, and 3303 perfumes — scaled by population. Subtracting re-exports matters because entrepôt economies import these goods for onward shipment. The main regressor is the GSCI social capital dimension DIM_SC_30, a balanced annual series covering 247 countries. The full panel is 3,883 country-years across 184 countries, 2000–2023; the estimation sample with all controls is 3,241 country-years across 159 countries. A second, smaller panel uses the WVS/EVS Integrated Values Survey trust measure at wave level (86 country-waves, 36 OECD countries), with luxury imports averaged over a five-year window centred on each wave year. The package contains the UN Comtrade extract and the PowerShell script that produced it from the Comtrade public API, the World Bank control variables and their download script, the GSCI series, the Integrated Values Survey trust file, the Stata do-files and logs, and Figures 1–3. Code/Replication_Luxury_SocialCapital.do reproduces every table and figure in the paper. Nothing is interpolated: a country-year enters a panel only if it was observed. See README.md.
title: Social capital and retained luxury imports: replication data and Stata code for a global panel, 2000–2023

Public task identifiers are retained to support reproducibility and linkage to the original dataset. Private linkage keys, original coding forms, personal declarations, task descriptions and the consolidated private research master are excluded. Uncertainty summaries are conditional on the 26 professional roles represented in the dataset.

summary: This software record provides the source code and selected experimental artifacts associated with the research paper entitled "Blockchain-Anchored Data Continuity for Smart-City Digital Twins: A Dual-State Verification Framework." The project presents a hardware–software proof of concept for maintaining and verifying data continuity between IoT sensor records, a local hash-linked ledger, and a digital-twin-oriented dashboard. The prototype uses an ESP8266-based sensor node, a DHT11 temperature sensor, Python-based data acquisition, SQLite storage, SHA-256 record fingerprinting, and a Streamlit dashboard. The main contribution implemented in the software is a dual-state verification approach that distinguishes ledger integrity from source-record coverage. This distinction enables the detection of cases in which the ledger remains internally valid while one or more source records are not represented by corresponding ledger references. The released materials include: IoT data acquisition and database storage code. Local hash-linked ledger implementation. Source-to-ledger verification procedures. Six controlled data-tampering scenarios. Local verification performance measurement scripts. Digital Twin dashboard implementation. Solidity smart-contract and local EVM integration files. Experimental multi-replica demonstration and associated tests. The SQLite experimental database snapshot used in the study. The included baseline database contains 481 sensor records and 482 ledger blocks, including one genesis block. The verification experiments cover source-record consistency, hash-chain integrity, unique record association, and source-record coverage. The repository is intended to support inspection and reproduction of the software experiments described in the associated research paper. Results may vary depending on the execution environment, hardware, software dependencies, and database state. This release is a research proof of concept. It does not claim production-scale deployment, independent distributed consensus, sensor identity authentication, physical measurement accuracy, or full-scale urban digital-twin simulation. title: Blockchain-Anchored Data Continuity for Smart-City Digital Twins: A Dual-State Verification Framework

summary: Teaching English for Specific Purposes (ESP) at specialized sports universities presents distinct pedagogical challenges, primarily due to student-athletes' rigorous training schedules, frequent competition travel, and heterogeneous baseline language proficiency. This study investigates the pedagogical efficacy of integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven platforms and interactive digital tools into an ESP curriculum to enhance speaking fluency, domain-specific vocabulary acquisition, and learner autonomy among undergraduate sports students. A quasi-experimental study was conducted over one academic semester involving 64 second-year students divided into an experimental group ($n = 32$) and a control group ($n = 32$). While the control group received conventional textbook-based classroom instruction, the experimental group utilized AI conversational agents for simulated press conferences, automated speech recognition (ASR) tools for pronunciation feedback, and gamified digital platforms for sports terminology retention. Pre- and post-test assessments, alongside a post-intervention learner perception survey, demonstrated statistically significant improvements in the experimental group's oral proficiency, specialized lexical accuracy, and self-regulated learning engagement ($p < 0.001$). The findings indicate that AI-assisted and digital language environments offer flexible, personalized, and anxiety-reducing pathways that align effectively with the dynamic schedules and practical career needs of future sports professionals.

summary: This database has eight zip files, each containing monthly netcdfs of daily 1/24-degree (~4 km) gridded counterfactual climate data for the western US. Variables represented are daily precipitation total (prec; mm), maximum and minimum temperature (tmax and tmin, respectively; degrees C), mean vapor pressure (hPa), mean 2-m wind velocity (m/s), mean downwelling solar and longwave radiation at the surfae (solar and longwave, respectively; W/m2), and surface pressure (hPa). The counterfactual dataset is meant to represent an alternative realization of the observed climate from 1951–2025 from which anthropogenic trends in background means and daily variances about those means have been removed. The observed climate dataset is available from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19636838. Anthropogenic trends in background means and daily variances are estimatated to be represented by a weighted mean of trends simulated by 24 CMIP6 climate models under the historical (1850–2014) and SSP2-4.5 (2015–2100) scenarios. Trends in background means and daily variances are assessed relative to a baseline period of 1851–1900 (1851–1910 for daily variances). Model trends are weighted based on a combination of performance and independence following the ClimWIP method, where performace is assessed as agreement with the observed linear trend in global mean surface temperature from 1961–2025 and independence is assessed based on inter-model differences in maps of historical climatological mean surface air temperature and sea-level pressure. The methods used to produce the observational dataset, CMIP6 model weightings, and the counterfactual dataset are described in a manuscript submitted to Earth System Science Data. This dataset will be made publicly available upon publication of the corresponding paper.

summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. summary: Positioning: PubMed stores scientific papers. ScientificClaims.org stores the evolving answers to scientific questions. The Scientific Claim Registry (SCR) is infrastructure for the memory of science — not its truth, consensus, or recommendations. It registers, it does not arbitrate . What v0.5 adds over v0.4: v0.4 made every evidence link independently verified. v0.5 is the first version in which the registry has been kept current by its own Layer 1 surveillance loop (retrieve → classify → dual-model verify → promote/corroborate → recompile → version), and it reports what that took, including where it failed. Growth through the loop, not manual curation. From v0.4 to v0.5 the lipedema pilot grew from 347 to 526 evidence claims and from 423 to 626 evidence records (895 question–claim links, 383 distinct DOIs) under the same 42 versioned questions. Sources: (1) an unattended weekly rotating contradiction sweep (R-AI-12), June–September 2026, pairing each topical retrieval with a null/negative/opposing-evidence pass; (2) a library-scale backfill re-running all 42 questions against the author’s curated lipedema library (4,563 structured records) plus Europe PMC. Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified ; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note. Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise. Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict. Prior-art honesty: SCR does not invent the claim primitive or persistent claim identity — nanopublications/Trusty URIs, micropublications, Wikidata, CIViC, ClinGen, Epistemonikos/PICO, SciFact, GRADE and MAGICapp already exist. The v0.5 contribution is evidence that a question-centric, verified, versioned registry can be maintained by its own loop, with the failure modes of unattended operation documented and guarded. Operated by the BIO (Biological Intelligence Observatory) research method.

summary: This deposit accompanies the study “ Balancing predictive accuracy and structural interpretability in airborne LiDAR biomass models of Mediterranean forests ”. It provides anonymised, analysis-ready forest inventory biomass responses, area-based and crown-based airborne LiDAR predictor tables, fixed outer and inner spatial cross-validation folds, R source code, allometric equation registries, selected derived tables, and a reference figure for Mediterranean forests in Castilla y León, Spain. The analysis combines PNOA-LiDAR data acquired in 2017-2019 with Fourth Spanish National Forest Inventory (IFN4) field observations from 2019. The deposited prepared data support reproduction of the nested spatial modelling, validation, and reporting stages. The archive includes an automated integrity validator, an executable workflow launcher, a column-level variable inventory, package versions, workflow documentation, and SHA-256 checksums. Raw IFN4 records, PNOA point clouds, corrected plot coordinates, original plot identifiers and the confidential identifier crosswalk are not redistributed. Scripts documenting raw-data preparation are included, but reconstruction from raw sources requires obtaining the original data from their official providers and complying with their licences. Corrected IFN4 plot coordinates and original keys have been removed. The public plot_uid is a release-specific anonymised sequential identifier. Code is provided under the MIT License. Author-created anonymised data, tables, figures and documentation are provided under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Conditions and attribution requirements of the source datasets remain applicable. PNOA attribution: Obra derivada de PNOA-LiDAR 2017-2019, CC BY 4.0, Instituto Geográfico Nacional/Centro Nacional de Información Geográfica (IGN/CNIG), Spain.

summary: This reproducibility package supports the study “Wearable Stress Models Across Sessions and Exercise Conditions: A Cross-Dataset Evaluation with Same-Session Controls.” The study developed wearable stress classification models using the WESAD dataset and externally evaluated them using the Wearable Device Dataset from Induced Stress and Structured Exercise Sessions, PhysioNet version 1.0.1. The package contains the analysis scripts, locked study protocols, Protocol Amendment v1.1, source manifests, integrity records, model settings, aggregate results, and analysis-freeze outputs used to produce the reported findings. It covers the 20-second primary analysis, the 30-second sensitivity analysis, external stress-versus-rest transport qualification, cross-session affective and exercise evaluation, same-session exercise-minus-final-rest comparisons, internally derived operating points, protocol-version checks, and self-report alignment analyses. The original WESAD and PhysioNet datasets are not included or redistributed. Users must obtain the datasets from their respective official sources and comply with their original terms of use. The package contains no newly collected participant data and no directly identifying information. The package is intended to support transparent inspection and computational reproduction of the study procedures and aggregate results. Differences in software versions, operating systems, or access to the original third-party datasets may affect exact execution details. Version v3 includes an additional audit package containing scripts and aggregate results for the original 70-feature diagnostics, participant-level and exercise-stage error analysis, and AUROC transport-gate sensitivity at 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, and 0.75. The supplement uses the existing study outputs without changing the trained models, evaluation protocol, or source datasets. Original WESAD and PhysioNet recordings are not redistributed.

The package is intended to support transparent inspection and computational reproduction of the study procedures and aggregate results. Version v3 includes an additional audit package containing scripts and aggregate results for the original 70-feature diagnostics, participant-level and exercise-stage error analysis, and AUROC transport-gate sensitivity at 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, and 0.75. summary: Agentic ecosystems are emerging as a new platform layer in which agents maintain persistent memory, retrieve from shared knowledge bases, execute through tool interfaces, and coordinate through shared states. These capabilities create a security problem that per-turn defenses miss: compromise can accumulate across sessions, agents, and system layers before visible failure. We define this threat as Agentic Sleeper, a system-level adversary that first behaves legitimately, gains routing trust, and later activates across memory, agent logic, and infrastructure. We formulate defense as inference under partial observability and propose Swarm Shepherd, a system-level defense framework centered on an inference filter for early warning, paired with a backward trace-back module for entry attribution. Our analysis yields a two-scale deployment rule that balances longer event histories against broader agent coverage. Across LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen, Agentic Sleeper drift begins 2.7--8.9$\times$ faster than natural baselines, propagates across agents on most topologies, and evades per-turn and stateful defenses above 80\%. Swarm Shepherd warns at least three sessions before visible degradation (2.6 sessions when failure is scored by the benchmark's own task grader), while trace-back reaches 0.69 top-1 accuracy and 0.72 macro-F1 over 24 variants. The two-scale deployment rule is empirically confirmed, and in live end-to-end runs on LangGraph and AutoGen the posterior-guided defense stack drives cross-agent propagation below the self-sustaining regime, which removing only the visibly compromised agent does not achieve.
title: Swarm Shepherd: Securing Multi-Agent Ecosystems Against Persistent Latent Compromise

summary: On-ramp merging is a typical safety and throughput problem on highways. Without proper coordination, human drivers and self-interested autonomous vehicles may make risky manoeuvres and cause accidents or congestion. With recent advances in connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), vehicles can be trained to coordinate for safe and efficient merging. However, in dense traffic, forming an effective observation of the traffic state is challenging. For example, observing only the neighbouring vehicles may lead to locally optimal decisions, while observing the entire traffic can introduce much irrelevant information. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based MARL vehicle control model to address these problems. A roadside infrastructure controller receives the states of all CAVs via vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication and sends control commands back to them. An attention-based observation encoder is designed where each vehicle can filter the relevant vehicle information from the global traffic state. The proposed model is evaluated in SUMO against three baselines: a model that observes only the neighbouring vehicles, a model that encodes the global traffic information, and the rule-based SUMO model. The results show that our model achieves the highest traffic flow, safety and smoothness. Furthermore, in a four-hour simulation with dynamic traffic demand, our model successfully avoids traffic jams, while other baseline models fail at high traffic flow. We also show that our model remains effective when human-driven vehicles are present. We further show that our model, trained in ideal communication conditions, can still remain collision-free and maintain throughput under realistic V2I communication errors. Finally, we visualise the relevance weights that an ego vehicle assigns to other vehicles in multiple traffic situations.
title: Infrastructure-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Attention for Highway Ramp Merging

summary: As agentic systems are increasingly deployed to support complex Web tasks, multi-agent architectures offer greater parallelism, specialization, and task coverage. However, increasing the number of agents does not necessarily improve system performance, as communication, synchronization, redundant work, and coordination overhead may offset the benefits of additional agents. This presents a fundamental scaling challenge for agentic Web systems: how can agent populations be organized to balance task performance and coordination costs? To address this challenge, we systematically investigate the relationship between agent population size, per-agent token consumption, and coordination overhead in collaborative agentic systems. Experiments on complex Web-oriented software development tasks reveal a non-linear scaling pattern: per-agent token consumption initially decreases as the agent population grows, but eventually exhibits diminishing returns. Motivated by these findings, we introduce the Surgical Team Model (STM), a structured coordination framework that organizes agents through role specialization, constrained inter-agent communication, and coordinator-mediated task aggregation. Experiments on full-stack Web application development tasks show that STM achieves competitive task completion quality and comparable token consumption relative to representative baselines, while incurring higher execution latency.
title: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development

summary: Fixed folds, an evaluation harness, a leakage checker and per-fold uncertainty for three distinct prediction tasks over the M2OR database of olfactory receptor bioassay records: T1 new molecule — scaffold-disjoint, five repeated splits: will this receptor respond to a chemotype not in training? T2 new source — publication-disjoint: will this laboratory's screen report a positive? T3 replication — publication-disjoint, test restricted to pairs already called positive by a training source: will an independent laboratory reproduce a reported positive? The harness rebuilds pair-level consensus labels inside each fold from training sources only, runs a four-way leakage audit (pairs, molecules, scaffolds, sources) on every fold and reports it as a table, and reports each fold with a percentile bootstrap interval instead of pooling folds into a single figure. Four reference models run on every fold: random forest, L2 logistic regression and histogram gradient boosting on Morgan fingerprints with a receptor indicator, plus a receptor prior that uses no chemical information at all and predicts each receptor's positive rate in the training fold. The prior is a diagnostic, not a recommended model: a result that does not clear it has not been shown to use chemical structure. Also included: an independent re-implementation of the three headline label-reliability statistics, written without reference to the primary analysis code and using only the Python standard library for parsing; the label-composition and dose-dependence statistics; two controls on the new-source result (a study-design split and a Dawid–Skene relabelling); and the code that regenerates every figure in the accompanying paper. The M2OR release of 28 April 2023 is redistributed unmodified under the Apache License 2.0 so that the exact bytes the paper analysed remain available; see NOTICE. Please cite the database (doi:10.1093/nar/gkad886) in addition to this record.
title: M2OR-Provenance: a three-task benchmark for olfactory receptor activity prediction

summary: Federated fine-tuning enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to collaboratively adapt to distributed private data. However, long-context fine-tuning on resource-constrained devices faces substantial challenges arising from excessive activation memory, heterogeneous token-importance patterns across clients, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose SMELL, a Sparsity-aware and Memory-Efficient federated fine-tuning framework for Long-context LLMs. SMELL integrates three complementary mechanisms: Local Sparse-Forward Adaptation (LSFA), Consensus-Anchored Sparsity Coordination (CASC), and Communication-Efficient Progressive Update Recovery (CPUR). These mechanisms jointly enable memory-efficient local adaptation, heterogeneity-aware sparsity coordination, and lightweight model-update transmission. Experiments on OPT-350M and LLaMA2-7B demonstrate that SMELL reduces peak memory consumption by up to 88.35% compared with conventional fine-tuning and 13.25% compared with forward-only LoRA fine-tuning at a 16K context length. Furthermore, SMELL improves fine-tuning performance under certain non-IID settings and supports compact update transmission with progressive reconstruction, demonstrating its potential for resource-efficient federated long-context LLM adaptation.
title: SMELL: Sparsity-aware Memory Efficient Federated Fine-tuning for Long-context LLMs

summary: Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states. We propose MAS-PINN, a neural-network architecture with a tailored training algorithm for a physics-informed learning framework that leverages the network topology and the agents' similarity to reduce computational and memory costs of simulating and identifying multi-agent systems. Its architecture represents agent trajectories through shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients. Training alternates between learning features, fitting coupled trajectories, and estimating physical parameters. A matrix-free update exploits local interactions to fit trajectories without forming large global matrices. Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka--Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators show improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, including inference in large systems and identification under partial observations or unknown topology, alongside substantial computational savings in coefficient fitting.
title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning

summary: Recent advances in video generation call for reliable detection grounded in explicit forensic evidence. However, current methods primarily depend on single-pass chain-of-thought reasoning that overlooks brief or localized artifacts, or on predefined multi-agent workflows that offer limited flexibility in selecting relevant inspections. Even with adaptive investigation, optimizing the investigation policy alone does not directly improve the forensic capabilities of fixed experts. We introduce WeVisForensics, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues. The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents. Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, DTPO, closes this loop through fast reinforcement learning of the investigator and slower refinement of the inspectors, guided by annotated artifact intervals, to report subtle artifacts they once dismissed. Furthermore, we curate ForenCue-30K, combining role-specific forensic annotations and interaction trajectories to supervise individual inspections and their coordination, with an accompanying reinforcement-learning pool. Experiments show that WeVisForensics averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, while grounding its verdicts in localized evidence.
title: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection

summary: Cooperative driving extends autonomous driving from individual vehicle decisions to joint maneuvers that improve traffic safety and efficiency. Optimization-based methods impose safety constraints but often fix paths to simplify multi-vehicle planning, limiting spatial flexibility. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) explores alternatives through interaction, but coordinated learning and safe execution remain challenging. Their integration nevertheless faces challenges in exploration efficiency, experience allocation, and execution reliability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CoopDistill, an equilibrium-guided multi-agent policy distillation framework. A potential-game (PG) formulation provides a fixed-path longitudinal reference, around which a residual MARL policy learns longitudinal acceleration, conflict-approach timing, and lateral path corrections. A hard-case curriculum concentrates experience on interactions that PG leaves unresolved or substantially delayed. A comparative rollout selector evaluates the joint consequences of learned corrections against PG before choosing the executed action. Experiments in merging, roundabout, and intersection scenarios compare CoopDistill with six baselines at four connected automated vehicle penetration levels. Relative to PG, success improves by 2.1--27.1 percentage points and delay decreases by 7.3--27.3\%, with no observed collisions. Code is available at https://github.com/FanGShiYuu/CoopDistill
title: CoopDistill: Equilibrium-Guided Multi-Agent Policy Distillation for Cooperative Driving

summary: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties from measurements. We develop a comprehensive suite of property identification tasks focused on hardware mechanisms relevant to Spectre-class attacks, covering speculative execution, branch prediction, memory dependence, and cache behavior. We evaluate ProcReverser on the XuanTie C910, the gem5 RISC-V O3 CPU model, and the SiFive P550. ProcReverser achieves Pass@1 and Pass@5 scores of 81.3% and 93.8%, respectively, on C910, and 83.0% and 100.0% on gem5 O3. On the SiFive P550, ProcReverser further characterizes microarchitectural properties covered by the proposed task suite. These findings highlight the potential of automated microarchitectural reverse engineering to support processor vulnerability analysis and defense evaluation.
title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis

summary: Kohn-Sham solver for isolated atoms using the finite-element discrete variable representation (FE-DVR). Pseudo-atoms with norm-conserving pseudopotentials in UPF format, including pseudopotentials without pseudo-atomic orbitals (e.g. SG15) All-electron atoms (non-relativistic), plus approximate scalar-relativistic (Koelling-Harmon) and ZORA treatments LDA and GGA functionals: PBE built in, all others via libxc Confined atomic orbitals with polarization functions for use as localized basis functions or projectors, exported on a logarithmic grid (Quantum ESPRESSO style), on the FE-DVR grid, or as spherical Bessel transforms; dipole matrix elements Photoemission : scattering phase shifts and dipole matrix elements to continuum states 🚀 Installation $ python3 -m pip install atomic_femdvr   The built-in exchange-correlation driver provides PBE. Other functionals (e.g. the LDA used for the NIST benchmark) need the libxc Python bindings, which are not on PyPI; see the installation guide . 💪 Getting started Calculations are defined by a JSON input file. A pseudo-atom with a confinement potential and polarization orbitals ( examples/Si_Pseudo.json ): { "control" : { "storage_dir" : " ./Si_pseudo " }, "sysparams" : { "element" : " Si " , "file_upf" : " ../tests/data/Si/Si.oncvpsp.upf " , "lmax" : 2 , "nmax" : 1 }, "dft" : { "xc_functional" : " PBE " , "mixing_scheme" : " anderson " , "alpha_mix" : 0.5 }, "confinement" : { "type" : " SoftStep " , "rc" : 20.0 , "ri_factor" : 0.5 , "polarization_mode" : " SoftCoul " }, "output" : { "output_wfc_qe" : true , "output_wfc_bessel" : true } }   $ cd examples $ atomic_femdvr pseudoatomic Si_Pseudo.json -t scf,nscf out   This solves the Kohn-Sham equations self-consistently ( scf ), computes two confined radial functions each for s, p and d ( nscf ), and writes them to out/ . All energies are in Hartree and all lengths in bohr. The all-electron solver is run with atomic_femdvr atomic (see examples/Ne_full.json ). See the documentation for the input reference, the method and the output formats. ✅ Validation All-electron : LDA eigenvalues agree with the NIST atomic reference data (Ne, to 2e-6 Ha). Pseudo-atoms : eigenvalues reproduce the all-electron reference energies stored by ONCVPSP in the UPF file to about 0.5 meV (Mo, Si). The scalar-relativistic and ZORA options are approximate and have not been benchmarked. Details are in the documentation . 📖 Citation If you use atomic-femdvr in your work, please cite the archived release: M. Schüler, atomic-femdvr , Zenodo (2026), doi:10.5281/zenodo.24314160 @software { atomic_femdvr , author = { Schüler, Michael } , title = { atomic-femdvr } , year = { 2026 } , publisher = { Zenodo } , doi = { 10.5281/zenodo.24314160 } , url = { https://github.com/michaelschueler/atomic-femdvr } }   See also CITATION.cff . ⚖️ License The code is licensed under the MIT License. The test pseudopotentials in tests/data are taken from PseudoDojo (M. J. van Setten et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 226 , 39 (2018)) and distributed under CC BY 4.0; see tests/data/README.md . 👐 Contributing Contributions, whether filing an issue, making a pull request, or forking, are appreciated. See CONTRIBUTING.md for more information. Development installation $ git clone https://github.com/michaelschueler/atomic-femdvr.git $ cd atomic-femdvr $ python3 -m pip install -e . $ python3 -m pytest tests   The NIST benchmark test is skipped unless pylibxc is installed. With tox installed ( pip install tox tox-uv ), tox -e py runs the tests, tox -e lint the linter and tox -e docs builds the documentation in docs/build/html . Making a release tox -e finish removes the -dev suffix from the version, builds and uploads the package to PyPI, tags the release, and bumps the version. It needs a PyPI token in the keyring ( keyring set https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/ __token__ ). After pushing, create a release on GitHub from the new tag.
title: atomic-femdvr: Kohn-Sham solver for isolated atoms using the finite-element discrete variable representation (FE-DVR).

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24314752 . Reviewer Report: Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine Manuscript: "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems" (G. Yang; Preprints.org , doi:10.20944/preprints202603.0470.v1, posted 5 March 2026) Type of report: Point-by-point reviewer report, prepared to help the author strengthen the work before journal submission. The manuscript proposes a computational "multi-track cognition" (MTC) framework that lets data from different medical systems (traditional Chinese medicine, biomedicine, Tibetan medicine, with others said to be addable) be compared and fused without forcing one system's vocabulary onto another. The author's stated aim is to move beyond format-level standardisation towards semantic alignment, and beyond single-point linear correspondence towards system-level mapping. Importance of the research area. Integrative medicine is widely practised and increasingly supported by health policy, including the World Health Organization's strategic work on traditional and complementary medicine. A persistent barrier to generating integrated evidence is that systems describe the patient and the intervention in different conceptual languages. Examples are pattern differentiation, nature and flavour, and meridian tropism on one side, and disease categories, biomarkers and molecular targets on the other. A general and extensible way to connect these descriptions would be useful for evidence synthesis, chronic-disease management and individualised care. The author appropriately targets semantic, and not merely syntactic, interoperability, which is a question that merits careful methodological work. Approach proposed. The framework has three layers (Figure 1; Section 2): 1. Cognitive tracks (Section 2.1). Each medical system has its own track with a native feature set, normalisation rules and a native "systemic effect" index. 2. Homeostatic representation network, HRN (Section 2.2). A directed acyclic graph of 28 laboratory indicators across eight physiological systems serves as the shared anchor. Its topology comes from literature and three expert physicians. Its parameters are learned with a Bayesian network on MIMIC-III. 3. System-level mapping (Section 2.3). A random forest, guided by three rules (cluster correspondence, network emergence, context dependence), is trained with a mean-squared-error loss to predict post-intervention changes in the HRN indicators. Performance is judged by Semantic Alignment Accuracy (SAA, the share of cases in which two mapped vectors reach cosine similarity ≥ 0.85), R², MAE and RMSE (Section 2.4). Evidence reported (Section 3). Four public datasets are used (Table 1), with a 70/30 split and 5-fold cross-validation. In the TCM–Western dual-track setting the framework reports SAA 91.27% and R² 0.852, against 59.13–76.58% SAA for three baselines (Table 2). A three-system extension adding Tibetan medicine reports SAA 86.34% and R² 0.821 (Section 3.4). Agreement with three clinical experts is reported as κ = 0.86, and a Lung–Spleen Qi Deficiency case illustrates the workflow (Section 3.5). The author concludes that the framework is lossless, general, and ready to support clinical integration. Strengths. title: PREreview of "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems"

summary: Adding new parameters to the baseline distribution using the generated family concept has been one of the most commonly used techniques in recent years. The Median-based Unit Rayleigh (MBUR) is a one-parameter unit distribution. In this paper, the author added another parameter using the Topp_Loene generated family. The new approach not used previously in the literature is to use the Lomax distribution. The author truncated the Lomax distribution to obtain the unit-truncated Lomax distribution and used it as a generator to elaborate the unit-truncated Lomax-generated MBUR distribution. The derivations of the new generalized forms are discussed. The properties of both distributions, including the quantile function and raw moments, are discussed in detail.   The quantile functions can be expressed in a closed form, while the raw moments cannot be expressed in a closed form. Both distributions have bathtub-shaped, J-shaped, and increasing shape hazard rates. Real data analysis is performed to compare the fitness of both distributions.
title: Topp Leone Generated MBUR and Unit Truncated Lomax Generated MBUR Distributions: New Generalization of The MBUR Distribution

summary: Data and Stata code for a study of whether social capital predicts retained luxury imports. The outcome is imports less re-exports of four HS headings — 7113 jewellery, 9101 wristwatches with cases of precious metal, 4202 trunks, handbags and similar containers, and 3303 perfumes — scaled by population. Subtracting re-exports matters because entrepôt economies import these goods for onward shipment. The main regressor is the GSCI social capital dimension DIM_SC_30, a balanced annual series covering 247 countries. The full panel is 3,883 country-years across 184 countries, 2000–2023; the estimation sample with all controls is 3,241 country-years across 159 countries. A second, smaller panel uses the WVS/EVS Integrated Values Survey trust measure at wave level (86 country-waves, 36 OECD countries), with luxury imports averaged over a five-year window centred on each wave year. The package contains the UN Comtrade extract and the PowerShell script that produced it from the Comtrade public API, the World Bank control variables and their download script, the GSCI series, the Integrated Values Survey trust file, the Stata do-files and logs, and Figures 1–3. Code/Replication_Luxury_SocialCapital.do reproduces every table and figure in the paper. Nothing is interpolated: a country-year enters a panel only if it was observed. See README.md.
title: Social capital and retained luxury imports: replication data and Stata code for a global panel, 2000–2023

summary: We compared target-specific eight-point dose layouts for four withheld interior responses in 171 held-out Merck 4 × 4 drug-pair matrices, with (1,1) designated as the primary target. For the projection predictor, near-minus-far mean absolute error was −0.05772 at the primary target (95% pair-bootstrap interval −0.07163 to −0.04441) and −0.07085 for the four-target pair average (−0.07899 to −0.06262). Overall projection errors for near, far-plus-anchor and fixed random layouts were 0.0412, 0.1120 and 0.0773; on the same near inputs, the order-based predictors had lower average errors than the tested local interpolators, while projection showed no clear added benefit over the raw witness. A post-hoc Gaussian-process comparator showed no clear average difference from projection on the Merck near inputs, with optimizer-bound warnings in 293 of 684 fits.
title: Fixed-Budget Dose Layouts in Merck 4 × 4 Combination Matrices

summary: All 5 models trained and tuned within the outer loop of a nested cross-validation to predict differential expression under ABA treatment. Each model takes both the forward and reverse complement sequence as input. The ensemble model combines all 5 models into one averaged prediction score.
title: DeepDifE models

summary: Two independent bulk RNA-sequencing datasets were generated using a zebrafish model of Dravet syndrome at 5 days post-fertilization (dpf). Dataset 1: Disease-associated transcriptional alterations Comparison of scn1lab−/− zebrafish with wild-type controls ( scn1lab+/+ ) to identify disease-associated changes in gene expression. scn1labvWT_metadata.txt scn1labvWT_unnormalised_counts.txt Dataset 2: Drug treatment and transcriptional response An independent dataset comprising scn1lab−/− zebrafish treated with sertraline, orphenadrine, brexpiprazole, fenfluramine, or DMSO. All treatment groups were compared against wild-type controls to investigate compound-induced transcriptional changes and their potential to reverse disease-associated gene expression signatures. scn1labvWT_treatment_metadata.txt scn1labvWT_treatment_unnormalised_counts.txt Data integration and batch correction Both datasets contain unnormalized gene-level RNA-sequencing counts and corresponding sample metadata. Although generated independently, the datasets can be analyzed jointly using appropriate batch correction or statistical models that account for dataset-specific effects. This enables integrated comparisons of disease-associated and treatment-induced transcriptional changes, provided that batch effects can be distinguished from the biological conditions of interest.
title: From molecular dysfunction to therapeutic discovery: Novel targets and drug repurposing candidates for Dravet syndrome

summary: This archive supports the manuscript “Beyond benchmark gains: a diagnostic sequence for centred moving-average forecasts of reference evapotranspiration”. It contains the final manuscript files, seven processed ET0 station inputs, quality-control data, provenance records, archived station-seed metrics, analysis scripts and the model checkpoints directly reloaded by the delivered analysis. The entry point is run_analysis.ps1, which regenerates the compact analysis tables from archived outputs without retraining. The package retains only the nodecomp, fixed365 and fixed365_causal checkpoint groups. All other reported model families are represented by their archived metrics and aggregate outputs. Original NCEI, NASA POWER and Tianditu terms continue to apply to the source records. See LICENSE and DATA_LICENSE.md in the archive. Run .\run_analysis.ps1 from the extracted archive root using Windows PowerShell and the dependencies listed in requirements.txt.
title: EMS Diagnostic Sequence v1.0: reproducibility package for centred moving-average ET0 forecasts

summary: Python code accompanying the manuscript "Thermal Mode Coupling and Identifiability Limits in Photothermal Diffraction Tomography". It implements the exact Ewald accessibility test, Fourier-chain harmonic and transient solutions of the heat equation with spatially varying conductivity, the first-order rank analysis, noise-scenario detection power, the positive-source counterexample and an independent finite-volume check. All calculations are analytic or synthetic; no measured data are included. Running analysis.py and expanded_figures.py reproduces all tables and figures of the manuscript.

summary: This software record provides the source code and selected experimental artifacts associated with the research paper entitled "Blockchain-Anchored Data Continuity for Smart-City Digital Twins: A Dual-State Verification Framework." The project presents a hardware–software proof of concept for maintaining and verifying data continuity between IoT sensor records, a local hash-linked ledger, and a digital-twin-oriented dashboard. The prototype uses an ESP8266-based sensor node, a DHT11 temperature sensor, Python-based data acquisition, SQLite storage, SHA-256 record fingerprinting, and a Streamlit dashboard. The main contribution implemented in the software is a dual-state verification approach that distinguishes ledger integrity from source-record coverage. This distinction enables the detection of cases in which the ledger remains internally valid while one or more source records are not represented by corresponding ledger references. The released materials include: IoT data acquisition and database storage code. Local hash-linked ledger implementation. Source-to-ledger verification procedures. Six controlled data-tampering scenarios. Local verification performance measurement scripts. Digital Twin dashboard implementation. Solidity smart-contract and local EVM integration files. Experimental multi-replica demonstration and associated tests. The SQLite experimental database snapshot used in the study. The included baseline database contains 481 sensor records and 482 ledger blocks, including one genesis block. The verification experiments cover source-record consistency, hash-chain integrity, unique record association, and source-record coverage. The repository is intended to support inspection and reproduction of the software experiments described in the associated research paper. Results may vary depending on the execution environment, hardware, software dependencies, and database state. This release is a research proof of concept. It does not claim production-scale deployment, independent distributed consensus, sensor identity authentication, physical measurement accuracy, or full-scale urban digital-twin simulation. Author: Amirhossein Rezaeian Affiliation: University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran Email: develop.rezaeian@ut.ac.ir ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0009-4398-1703 Website: https://autorz.ir/
title: Blockchain-Anchored Data Continuity for Smart-City Digital Twins: A Dual-State Verification Framework

summary: Teaching English for Specific Purposes (ESP) at specialized sports universities presents distinct pedagogical challenges, primarily due to student-athletes' rigorous training schedules, frequent competition travel, and heterogeneous baseline language proficiency. This study investigates the pedagogical efficacy of integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven platforms and interactive digital tools into an ESP curriculum to enhance speaking fluency, domain-specific vocabulary acquisition, and learner autonomy among undergraduate sports students. A quasi-experimental study was conducted over one academic semester involving 64 second-year students divided into an experimental group ($n = 32$) and a control group ($n = 32$). While the control group received conventional textbook-based classroom instruction, the experimental group utilized AI conversational agents for simulated press conferences, automated speech recognition (ASR) tools for pronunciation feedback, and gamified digital platforms for sports terminology retention. Pre- and post-test assessments, alongside a post-intervention learner perception survey, demonstrated statistically significant improvements in the experimental group's oral proficiency, specialized lexical accuracy, and self-regulated learning engagement ($p < 0.001$). The findings indicate that AI-assisted and digital language environments offer flexible, personalized, and anxiety-reducing pathways that align effectively with the dynamic schedules and practical career needs of future sports professionals.

summary: This database has eight zip files, each containing monthly netcdfs of daily 1/24-degree (~4 km) gridded counterfactual climate data for the western US. Variables represented are daily precipitation total (prec; mm), maximum and minimum temperature (tmax and tmin, respectively; degrees C), mean vapor pressure (hPa), mean 2-m wind velocity (m/s), mean downwelling solar and longwave radiation at the surfae (solar and longwave, respectively; W/m2), and surface pressure (hPa). The counterfactual dataset is meant to represent an alternative realization of the observed climate from 1951–2025 from which anthropogenic trends in background means and daily variances about those means have been removed. The observed climate dataset is available from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19636838. Anthropogenic trends in background means and daily variances are estimatated to be represented by a weighted mean of trends simulated by 24 CMIP6 climate models under the historical (1850–2014) and SSP2-4.5 (2015–2100) scenarios. Trends in background means and daily variances are assessed relative to a baseline period of 1851–1900 (1851–1910 for daily variances). Model trends are weighted based on a combination of performance and independence following the ClimWIP method, where performace is assessed as agreement with the observed linear trend in global mean surface temperature from 1961–2025 and independence is assessed based on inter-model differences in maps of historical climatological mean surface air temperature and sea-level pressure. The methods used to produce the observational dataset, CMIP6 model weightings, and the counterfactual dataset are described in a manuscript submitted to Earth System Science Data. This dataset will be made publicly available upon publication of the corresponding paper.
title: Couterfactual version of 1/24-degree gridded daily observed climate for the western United States after removal of CMIP6 trends in background means and daily variances, 1951–2025

summary: Positioning: PubMed stores scientific papers. ScientificClaims.org stores the evolving answers to scientific questions. The Scientific Claim Registry (SCR) is infrastructure for the memory of science — not its truth, consensus, or recommendations. It registers, it does not arbitrate . What v0.5 adds over v0.4: v0.4 made every evidence link independently verified. v0.5 is the first version in which the registry has been kept current by its own Layer 1 surveillance loop (retrieve → classify → dual-model verify → promote/corroborate → recompile → version), and it reports what that took, including where it failed. Growth through the loop, not manual curation. From v0.4 to v0.5 the lipedema pilot grew from 347 to 526 evidence claims and from 423 to 626 evidence records (895 question–claim links, 383 distinct DOIs) under the same 42 versioned questions. Sources: (1) an unattended weekly rotating contradiction sweep (R-AI-12), June–September 2026, pairing each topical retrieval with a null/negative/opposing-evidence pass; (2) a library-scale backfill re-running all 42 questions against the author’s curated lipedema library (4,563 structured records) plus Europe PMC. Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified ; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note. Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise. Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict. Prior-art honesty: SCR does not invent the claim primitive or persistent claim identity — nanopublications/Trusty URIs, micropublications, Wikidata, CIViC, ClinGen, Epistemonikos/PICO, SciFact, GRADE and MAGICapp already exist. The v0.5 contribution is evidence that a question-centric, verified, versioned registry can be maintained by its own loop, with the failure modes of unattended operation documented and guarded. Operated by the BIO (Biological Intelligence Observatory) research method.
title: Scientific Claim Registry (SCR): A Versioned Memory of How Scientific Answers Evolve — Framework v0.5: Unattended Layer 1 Surveillance at Library Scale, with Documented Failure Modes

Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified ; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note. Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise. Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict. Prior-art honesty: SCR does not invent the claim primitive or persistent claim identity — nanopublications/Trusty URIs, micropublications, Wikidata, CIViC, ClinGen, Epistemonikos/PICO, SciFact, GRADE and MAGICapp already exist. The v0.5 contribution is evidence that a question-centric, verified, versioned registry can be maintained by its own loop, with the failure modes of unattended operation documented and guarded. Operated by the BIO (Biological Intelligence Observatory) research method.
title: Scientific Claim Registry (SCR): A Versioned Memory of How Scientific Answers Evolve — Framework v0.5: Unattended Layer 1 Surveillance at Library Scale, with Documented Failure Modes

summary: This deposit accompanies the study “ Balancing predictive accuracy and structural interpretability in airborne LiDAR biomass models of Mediterranean forests ”. It provides anonymised, analysis-ready forest inventory biomass responses, area-based and crown-based airborne LiDAR predictor tables, fixed outer and inner spatial cross-validation folds, R source code, allometric equation registries, selected derived tables, and a reference figure for Mediterranean forests in Castilla y León, Spain. The analysis combines PNOA-LiDAR data acquired in 2017-2019 with Fourth Spanish National Forest Inventory (IFN4) field observations from 2019. The deposited prepared data support reproduction of the nested spatial modelling, validation, and reporting stages. The archive includes an automated integrity validator, an executable workflow launcher, a column-level variable inventory, package versions, workflow documentation, and SHA-256 checksums. Raw IFN4 records, PNOA point clouds, corrected plot coordinates, original plot identifiers and the confidential identifier crosswalk are not redistributed. Scripts documenting raw-data preparation are included, but reconstruction from raw sources requires obtaining the original data from their official providers and complying with their licences. Corrected IFN4 plot coordinates and original keys have been removed. The public plot_uid is a release-specific anonymised sequential identifier. Code is provided under the MIT License. Author-created anonymised data, tables, figures and documentation are provided under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Conditions and attribution requirements of the source datasets remain applicable. PNOA attribution: Obra derivada de PNOA-LiDAR 2017-2019, CC BY 4.0, Instituto Geográfico Nacional/Centro Nacional de Información Geográfica (IGN/CNIG), Spain.

summary: This reproducibility package supports the study “Wearable Stress Models Across Sessions and Exercise Conditions: A Cross-Dataset Evaluation with Same-Session Controls.” The study developed wearable stress classification models using the WESAD dataset and externally evaluated them using the Wearable Device Dataset from Induced Stress and Structured Exercise Sessions, PhysioNet version 1.0.1. The package contains the analysis scripts, locked study protocols, Protocol Amendment v1.1, source manifests, integrity records, model settings, aggregate results, and analysis-freeze outputs used to produce the reported findings. It covers the 20-second primary analysis, the 30-second sensitivity analysis, external stress-versus-rest transport qualification, cross-session affective and exercise evaluation, same-session exercise-minus-final-rest comparisons, internally derived operating points, protocol-version checks, and self-report alignment analyses. The original WESAD and PhysioNet datasets are not included or redistributed. Users must obtain the datasets from their respective official sources and comply with their original terms of use. The package contains no newly collected participant data and no directly identifying information. The package is intended to support transparent inspection and computational reproduction of the study procedures and aggregate results. Differences in software versions, operating systems, or access to the original third-party datasets may affect exact execution details. Version v3 includes an additional audit package containing scripts and aggregate results for the original 70-feature diagnostics, participant-level and exercise-stage error analysis, and AUROC transport-gate sensitivity at 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, and 0.75. The supplement uses the existing study outputs without changing the trained models, evaluation protocol, or source datasets. Original WESAD and PhysioNet recordings are not redistributed.
title: Reproducibility Package for "Wearable Stress Models Across Sessions and Exercise Conditions: A Cross-Dataset Evaluation with Same-Session Controls"

summary: Multi-agent self-improvement enables agents to improve through interaction and feedback. However, sequential dependencies across agents and refinement rounds can propagate errors, increase computational costs, and limit parallelism. Moreover, refining individual features or agents in isolation can overlook their dependencies and restrict collective coordination. To address these challenges, we propose ConvRSI, a framework for parallelizing multi-agent self-improvement through convolution. ConvRSI couples intra-agent convolution, which jointly refines related agent features, with inter-agent graph convolution, which aggregates messages according to the collaboration topology. Both stages operate in latent space, enabling parallel updates without repeatedly decoding and re-encoding intermediate messages. Experiments on MATH-500 show that ConvRSI achieves 5.04% performance improvement while reducing 17.27% inference cost, and 45.11% latency compared with RecursiveMAS. It also supports diverse collaboration patterns by representing their topologies as adjacency matrices. These results demonstrate the potential of convolutional co-evolution for efficient multi-agent self-improvement. Our code and datasets are provided in https://github.com/LYA2333/ConvRSI.
title: From Recursion to Convolution: Parallel Self-Improvement for Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Analyzing whole-slide images (WSIs) requires combining evidence across tissue regions and spatial scales. Multi-agent systems offer a promising approach to this task. However, existing systems make limited use of molecular evidence, often select visually prominent but less representative regions while overlooking global context, and struggle to reuse experience from previous cases. To address these challenges, we present PathLoop, a self-evolving multi-agent framework that integrates omics data for evidence-grounded WSI analysis. Specifically, PathLoop coordinates visual and omics interpreters across slide, patch, and pixel levels, using molecular signals to guide region selection and combining local tissue details with global slide features. A judgment agent then checks the consistency of the collected evidence against Pathology-Wiki, a knowledge base built from 48 entries across 24 organ systems, and triggers re-examination when the evidence is inconsistent. To reuse past experience, a four-level memory stores reasoning trajectories, practical tips, skills, and tools to guide future cases, forming a loop of evidence collection, review, and memory update. We evaluate PathLoop on four TCGA cohorts with biomarker prediction, survival prediction, and subtype classification. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of PathLoop across these tasks and support its use for evidence-grounded WSI analysis.
title: PathLoop: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Reasoning for Evidence-Grounded Whole-Slide Image Analysis

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24326466 . Overall assessment: Hollmann et al. present a study that addresses an enduring mystery in the field of HIV biology: how does HIV target only two copies into the viral particle during viral assembly at the membrane? The authors use biochemistry, negative stain electron microscopy, and cryogenic electron microscopy to show the structural basis for the selection of dimeric copies of the HIV RNA genome by the immature Gag protein during assembly of the virion. This approach provides compelling biophysical evidence for the main claim that RNA packaging by HIV Gag is selective for dimeric species. The author's system for preparation of smaller, soluble Gag:RNA species will be useful for many labs. This preprint review provides comments aimed to improve readability and boost support for the main claims of the study, detailed in the major and minor points below. Major points ● The introduction discusses the role of genome dimerization and packaging. A simple infection assay demonstrating that mutation of the dimerization nucleotide tract (as in Figure 2a) abolishes infection would experimentally validate the central claim that genome dimerization is a critical component of infection. ● In the first section of the results (corresponding to Figure 1a, Figure 2a, Figure S3a), dimerization mutants are described that impact assembly. However, it is unclear whether mutant truncates the dimerization tract from 10 nucleotides to four (shortening the ruler) or if the length is maintained but the sequence swapped with GAGA repeats. Adding language to clarify the mutation made and adding discussion of these findings in the results section to explain how the results demonstrate a molecular ruler function would increase credibility. ● In Figure 3c/e/g, the six helical bundle is depicted interacting with density corresponding to RNA. However, the density maps do not show which residues or nucleotides are critical for the contact. A sentence clarifying the limitation of their cryoEM analysis and explaining how the mutations performed in the RNAse activity assay (Figure 3j/k) provide orthogonal support would increase clarity. The authors might consider conducting focused classification of the six-helical bundle and the RNA density from their existing single-particle datasets (Figure S6) to resolve the molecular details of RNA binding. Minor points: ● The authors use HIV-related and structural biology jargon extensively. While this conveys expertise, it also is a major barrier to clearly understanding the main point of the paper for readers outside specific sub-fields of HIV biology. To make the paper more accessible to an audience outside of the narrow HIV field, the authors could consider simplifying the language and using simpler, shorter sentences and fewer abbreviations. ● Figure 1a: It is difficult to interpret which nucleotides belong to which monomer of the dimer. A color-coded linear diagram or schematic of a single 5' 350 nt section of the HIV genome would allow the readers to more easily interpret the figure. ● Figure 1a: It is unclear from the diagram in Figure 1 how the dimerization signal is hypothesized to function and which elements were included in the study. Consider adding a gray box to highlight which pieces of the RNA were used in the study. ● Figure 1b-c: The color coding is a little confusing. It looks like the domains should possibly correspond to traces, but upon reading the legend, the colors in b and c are revealed to be disconnected. The authors could consider using non-overlapping color sets between the two panels. ● Figure 1c: The typical void volume for a Superdex 200 10/300 (used for the size exclusion chromatography in Figure 1c) is 8.5-9.5 mL. Includes majority-vote baselines, Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa agreement diagnostics, bootstrap confidence intervals, and panel simulators for planning and failure-mode analysis. Validated on a real five-judge panel over 400 agent trajectories where estimated judge accuracies can be checked against construction-time gold labels, including an honest account of the correlated-judge failure mode.

summary: This repository contains the replication materials supporting the manuscript "Forecasting U.S. Residential Property Prices: An Autometrics Approach with Indicator Saturation" by Shipra Aggarwal and Manish Aggarwal, submitted to Discover Analytics. The study applies Autometrics with impulse indicator saturation (IIS) and step indicator saturation (SIS) to quarterly U.S. real residential property prices (FRED series QUSR628BIS). The replication package includes archived data vintages, PcGive estimation outputs, forecasting results, Python analysis scripts, model specifications, methodological documentation, and supporting tables. The principal forecast evaluation covers 2013-Q3 to 2024-Q1, using models estimated through 2013-Q2. A separate robustness exercise uses a later data vintage and forecasts through 2026-Q1. The materials enable reproduction of the reported model estimates, forecasting accuracy measures, directional accuracy statistics, and forecast comparison tests. Data source: Bank for International Settlements (BIS), distributed through Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED), series QUSR628BIS. Associated manuscript: Forecasting U.S. Residential Property Prices: An Autometrics Approach with Indicator Saturation. Software used: OxMetrics/PcGive and Python. The README.md and METHODS.md files provide details of the replication procedure and software requirements.
