summary: This dataset contains de-identified clinical, hematological, biochemical, questionnaire, and molecular data from a prospective longitudinal study investigating biological features associated with anxiety symptoms in medical students. The study included 33 medical students, classified into an anxiety-symptom group (n = 16) and a control group (n = 17) according to the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). Clinical and biological measurements were collected at baseline and follow-up to explore changes associated with anxiety symptom severity over time. The dataset includes demographic characteristics, lifestyle-related variables, HAM-A total scores and symptom-domain assessments, hematological parameters (erythrocyte count, hemoglobin, and hematocrit), and serum cortisol concentrations. In addition, mitochondrial 7S RNA expression was evaluated by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in an exploratory subgroup of 10 participants (5 per group). The molecular dataset includes cycle threshold (Ct) values for mitochondrial 7S RNA and the reference gene RPLP0, as well as derived expression measurements calculated using the comparative 2⁻ΔΔCt method and log2 fold change transformation. The repository includes the complete clinical dataset, the RT-qPCR dataset, an Excel workbook containing the datasets, and a data dictionary describing the variables, units, and measurement methods. These data are intended to support transparency, reproducibility, and further research into the potential relationship between mitochondrial RNA regulation, neuroendocrine responses, and anxiety symptoms in the context of persistent academic stress. The findings and molecular measurements should be interpreted in light of the observational longitudinal design and the exploratory nature of the RT-qPCR subgroup analysis.
title: Mitochondrial 7S RNA Expression and Anxiety Symptoms Dataset

summary: TRANSREP — Experimental Results and Numerical Reproducibility (v1.3.0) This release provides experimental numerical data, analysis code, evaluation results, and reproducibility resources supporting the study Same Accuracy, Different Features: Checkpoint Alignment Changes Positional-Encoding Transfer Rankings in Vision Transformers . Version 1.3.0 extends the previously published v1.2.0 release with additional controlled experiments, depth- and token-resolved transfer analyses, and executable numerical verification tools. Experimental coverage Endpoint cohort E: 24 ImageNet-100 ViT-Base models across four positional-encoding configurations (Learned, Sinusoidal, 1D RoPE, and ALiBi), with six independent runs per configuration. Longitudinal cohort L: Twelve independently trained Learned and RoPE models, including upstream training trajectories, checkpoint-aligned transfer evaluations, and Oxford-IIIT Pets depth-resolved analyses. Completed-schedule cohort C: Twelve independently trained models under upstream-matched training schedules, with frozen-feature evaluations across five downstream classification tasks. Depth- and token-resolved analysis: 1,560 model-level probe scores across 13 representation depths and two token readouts (CLS and mean patch pooling). Epoch-300 evaluation: Frozen-feature readout comparisons and model-level upstream validation accuracies for twelve original endpoint models. External validation: Nine fixed public DeiT-III ImageNet-1k checkpoints comparing absolute positional embeddings with axial and mixed two-dimensional RoPE. Additional analyses: CKA representation comparisons, exploratory depth-dependent contrasts, and longitudinal late-readout comparisons. Numerical reproducibility The archive includes original numerical records, derived tables, analysis programs, and SHA-256 integrity manifests. A unified CPU-only verification procedure reproduces the supported score-level analyses, including the longitudinal and epoch-300 summaries, 65 depth-specific token-readout interaction contrasts, and 130 direct positional-encoding contrasts from archived B4-C model-level results. Verification instructions and software dependencies are provided in the root README and requirements-numerical.txt . The distribution does not include raw benchmark images, trained checkpoint weights, or large extracted feature arrays. Full model retraining and GPU feature extraction are therefore outside the scope of the portable numerical verification package. Original project-generated numerical data, figures, and associated documentation are provided under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, subject to the provenance and third-party rights detailed in LICENSES.md . summary: Compartment-Resolved Compatibility of MTA-Cooperative PRMT5 Inhibition and PDE4 Activation in MTAP-Deleted Glioblastoma A falsifiable dual-state hypothesis and translational research framework El Amin Bouchelit HISTAMOS — Independent R&D Decision Intelligence Initiative, Germany Correspondence: contact@histamos.com   |   https://histamos.com/ Abstract Background: Homozygous methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP) loss in cancer can create methylthioadenosine (MTA)-dependent vulnerability to protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) inhibition while also reshaping antitumor immunity. The relationship is not uniform across models: primary human MTAP-deleted glioblastomas (GBM) have sometimes lacked the predicted bulk MTA accumulation, plausibly because MTAP-competent stromal cells metabolize extracellular MTA. Separately, a November 2026 study found that pharmacological activation of cyclic AMP phosphodiesterase (PDE), using MR-L2 in MTAP-deficient GBM models, improved T-cell function and mouse outcomes. summary: This record contains the code, district-level data, and stored outputs needed to reproduce the tables and figures of “Who Pays for Disasters? Evidence from a Household Panel in Peru” (Víctor Cárdenas-Santiago and Roberto Guerrero Compeán, Inter-American Development Bank, 2026). The paper uses Peru’s national household survey panel (ENAHO, 2007 to 2024) to study who reports disasters, how reports relate to welfare, and how incorrect household linkage in a rotating panel can reverse the distributive answer. Self-reported exposure is contrasted with daily satellite rainfall (CHIRPS) and with administrative emergency records (INDECI). Contents: All programs (Stata and Python) that build the household unit, estimate every table, and produce every figure. District-level CHIRPS extreme-rain measures and INDECI district-year records. The stored outputs (coefficients, intervals, counts) behind each table and figure, so that every number in the paper can be checked without running the code. A README with the correspondence between tables, programs and outputs, the order of execution, software requirements, and a manifest with the MD5 checksum of every file. Household-level files (ENAHO microdata from INEI and the analytical bases derived from them) are published in a separate record with restricted access. Extracting both records into the same folder merges them into one tree, and the programs then re-estimate all results. With this public record alone, all results can be verified against the stored outputs but not recomputed. summary: Kohn-Sham solver for isolated atoms using the finite-element discrete variable representation (FE-DVR). Pseudo-atoms with norm-conserving pseudopotentials in UPF format, including pseudopotentials without pseudo-atomic orbitals (e.g. SG15) All-electron atoms (non-relativistic), plus approximate scalar-relativistic (Koelling-Harmon) and ZORA treatments LDA and GGA functionals: PBE built in, all others via libxc Confined atomic orbitals with polarization functions for use as localized basis functions or projectors, exported on a logarithmic grid (Quantum ESPRESSO style), on the FE-DVR grid, or as spherical Bessel transforms; dipole matrix elements Photoemission : scattering phase shifts and dipole matrix elements to continuum states 🚀 Installation $ python3 -m pip install atomic_femdvr   The built-in exchange-correlation driver provides PBE. Other functionals (e.g. the LDA used for the NIST benchmark) need the libxc Python bindings, which are not on PyPI; see the installation guide . 💪 Getting started Calculations are defined by a JSON input file. A pseudo-atom with a confinement potential and polarization orbitals ( examples/Si_Pseudo.json ): { "control" : { "storage_dir" : " ./Si_pseudo " }, "sysparams" : { "element" : " Si " , "file_upf" : " ../tests/data/Si/Si.oncvpsp.upf " , "lmax" : 2 , "nmax" : 1 }, "dft" : { "xc_functional" : " PBE " , "mixing_scheme" : " anderson " , "alpha_mix" : 0.5 }, "confinement" : { "type" : " SoftStep " , "rc" : 20.0 , "ri_factor" : 0.5 , "polarization_mode" : " SoftCoul " }, "output" : { "output_wfc_qe" : true , "output_wfc_bessel" : true } }   $ cd examples $ atomic_femdvr pseudoatomic Si_Pseudo.json -t scf,nscf out   This solves the Kohn-Sham equations self-consistently ( scf ), computes two confined radial functions each for s, p and d ( nscf ), and writes them to out/ . All energies are in Hartree and all lengths in bohr. The all-electron solver is run with atomic_femdvr atomic (see examples/Ne_full.json ). See the documentation for the input reference, the method and the output formats. ✅ Validation All-electron : LDA eigenvalues agree with the NIST atomic reference data (Ne, to 2e-6 Ha). Pseudo-atoms : eigenvalues reproduce the all-electron reference energies stored by ONCVPSP in the UPF file to about 0.5 meV (Mo, Si). The scalar-relativistic and ZORA options are approximate and have not been benchmarked. Details are in the documentation . 📖 Citation If you use atomic-femdvr in your work, please cite the archived release: M. Schüler, atomic-femdvr , Zenodo (2026), doi:10.5281/zenodo.24314160 @software { atomic_femdvr , author = { Schüler, Michael } , title = { atomic-femdvr } , year = { 2026 } , publisher = { Zenodo } , doi = { 10.5281/zenodo.24314160 } , url = { https://github.com/michaelschueler/atomic-femdvr } }   See also CITATION.cff . ⚖️ License The code is licensed under the MIT License. The test pseudopotentials in tests/data are taken from PseudoDojo (M. J. van Setten et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 226 , 39 (2018)) and distributed under CC BY 4.0; see tests/data/README.md . 👐 Contributing Contributions, whether filing an issue, making a pull request, or forking, are appreciated. See CONTRIBUTING.md for more information. Development installation $ git clone https://github.com/michaelschueler/atomic-femdvr.git $ cd atomic-femdvr $ python3 -m pip install -e . $ python3 -m pytest tests   The NIST benchmark test is skipped unless pylibxc is installed. With tox installed ( pip install tox tox-uv ), tox -e py runs the tests, tox -e lint the linter and tox -e docs builds the documentation in docs/build/html . Making a release tox -e finish removes the -dev suffix from the version, builds and uploads the package to PyPI, tags the release, and bumps the version. It needs a PyPI token in the keyring ( keyring set https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/ __token__ ). After pushing, create a release on GitHub from the new tag.
title: atomic-femdvr: Kohn-Sham solver for isolated atoms using the finite-element discrete variable representation (FE-DVR).

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24314752 . Reviewer Report: Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine Manuscript: "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems" (G. Yang; Preprints.org , doi:10.20944/preprints202603.0470.v1, posted 5 March 2026) Type of report: Point-by-point reviewer report, prepared to help the author strengthen the work before journal submission. The manuscript proposes a computational "multi-track cognition" (MTC) framework that lets data from different medical systems (traditional Chinese medicine, biomedicine, Tibetan medicine, with others said to be addable) be compared and fused without forcing one system's vocabulary onto another. The author's stated aim is to move beyond format-level standardisation towards semantic alignment, and beyond single-point linear correspondence towards system-level mapping. Importance of the research area. Integrative medicine is widely practised and increasingly supported by health policy, including the World Health Organization's strategic work on traditional and complementary medicine. A persistent barrier to generating integrated evidence is that systems describe the patient and the intervention in different conceptual languages. Examples are pattern differentiation, nature and flavour, and meridian tropism on one side, and disease categories, biomarkers and molecular targets on the other. A general and extensible way to connect these descriptions would be useful for evidence synthesis, chronic-disease management and individualised care. The author appropriately targets semantic, and not merely syntactic, interoperability, which is a question that merits careful methodological work. Approach proposed. The framework has three layers (Figure 1; Section 2): 1. Cognitive tracks (Section 2.1). Each medical system has its own track with a native feature set, normalisation rules and a native "systemic effect" index. 2. Homeostatic representation network, HRN (Section 2.2). A directed acyclic graph of 28 laboratory indicators across eight physiological systems serves as the shared anchor. Its topology comes from literature and three expert physicians. Its parameters are learned with a Bayesian network on MIMIC-III. 3. System-level mapping (Section 2.3). A random forest, guided by three rules (cluster correspondence, network emergence, context dependence), is trained with a mean-squared-error loss to predict post-intervention changes in the HRN indicators. Performance is judged by Semantic Alignment Accuracy (SAA, the share of cases in which two mapped vectors reach cosine similarity ≥ 0.85), R², MAE and RMSE (Section 2.4). Evidence reported (Section 3). Four public datasets are used (Table 1), with a 70/30 split and 5-fold cross-validation. In the TCM–Western dual-track setting the framework reports SAA 91.27% and R² 0.852, against 59.13–76.58% SAA for three baselines (Table 2). A three-system extension adding Tibetan medicine reports SAA 86.34% and R² 0.821 (Section 3.4). Agreement with three clinical experts is reported as κ = 0.86, and a Lung–Spleen Qi Deficiency case illustrates the workflow (Section 3.5). The author concludes that the framework is lossless, general, and ready to support clinical integration. Strengths. The following strengths provide a sound basis for revision: • The problem is timely and clinically meaningful. • The modular idea, with track-specific components and one shared core, is attractive and in principle testable. • An outcome-level physiological anchor is a practical way to compare interventions that act through different theories. • The model, loss, hyperparameters and pseudo-code are stated explicitly, which allows scrutiny. • The author attempts expert annotation, effect sizes and a multi-system extension. •
title: PREreview of "A Multi-Track Cognition Framework for Global Integrative Medicine: Breaking Paradigm Incommensurability Through System-Level Mapping Across Medical Systems"

summary: Ema Vosgerau (1,2,3) Timo Houben (1,2), Thomas Trabert (1,2), Melanie Krause (3), and Jan Bumberger (1,2,4) (1) Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research - UFZ, Research Data Management - RDM, Permoserstraße 15, 04318 Leipzig, Germany (2) Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research - UFZ, Department Monitoring and Exploration Technologies, Permoserstraße 15, 04318 Leipzig, Germany (3) Leipzig University - Faculty of Business and Economics, Grimmaische Straße 12, 04109 Leipzig, Germany (4) German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv) Halle-Jena-Leipzig, Puschstraße 4, Leipzig 04103, Germany   Dataset description:  The two datasets (dataset_1 & dataset_2) cover two different observation periods. Dataset 1 was used for model training and testing with artificially introduced data gaps. Dataset 2 served as the basis for the imputation experiment with naturally occurring data gaps. Dataset 1 contains all features considered in the feature evaluation, including air pollutant concentrations (NO₂, O₃, PM₁₀ and PM₂.₅), local meteorological variables (temperature and relative humidity), global meteorological variables (temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, wind direction, atmospheric pressure, cloud cover, precipitation and dew point), temporal and calendar features, spatial features, and sensor metadata. Dataset 2 contains only the subset of features that achieved the best model performance. Both datasets are stored in long format, sorted by sensor serial number, and include a UTC timestamp column. Feature name Feature meaning Feature group rh temp relative humidity in % temperature in °C weather_local relative_humidity temperature relative humidity in % temperature in °C weather_global precipitation pressure_msl cloud_cover dew_point precipitation in mm pressure at mean sea level in hPa cloud cover in % dew point in °C weather_addition wind_speed wind_direction wind speed inm/s wind direction in ° wind_1 wind_speed wind_sin wind_cos wind speed in m/s wind direction in sine wind direction in cosine wind_2 wind_u wind_v wind zonal in m/s wind meridional in m/s wind_3 hour_sin hour_cos dow_sin dow_cos doy_sin doy_cos is_dst hour of the day  in sine hour of the day in cosine day of the week in sine  day of the week in cosine day of the year in sine  day of the year in cosine  is daylight saving time time season weekday day_night holiday season weekday day or night holiday calendar x_km, y_km dist_km x and y in km distance to city centre in km  location district_Mitte  district_Nord  district_Nordost district_Ost district_Südwest district_West is_traffic district Mitte district Nord district Nordost  district Ost district Südwest district West  is traffic or background meta   The Excel workbook benchmark_evaluation contains eight sheets documenting the results of the feature evaluation using MSE, MAE, RMSE and R². The first sheet presents the different wind representations that were compared to identify the most informative wind encoding for the imputation task. After selecting the best-performing wind representation, the contribution of additional feature groups was evaluated through two complementary experiments. In the first, each feature group was added separately to the BASE dataset, which contained only the four target pollutants, UTC timestamps and sensor serial numbers. This assessed the contribution of each feature group in a minimal model setting. In the second, each feature group was removed separately from the FULL dataset, which contained all available predictors, including the selected wind representation. This assessed the effect of removing individual feature groups on model performance. Different masking configurations were subsequently evaluated. The tested hyperparameters included the masking ratio and masking type. Block and hybrid masking were compared using masking ratio

summary: MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE QUANTUM ENTANGLEMENT AND VOLITIONAL CORRELATION TESTS FAMILY 20  ·  F096–F100  ·  Scientific Technical Notebook v1.0 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜;讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. 33 × STARLI  |  White Rainbow Epoch Prospective · Nonclinical · Falsifiable · Recomputable. All numerical examples are synthetic. No clinical or volitional-entanglement claim is established. F096 · Physical Feasibility of Volition-Related Quantum Entanglement Hypotheses at the Limit F097 · Nonlocal Neural Correlations and Common-Cause Exclusion at the Limit F098 · Entanglement Witnesses and Identifiability in Neural Measurements at the Limit F099 · Distant Volitional Synchrony Claims and Information-Leakage Blinding at the Limit F100 · Quantum Entanglement Versus Classical Correlation in Volitional Research at the Limit     Scientific position and cultural inheritance Five evidence identities F096 asks whether a specified physical joint state and measurement path are even feasible. F097 compares neural associations against common-cause alternatives. F098 requires a physically defined witness; F099 investigates concealed-target identification; F100 tests classical predictive residuals. These outputs have different units and logical meanings. A likelihood ratio does not have the interpretation of an operator expectation or an accuracy contrast. A negative result at one necessary link cannot be paid for by a high score elsewhere. The family is integrated by traceable interfaces, not by a civilization index. Entanglement is a property of specified subsystems A nonseparable density operator is not defined by a narrative about connectedness. The tensor partition, physical preparation and observation operators establish the question. Classical mixtures can produce striking correlations. Begin with reference qubits in a controlled bench or simulation; verify independent preparation and record losses, phase, basis, source identity and uncertainty. Do not extrapolate a verified laboratory entangled state to neural tissue without an independently validated transduction and state model. Bell tests and the locality boundary The CHSH inequality constrains a class of local hidden-variable models under specified assumptions. Hensen and colleagues used independently controlled electron spins in diamond; this is not a demonstration in human brains. The experiment must specify the settings, admissible trials, event ordering and outcome distribution. Analyze the actual four setting-conditioned correlations, not an ordinary Pearson coefficient from two EEG traces. Even a valid Bell violation does not provide controllable faster-than-light signalling. Ordinary correlation deserves the strongest defense A shared environment, clock, stimulus schedule or physiological rhythm can create cross-site association. F097 makes this ordinary explanation a serious predictive model rather than a weak nuisance adjustment. Measure independent reference channels, precommit preprocessing, retain dyad-level units and fit common-driver alternatives on training records only. A residual unexplained by measured covariates is uncertainty, not a unique indication of nonlocal causation. An operator is not a metaphor F098 starts from a concrete witness, such as the Bell-projector witness W=I/2-P. Negative expectation certifies entanglement for a trusted two-qubit measurement with established assumptions. The blueprint leaves the witness units unspecified. summary: Positioning: PubMed stores scientific papers. ScientificClaims.org stores the evolving answers to scientific questions. The Scientific Claim Registry (SCR) is infrastructure for the memory of science — not its truth, consensus, or recommendations. It registers, it does not arbitrate . What v0.5 adds over v0.4: v0.4 made every evidence link independently verified. v0.5 is the first version in which the registry has been kept current by its own Layer 1 surveillance loop (retrieve → classify → dual-model verify → promote/corroborate → recompile → version), and it reports what that took, including where it failed. Growth through the loop, not manual curation. From v0.4 to v0.5 the lipedema pilot grew from 347 to 526 evidence claims and from 423 to 626 evidence records (895 question–claim links, 383 distinct DOIs) under the same 42 versioned questions. Sources: (1) an unattended weekly rotating contradiction sweep (R-AI-12), June–September 2026, pairing each topical retrieval with a null/negative/opposing-evidence pass; (2) a library-scale backfill re-running all 42 questions against the author’s curated lipedema library (4,563 structured records) plus Europe PMC. Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified ; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note. Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise. Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict. Prior-art honesty: SCR does not invent the claim primitive or persistent claim identity — nanopublications/Trusty URIs, micropublications, Wikidata, CIViC, ClinGen, Epistemonikos/PICO, SciFact, GRADE and MAGICapp already exist. The v0.5 contribution is evidence that a question-centric, verified, versioned registry can be maintained by its own loop, with the failure modes of unattended operation documented and guarded. Operated by the BIO (Biological Intelligence Observatory) research method.
title: Scientific Claim Registry (SCR): A Versioned Memory of How Scientific Answers Evolve — Framework v0.5: Unattended Layer 1 Surveillance at Library Scale, with Documented Failure Modes

summary: Analyzing whole-slide images (WSIs) requires combining evidence across tissue regions and spatial scales. Multi-agent systems offer a promising approach to this task. However, existing systems make limited use of molecular evidence, often select visually prominent but less representative regions while overlooking global context, and struggle to reuse experience from previous cases. To address these challenges, we present PathLoop, a self-evolving multi-agent framework that integrates omics data for evidence-grounded WSI analysis. Specifically, PathLoop coordinates visual and omics interpreters across slide, patch, and pixel levels, using molecular signals to guide region selection and combining local tissue details with global slide features. A judgment agent then checks the consistency of the collected evidence against Pathology-Wiki, a knowledge base built from 48 entries across 24 organ systems, and triggers re-examination when the evidence is inconsistent. To reuse past experience, a four-level memory stores reasoning trajectories, practical tips, skills, and tools to guide future cases, forming a loop of evidence collection, review, and memory update. We evaluate PathLoop on four TCGA cohorts with biomarker prediction, survival prediction, and subtype classification. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of PathLoop across these tasks and support its use for evidence-grounded WSI analysis.
title: PathLoop: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Reasoning for Evidence-Grounded Whole-Slide Image Analysis

summary: TRANSREP — Experimental Results and Numerical Reproducibility (v1.3.0) This release provides experimental numerical data, analysis code, evaluation results, and reproducibility resources supporting the study Same Accuracy, Different Features: Checkpoint Alignment Changes Positional-Encoding Transfer Rankings in Vision Transformers . Version 1.3.0 extends the previously published v1.2.0 release with additional controlled experiments, depth- and token-resolved transfer analyses, and executable numerical verification tools. Experimental coverage Endpoint cohort E: 24 ImageNet-100 ViT-Base models across four positional-encoding configurations (Learned, Sinusoidal, 1D RoPE, and ALiBi), with six independent runs per configuration. Longitudinal cohort L: Twelve independently trained Learned and RoPE models, including upstream training trajectories, checkpoint-aligned transfer evaluations, and Oxford-IIIT Pets depth-resolved analyses. Completed-schedule cohort C: Twelve independently trained models under upstream-matched training schedules, with frozen-feature evaluations across five downstream classification tasks. Depth- and token-resolved analysis: 1,560 model-level probe scores across 13 representation depths and two token readouts (CLS and mean patch pooling). Epoch-300 evaluation: Frozen-feature readout comparisons and model-level upstream validation accuracies for twelve original endpoint models. External validation: Nine fixed public DeiT-III ImageNet-1k checkpoints comparing absolute positional embeddings with axial and mixed two-dimensional RoPE. Additional analyses: CKA representation comparisons, exploratory depth-dependent contrasts, and longitudinal late-readout comparisons. Numerical reproducibility The archive includes original numerical records, derived tables, analysis programs, and SHA-256 integrity manifests. A unified CPU-only verification procedure reproduces the supported score-level analyses, including the longitudinal and epoch-300 summaries, 65 depth-specific token-readout interaction contrasts, and 130 direct positional-encoding contrasts from archived B4-C model-level results. Verification instructions and software dependencies are provided in the root README and requirements-numerical.txt . The distribution does not include raw benchmark images, trained checkpoint weights, or large extracted feature arrays. Full model retraining and GPU feature extraction are therefore outside the scope of the portable numerical verification package. Original project-generated numerical data, figures, and associated documentation are provided under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, subject to the provenance and third-party rights detailed in LICENSES.md . summary: Autonomous agents often reason and coordinate through labels that do not reveal which external information they denote. We present Sema, a content-addressed reference system for reasoning and communication that creates hash-based verifiable words: participants encode and hash information under an agreed representation, then reuse the content address as a term, optionally with a human-readable handle. Sema can use any representation if participants agree on how content is encoded, hashed, resolved, and decoded. This paper develops one concrete realization based on canonicalized JSON-compatible objects, field-level Merkle commitments, explicit identity rules, and content-addressed references. Full-reference verification establishes identity of the resolved hashed content, while semantic equivalence, correctness, and compliance remain separate questions. As a worked application of the Sema primitive, we introduce Pattern Cards, a concrete schema for deliberate, System 2-style reasoning. They make often-skipped reasoning moves explicit through contracts for mechanisms, conditions, invariants, typed dependencies, and failure modes. Within one agent, resolving a card can make a reusable reasoning procedure explicit. Across agents, the same content-addressed definitions support coordination: agents can verify that they resolved the same definitions; in strict mode, an enforced handshake halts on mismatch. A bootstrap library of more than six hundred cards demonstrates the design. Its contract fields averaged 26.7 times the tokens of short wire references—a transmission-compression result, not an inference-token saving, because definitions were hydrated before use. Illustrative agent demonstrations examine coordination behavior. The same primitive could support a Living Taxonomy of Thought; its utility, evolution, and governance remain open questions.
title: Sema: When the Hash Is the Word

summary: These are audio recordings taken by an Eclipse Soundscapes (ES) Data Collector during the week of the April 08, 2024 Total Solar Eclipse.  It was decided to include only raw, unprocessed audio data files in each site-specific Zenodo record. This decision was so that any researcher can independently verify, reproduce, and extend the analysis performed. As a result, some sites have WAV files with 0 bytes of data or timestamps outside the range of probable recording times. Procedures used by the Eclipse Soundscapes team to process audio data for its purposes are outlined in the Data Management reports located in the Eclipse Soundscapes Zenodo community. Data with 0 bytes of data were included for completeness. When possible, all site-specific files, including the audio files, are included in a single zip file for ease of download. If a single zip file upload was not possible due to upload or bandwidth limitations, audio files are included in multiple zip files based on the day of the observation. summary: Standard nanoindentation analysis suppresses the time-dependent response of a tested material, discarding the property that governs how a heritage paint film survives climatic loading: its viscoplastic dissipation potential. We recover it, together with the elastic modulus, from a single displacement-controlled relaxation indent by Bayesian inverse identification through a Gaussian-process surrogate of a finite-element contact model. The central difficulty is that the constitutive law is adequate during relaxation but structurally violated during loading, where the particulate film deforms by granular compaction. Overweighting the loading forces the optimiser to absorb this model-form discrepancy into the constitutive parameters, leaving a deceptively good global fit. We expose this failure mode through a three-way audit of weighting schemes: expert-encoded physics, Fisher-information optimality, and a data-driven Empirical Bayes filter. Information-optimal weighting under model-form error produces the most biased parameters with an equally tight posterior, an effect we term Constitutive Overfitting. A polycarbonate control, for which the model is uniformly adequate, confirms that the three schemes converge, establishing the audit as a diagnostic of model inadequacy rather than a pipeline artefact. This work has two outcomes. The first is the complete viscoplastic dissipation potential of a heritage paint film, the rate-dependent descriptor that fracture and digital-twin models require, from a single high-information indent. The second is the audit: an unaudited inversion would report a tight posterior on a biased modulus, whereas the three-way comparison separates reliable parameters from artefacts wherever constitutive fidelity varies within a single experiment. Population-level variability is deferred to a forthcoming multi-indent study.

summary: We Are Here : a Resource-Ratio Alternative to Energy-Based Civilizational Scales   A Discussion Paper Alexandre Costa Coelho, M.Sc. [1] M.Sc., Massachusetts Institute of Technology, MIT Sloan Fellow '07 December 11, 2026 - DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24202174   Keywords: Fermi Paradox, Kardashev scale, SETI, STRATA gradients, civilizational advancement Abstract Civilizations have been ranked by how much energy they burn. That habit bundles together two questions that should never have shared one variable. What to measure, in order to find a civilization at all, and by what means. And how advanced it is, once found. Dyson raised the first in 1960. A star-enclosing energy collector radiates detectable waste heat. Kardashev, four years later, defined his civilization types by energy, inside an analysis of how much power a transmitter would need to be heard across interstellar distances. Dyson's sphere was his example of a Type II civilization. The scale grew out of a detection question and was then used as a ranking of how advanced a civilization is. The two roles were never separated, and we argue they should be. Call it the Two Stones, Two Birds Problem. One stone, energy, thrown at two birds that were never in the same tree. This paper throws both stones, one at a time. For ranking, we propose a Resource Utilization Ratio, which scores consumption against need and the ecological cost of energy, and we combine it with two defined but unmeasured dimensions, a behavioral capacity and an empathic one, in a Civilizational Advancement Index (CAI). The illustrative Earth baseline of about 13% depends on the author's hypothetical values for those two dimensions. We also propose STRATA I, II and III, bands of the CAI, as a ranking alternative to Kardashev's Types I, II and III, and the two sets of names do not mean the same thing. For detection, we propose Tunelength (TnL), a speculative signal drawn from brain-interface engineering and a peer-reviewed, if contested, theory of consciousness. Prospective · Nonclinical · Falsifiable · Recomputable. This notebook contains research plans and synthetic calculations, not empirical results. No clinical intervention is proposed.     A twin is a question, not a second body A traditional practice can be described through breathing, movement, rhythm, attention and accumulated experience, but the description is not the person. Qigong and Xianggong invite an integrative inquiry into observable trajectories rather than a presumption that an invisible mechanism has been found. A computational twin deliberately reduces a rich human activity to selected state variables. The reduction is a scientific commitment: specify what is observed and what remains latent. A respiratory belt is not lung volume; a predicted joint angle is not an observed neural state; agreement between sensors is not independent calibration. The model must state the domain over which its abstraction can be tested. The family is prospective and nonclinical. All calculated figures are deterministic synthetic examples, and all described tests are proposals. No participant data, clinical validation, extraordinary causal effect or therapeutic efficacy is claimed. Preserve an explicit path to the null. The philosophy of restraint Wuwei, understood here as an invitation to avoid unnecessary intervention, offers a design question rather than a physical theory. A twin ought to be able to refuse an unsupported prediction instead of producing a pleasing answer at every query. A practitioner may choose rest or decline measurement without that choice becoming an optimization failure. Eastern philosophical vocabulary can name relations and guide inquiry, but it cannot supply a missing calibration coefficient or establish quantum coherence. Breath and intention require distinct operational definitions. The possibility of no identifiable effect remains as important as the possibility of a meaningful mechanism. Create separation between measurement, inference, recommendation and authorized action. This family does not authorize changes to a person's practice based on a simulated response surface. Every claim to improve future prediction has a comparator and an independent witness. Identifiability before accuracy Different parameters can produce the same output. A model may forecast beautifully and still be unable to explain which parameter is responsible for the behavior. The respiratory-motion branch therefore distinguishes structural ambiguity from uncertainty caused by limited noisy data. Raue et al. (2009), Structural and practical identifiability analysis of partially observed dynamical models by exploiting the profile likelihood, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp358, provides the method of interrogating parameter identifiability through profile likelihood. It is a methodological reference, not evidence about a particular Qigong mechanism. Fit on coded synthetic excitations and evaluate on new input shapes. Make likelihood ridges visible and compare a reference-equipped model with a belt-only fit. Preserve compatible parameter sets when the data do not support unique values. A prediction is a distribution Xianggong motor trajectories invite models of rhythm and joint motion, but a smooth predicted angle may conceal a plausible alternative future. A useful neuromotor twin carries conditional uncertainty, coordinate conventions and an exact information cutoff. A forecast of joint geometry cannot by itself identify a neural source. Compare held-out angles in degrees, report empirical interval coverage and avo

summary: MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE MIND–BODY DIGITAL TWINS AND NONCLINICAL VALIDATION FAMILY 32  /  F156–F160 SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK  /  33 × STARLI 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜;讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. Prospective · Nonclinical · Falsifiable · Recomputable. This notebook contains research plans and synthetic calculations, not empirical results. No clinical intervention is proposed.     A twin is a question, not a second body A traditional practice can be described through breathing, movement, rhythm, attention and accumulated experience, but the description is not the person. Qigong and Xianggong invite an integrative inquiry into observable trajectories rather than a presumption that an invisible mechanism has been found. A computational twin deliberately reduces a rich human activity to selected state variables. The reduction is a scientific commitment: specify what is observed and what remains latent. A respiratory belt is not lung volume; a predicted joint angle is not an observed neural state; agreement between sensors is not independent calibration. The model must state the domain over which its abstraction can be tested. The family is prospective and nonclinical. All calculated figures are deterministic synthetic examples, and all described tests are proposals. No participant data, clinical validation, extraordinary causal effect or therapeutic efficacy is claimed. Preserve an explicit path to the null. The philosophy of restraint Wuwei, understood here as an invitation to avoid unnecessary intervention, offers a design question rather than a physical theory. A twin ought to be able to refuse an unsupported prediction instead of producing a pleasing answer at every query. A practitioner may choose rest or decline measurement without that choice becoming an optimization failure. Eastern philosophical vocabulary can name relations and guide inquiry, but it cannot supply a missing calibration coefficient or establish quantum coherence. Breath and intention require distinct operational definitions. The possibility of no identifiable effect remains as important as the possibility of a meaningful mechanism. Create separation between measurement, inference, recommendation and authorized action. This family does not authorize changes to a person's practice based on a simulated response surface. Every claim to improve future prediction has a comparator and an independent witness. Identifiability before accuracy Different parameters can produce the same output. A model may forecast beautifully and still be unable to explain which parameter is responsible for the behavior. The respiratory-motion branch therefore distinguishes structural ambiguity from uncertainty caused by limited noisy data. Raue et al. (2009), Structural and practical identifiability analysis of partially observed dynamical models by exploiting the profile likelihood, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp358, provides the method of interrogating parameter identifiability through profile likelihood. It is a methodological reference, not evidence about a particular Qigong mechanism. Fit on coded synthetic excitations and evaluate on new input shapes. Make likelihood ridges visible and compare a reference-equipped model with a belt-only fit. Preserve compatible parameter sets when the data do not support unique values. A prediction is a distribution Xianggong motor trajectories invite models of rhythm and joint motion, but a smooth predicted angle may conceal a plausible alternative future. A useful neuromotor twin carries conditional uncertainty, coordinate conventions and an exact information cutoff. A forecast of joint geometry cannot by itself identify a neural source. Compare held-out angles in degrees, report empirical interval coverage and avo

summary: MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE MIND–BODY DIGITAL TWINS AND NONCLINICAL VALIDATION FAMILY 32  /  F156–F160 SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK  /  33 × STARLI 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜;讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. Prospective · Nonclinical · Falsifiable · Recomputable. This notebook contains research plans and synthetic calculations, not empirical results. No clinical intervention is proposed.     A twin is a question, not a second body A traditional practice can be described through breathing, movement, rhythm, attention and accumulated experience, but the description is not the person. Qigong and Xianggong invite an integrative inquiry into observable trajectories rather than a presumption that an invisible mechanism has been found. A computational twin deliberately reduces a rich human activity to selected state variables. The reduction is a scientific commitment: specify what is observed and what remains latent. A respiratory belt is not lung volume; a predicted joint angle is not an observed neural state; agreement between sensors is not independent calibration. The model must state the domain over which its abstraction can be tested. The family is prospective and nonclinical. All calculated figures are deterministic synthetic examples, and all described tests are proposals. No participant data, clinical validation, extraordinary causal effect or therapeutic efficacy is claimed. Preserve an explicit path to the null. The philosophy of restraint Wuwei, understood here as an invitation to avoid unnecessary intervention, offers a design question rather than a physical theory. A twin ought to be able to refuse an unsupported prediction instead of producing a pleasing answer at every query. A practitioner may choose rest or decline measurement without that choice becoming an optimization failure. Eastern philosophical vocabulary can name relations and guide inquiry, but it cannot supply a missing calibration coefficient or establish quantum coherence. Breath and intention require distinct operational definitions. The possibility of no identifiable effect remains as important as the possibility of a meaningful mechanism. Create separation between measurement, inference, recommendation and authorized action. This family does not authorize changes to a person's practice based on a simulated response surface. Every claim to improve future prediction has a comparator and an independent witness. Identifiability before accuracy Different parameters can produce the same output. A model may forecast beautifully and still be unable to explain which parameter is responsible for the behavior. The respiratory-motion branch therefore distinguishes structural ambiguity from uncertainty caused by limited noisy data. Raue et al. (2009), Structural and practical identifiability analysis of partially observed dynamical models by exploiting the profile likelihood, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp358, provides the method of interrogating parameter identifiability through profile likelihood. It is a methodological reference, not evidence about a particular Qigong mechanism. Fit on coded synthetic excitations and evaluate on new input shapes. Make likelihood ridges visible and compare a reference-equipped model with a belt-only fit. Preserve compatible parameter sets when the data do not support unique values. A prediction is a distribution Xianggong motor trajectories invite models of rhythm and joint motion, but a smooth predicted angle may conceal a plausible alternative future. A useful neuromotor twin carries conditional uncertainty, coordinate conventions and an exact information cutoff. A forecast of joint geometry cannot by itself identify a neural source. Compare held-out angles in degrees, report empirical interval coverage and avo

summary: MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE MIND–BODY DIGITAL TWINS AND NONCLINICAL VALIDATION FAMILY 32  /  F156–F160 SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK  /  33 × STARLI 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜;讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. Prospective · Nonclinical · Falsifiable · Recomputable. This notebook contains research plans and synthetic calculations, not empirical results. No clinical intervention is proposed.     A twin is a question, not a second body A traditional practice can be described through breathing, movement, rhythm, attention and accumulated experience, but the description is not the person. Qigong and Xianggong invite an integrative inquiry into observable trajectories rather than a presumption that an invisible mechanism has been found. A computational twin deliberately reduces a rich human activity to selected state variables. The reduction is a scientific commitment: specify what is observed and what remains latent. A respiratory belt is not lung volume; a predicted joint angle is not an observed neural state; agreement between sensors is not independent calibration. The model must state the domain over which its abstraction can be tested. The family is prospective and nonclinical. All calculated figures are deterministic synthetic examples, and all described tests are proposals. No participant data, clinical validation, extraordinary causal effect or therapeutic efficacy is claimed. Preserve an explicit path to the null. The philosophy of restraint Wuwei, understood here as an invitation to avoid unnecessary intervention, offers a design question rather than a physical theory. A twin ought to be able to refuse an unsupported prediction instead of producing a pleasing answer at every query. A practitioner may choose rest or decline measurement without that choice becoming an optimization failure. Eastern philosophical vocabulary can name relations and guide inquiry, but it cannot supply a missing calibration coefficient or establish quantum coherence. Breath and intention require distinct operational definitions. The possibility of no identifiable effect remains as important as the possibility of a meaningful mechanism. Create separation between measurement, inference, recommendation and authorized action. This family does not authorize changes to a person's practice based on a simulated response surface. Every claim to improve future prediction has a comparator and an independent witness. Identifiability before accuracy Different parameters can produce the same output. A model may forecast beautifully and still be unable to explain which parameter is responsible for the behavior. The respiratory-motion branch therefore distinguishes structural ambiguity from uncertainty caused by limited noisy data. Raue et al. (2009), Structural and practical identifiability analysis of partially observed dynamical models by exploiting the profile likelihood, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp358, provides the method of interrogating parameter identifiability through profile likelihood. It is a methodological reference, not evidence about a particular Qigong mechanism. Fit on coded synthetic excitations and evaluate on new input shapes. Make likelihood ridges visible and compare a reference-equipped model with a belt-only fit. Preserve compatible parameter sets when the data do not support unique values. A prediction is a distribution Xianggong motor trajectories invite models of rhythm and joint motion, but a smooth predicted angle may conceal a plausible alternative future. A useful neuromotor twin carries conditional uncertainty, coordinate conventions and an exact information cutoff. A forecast of joint geometry cannot by itself identify a neural source. Compare held-out angles in degrees, report empirical interval coverage and avo

summary: MYSTERIOUS EASTERN CULTURE MIND–BODY DIGITAL TWINS AND NONCLINICAL VALIDATION FAMILY 32  /  F156–F160 SCIENTIFIC TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK  /  33 × STARLI 讓古老的謎題保有詩意,讓未來的科學保有謙遜;讓每一個尚未解開的問題,都有機會成為下一個文明的起點。 Let ancient mysteries retain their poetry, and future science its humility; let every unanswered question become a possible beginning for the next civilization. Prospective · Nonclinical · Falsifiable · Recomputable. This notebook contains research plans and synthetic calculations, not empirical results. No clinical intervention is proposed.     A twin is a question, not a second body A traditional practice can be described through breathing, movement, rhythm, attention and accumulated experience, but the description is not the person. Qigong and Xianggong invite an integrative inquiry into observable trajectories rather than a presumption that an invisible mechanism has been found. A computational twin deliberately reduces a rich human activity to selected state variables. The reduction is a scientific commitment: specify what is observed and what remains latent. A respiratory belt is not lung volume; a predicted joint angle is not an observed neural state; agreement between sensors is not independent calibration. The model must state the domain over which its abstraction can be tested. The family is prospective and nonclinical. All calculated figures are deterministic synthetic examples, and all described tests are proposals. No participant data, clinical validation, extraordinary causal effect or therapeutic efficacy is claimed. Preserve an explicit path to the null. The philosophy of restraint Wuwei, understood here as an invitation to avoid unnecessary intervention, offers a design question rather than a physical theory. A twin ought to be able to refuse an unsupported prediction instead of producing a pleasing answer at every query. A practitioner may choose rest or decline measurement without that choice becoming an optimization failure. Eastern philosophical vocabulary can name relations and guide inquiry, but it cannot supply a missing calibration coefficient or establish quantum coherence. Breath and intention require distinct operational definitions. The possibility of no identifiable effect remains as important as the possibility of a meaningful mechanism. Create separation between measurement, inference, recommendation and authorized action. This family does not authorize changes to a person's practice based on a simulated response surface. Every claim to improve future prediction has a comparator and an independent witness. Identifiability before accuracy Different parameters can produce the same output. A model may forecast beautifully and still be unable to explain which parameter is responsible for the behavior. The respiratory-motion branch therefore distinguishes structural ambiguity from uncertainty caused by limited noisy data. Raue et al. (2009), Structural and practical identifiability analysis of partially observed dynamical models by exploiting the profile likelihood, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp358, provides the method of interrogating parameter identifiability through profile likelihood. It is a methodological reference, not evidence about a particular Qigong mechanism. Fit on coded synthetic excitations and evaluate on new input shapes. Make likelihood ridges visible and compare a reference-equipped model with a belt-only fit. Preserve compatible parameter sets when the data do not support unique values. A prediction is a distribution Xianggong motor trajectories invite models of rhythm and joint motion, but a smooth predicted angle may conceal a plausible alternative future. A useful neuromotor twin carries conditional uncertainty, coordinate conventions and an exact information cutoff. A forecast of joint geometry cannot by itself identify a neural source. Compare held-out angles in degrees, report empirical interval coverage and avo

summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π (x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Version 1.0. The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof and claims this approach as his own; the missing step is named.     Работа продолжает геометрическую модель распределения простых чисел [2] и работу «Числовая стрела и прямая 1/2» [1]. Геометрическая формула числа нечётных составных до p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, рассматривается как первый уровень лестницы, в которой масштаб на каждой ступени возводится в квадрат: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. Показано, что эта формула — наилучшая квадратичная формула уровня до 5⁴: она точна везде, кроме одной компенсирующей пары промахов (p = 15 и p = 17). Квадратичная решётка уровня держится до базиса 7 включительно и разрушается сразу после него. Ошибка формулы раскладывается на две наложенные таблицы: плавную поправку уровня и колебание, которое в явной формуле есть сумма косинусов по нулям дзета-функции. Главный результат — закон уровней, проверенный на точных значениях π(x) до 3³² ≈ 1,9 · 10¹⁵: при возведении масштаба в квадрат относительная ошибка счёта простых возводится в квадрат, а сама ошибка обратна линейной шкале p = √x, получаемой из разности квадратов: ε · p остаётся порядка единицы на всех проверенных ступенях.

summary: Positioning: PubMed stores scientific papers. ScientificClaims.org stores the evolving answers to scientific questions. The Scientific Claim Registry (SCR) is infrastructure for the memory of science — not its truth, consensus, or recommendations. It registers, it does not arbitrate . What v0.5 adds over v0.4: v0.4 made every evidence link independently verified. v0.5 is the first version in which the registry has been kept current by its own Layer 1 surveillance loop (retrieve → classify → dual-model verify → promote/corroborate → recompile → version), and it reports what that took, including where it failed. Growth through the loop, not manual curation. From v0.4 to v0.5 the lipedema pilot grew from 347 to 526 evidence claims and from 423 to 626 evidence records (895 question–claim links, 383 distinct DOIs) under the same 42 versioned questions. Sources: (1) an unattended weekly rotating contradiction sweep (R-AI-12), June–September 2026, pairing each topical retrieval with a null/negative/opposing-evidence pass; (2) a library-scale backfill re-running all 42 questions against the author’s curated lipedema library (4,563 structured records) plus Europe PMC. Verification across the registry: 614 verified, 5 disputed (kept and flagged), 7 unverified ; 19 records contradict the claim they sit under. Each changed answer received a new immutable version with a “what changed” note. Operational honesty. Unattended operation exposed failures a demo never shows, documented with the guarantees added: (a) eight silent weeks in which a missing LLM credential made every run fail while the rotation still advanced and logged the questions as swept — the rotation now advances only on successful runs, and a missing credential is a loud warning; (b) silently degraded semantic retrieval, now with keyword fallback and a self-started library service; (c) a malformed model response that discarded a whole run (atomic writes kept the registry intact), now parsed leniently on retry. A memory system that hides its own gaps contradicts its premise. Object model (unchanged). The scientific question (e.g. SQ-LIP-000007) is the primary navigable object. Underneath it, claims (SCR-LIP-000001) are structured, versioned units of evidence with an explicit role (supporting / contradicting / refines / context), PECO context, a GRADE rating, dated provenance, a change log, sentence-level provenance and an independent verification verdict. Prior-art honesty: SCR does not invent the claim primitive or persistent claim identity — nanopublications/Trusty URIs, micropublications, Wikidata, CIViC, ClinGen, Epistemonikos/PICO, SciFact, GRADE and MAGICapp already exist. The v0.5 contribution is evidence that a question-centric, verified, versioned registry can be maintained by its own loop, with the failure modes of unattended operation documented and guarded. Operated by the BIO (Biological Intelligence Observatory) research method.
title: Scientific Claim Registry (SCR): A Versioned Memory of How Scientific Answers Evolve — Framework v0.5: Unattended Layer 1 Surveillance at Library Scale, with Documented Failure Modes

summary: This dataset contains de-identified clinical, hematological, biochemical, questionnaire, and molecular data from a prospective longitudinal study investigating biological features associated with anxiety symptoms in medical students. The study included 33 medical students, classified into an anxiety-symptom group (n = 16) and a control group (n = 17) according to the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A). Clinical and biological measurements were collected at baseline and follow-up to explore changes associated with anxiety symptom severity over time. The dataset includes demographic characteristics, lifestyle-related variables, HAM-A total scores and symptom-domain assessments, hematological parameters (erythrocyte count, hemoglobin, and hematocrit), and serum cortisol concentrations. In addition, mitochondrial 7S RNA expression was evaluated by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in an exploratory subgroup of 10 participants (5 per group). The molecular dataset includes cycle threshold (Ct) values for mitochondrial 7S RNA and the reference gene RPLP0, as well as derived expression measurements calculated using the comparative 2⁻ΔΔCt method and log2 fold change transformation. The repository includes the complete clinical dataset, the RT-qPCR dataset, an Excel workbook containing the datasets, and a data dictionary describing the variables, units, and measurement methods. These data are intended to support transparency, reproducibility, and further research into the potential relationship between mitochondrial RNA regulation, neuroendocrine responses, and anxiety symptoms in the context of persistent academic stress. The findings and molecular measurements should be interpreted in light of the observational longitudinal design and the exploratory nature of the RT-qPCR subgroup analysis.
title: Mitochondrial 7S RNA Expression and Anxiety Symptoms Dataset

summary: TRANSREP — Experimental Results and Numerical Reproducibility (v1.3.0) This release provides experimental numerical data, analysis code, evaluation results, and reproducibility resources supporting the study Same Accuracy, Different Features: Checkpoint Alignment Changes Positional-Encoding Transfer Rankings in Vision Transformers . Version 1.3.0 extends the previously published v1.2.0 release with additional controlled experiments, depth- and token-resolved transfer analyses, and executable numerical verification tools. Experimental coverage Endpoint cohort E: 24 ImageNet-100 ViT-Base models across four positional-encoding configurations (Learned, Sinusoidal, 1D RoPE, and ALiBi), with six independent runs per configuration. Longitudinal cohort L: Twelve independently trained Learned and RoPE models, including upstream training trajectories, checkpoint-aligned transfer evaluations, and Oxford-IIIT Pets depth-resolved analyses. Completed-schedule cohort C: Twelve independently trained models under upstream-matched training schedules, with frozen-feature evaluations across five downstream classification tasks. Depth- and token-resolved analysis: 1,560 model-level probe scores across 13 representation depths and two token readouts (CLS and mean patch pooling). Epoch-300 evaluation: Frozen-feature readout comparisons and model-level upstream validation accuracies for twelve original endpoint models. External validation: Nine fixed public DeiT-III ImageNet-1k checkpoints comparing absolute positional embeddings with axial and mixed two-dimensional RoPE. Additional analyses: CKA representation comparisons, exploratory depth-dependent contrasts, and longitudinal late-readout comparisons. Numerical reproducibility The archive includes original numerical records, derived tables, analysis programs, and SHA-256 integrity manifests. A unified CPU-only verification procedure reproduces the supported score-level analyses, including the longitudinal and epoch-300 summaries, 65 depth-specific token-readout interaction contrasts, and 130 direct positional-encoding contrasts from archived B4-C model-level results. Verification instructions and software dependencies are provided in the root README and requirements-numerical.txt . The distribution does not include raw benchmark images, trained checkpoint weights, or large extracted feature arrays. Full model retraining and GPU feature extraction are therefore outside the scope of the portable numerical verification package. summary: This record contains the code, district-level data, and stored outputs needed to reproduce the tables and figures of “Who Pays for Disasters? Evidence from a Household Panel in Peru” (Víctor Cárdenas-Santiago and Roberto Guerrero Compeán, Inter-American Development Bank, 2026). The paper uses Peru’s national household survey panel (ENAHO, 2007 to 2024) to study who reports disasters, how reports relate to welfare, and how incorrect household linkage in a rotating panel can reverse the distributive answer. Self-reported exposure is contrasted with daily satellite rainfall (CHIRPS) and with administrative emergency records (INDECI). Contents: All programs (Stata and Python) that build the household unit, estimate every table, and produce every figure. District-level CHIRPS extreme-rain measures and INDECI district-year records. The stored outputs (coefficients, intervals, counts) behind each table and figure, so that every number in the paper can be checked without running the code. A README with the correspondence between tables, programs and outputs, the order of execution, software requirements, and a manifest with the MD5 checksum of every file. Household-level files (ENAHO microdata from INEI and the analytical bases derived from them) are published in a separate record with restricted access. Extracting both records into the same folder merges them into one tree, and the programs then re-estimate all results. With this public record alone, all results can be verified against the stored outputs but not recomputed. ENAHO microdata are distributed free of charge by INEI at https://proyectos.inei.gob.pe/microdatos/ . Software: Stata 19.5 SE (reghdfe, ftools, eventstudyinteract, csdid, boottest) and Python 3.10 (pandas, numpy, scipy, pyreadstat, matplotlib). title: Who Pays For Disasters

summary: Unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral $n$-layer graphene exhibits a rich phase diagram with multiple distinct superconducting regions, whose microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we investigate the competition between charge-density-wave (CDW) and pair-density-wave (PDW) instabilities near the inner van Hove singularities (VHSs), using a patch renormalization-group approach with the realistic band structures incorporated. We identify two key findings. First, we find an effective attractive interaction emerging from purely repulsive interactions through RG flow in the presence of $C_3$ symmetry breaking. The resulting interaction structure, with two repulsive couplings and one attractive coupling, gives rise to competing CDW and PDW instabilities. Second, the competition is controlled by the detuning from the VHS. While CDW dominates near the VHS filling and at higher temperatures, PDW becomes the leading instability on either side of the VHS and at lower temperatures. This mechanism naturally produces two superconducting regions separated by a CDW-dominated regime, providing a possible qualitative explanation for the experimentally observed separation between SC1 and SC2.
title: Emergent Attraction and Competing Orders near the Van Hove Singularity in Rhombohedral $n$-layer Graphene

summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.
title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution

We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length. Within any fixed prompt the fairness label, response length and the presence of a protected-group token are collinear at $φ= 0.95$, partly by definition of the labelling rule, so no observational analysis can attribute the map to any of them, and no method in this family performs an experiment that could. The substantive claims fail independently: bias selectivity is not late-layer-concentrated on either model under either reference reading, and no head set we tested reduces the unfairness rate when ablated. Its complement, scored on the opposite label, reliably destroys refusal behaviour ($p = 2.7\times10^{-5}$), demonstrating that the pipeline detects effects at this scale.

summary: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are essential components for quantum-limited microwave measurement, but their dynamic range is often constrained by Kerr and other pump-induced nonlinear effects. In this work, we systematically study the performance of a parametric amplifier based on the linear inductive coupler (LINC). Starting from the driven-circuit Hamiltonian, we derive the effective three-wave-mixing amplifier model, including leading flux-driven nonlinear corrections relevant to realistic operation. We analyze the resulting gain response, saturation behavior, and intermodulation distortion, comparing them with representative state-of-the-art JPA designs. Our results show that the symmetry-protected structure of the LINC suppresses static Kerr nonlinearity. Moreover, suitable circuit-parameter optimization can further reduce the dressed-squeezing and driven-Kerr effects, leading to considerable improvements in power-handling metrics. These results identify the LINC architecture as a promising platform for high-linearity Josephson parametric amplification.
title: Quantum amplification with a linear quantum coupler

summary: Unequal couplings to a common emergent gauge field provide a continuous way to tune competing magnetic instabilities in an effective description of $U(1)$ spin-liquid mixtures. We study this mechanism in quantum electrodynamics in 2+1 dimensions with two families of four-component Dirac fermions. Combining a leading large-$N$ treatment with Schwinger--Dyson equations, we obtain chiral condensates representing Néel order in the two sectors. At fixed fermion number, the coupling ratio $κ=e_2^2/e_1^2$ controls which condensates develop. Depending on $N$, the phases with a single condensate are connected through either coexistence or a finite interval in which both fermion families remain gapless. The mass-generation thresholds are reciprocal, and the fermion gaps close with Miransky essential singularities. The renormalization group flow has a circular line of fixed points parametrized by the invariant ratio $κ$. At the calculated order, gauge-invariant staggered magnetization correlations have continuously varying exponents in the gapless regime, while the exponent for correlations between the two sectors is independent of $κ$. These results connect the competition between magnetic orders to a continuous family of critical theories and identify magnetic correlation signatures of the intervening gapless regime.
title: Competing Magnetic Orders and Continuously Varying Exponents in $U(1)$ Spin Liquids

summary: Unequal couplings to a common emergent gauge field provide a continuous way to tune competing magnetic instabilities in an effective description of $U(1)$ spin-liquid mixtures. We study this mechanism in quantum electrodynamics in 2+1 dimensions with two families of four-component Dirac fermions. Combining a leading large-$N$ treatment with Schwinger--Dyson equations, we obtain chiral condensates representing Néel order in the two sectors. At fixed fermion number, the coupling ratio $κ=e_2^2/e_1^2$ controls which condensates develop. Depending on $N$, the phases with a single condensate are connected through either coexistence or a finite interval in which both fermion families remain gapless. The mass-generation thresholds are reciprocal, and the fermion gaps close with Miransky essential singularities. The renormalization group flow has a circular line of fixed points parametrized by the invariant ratio $κ$. At the calculated order, gauge-invariant staggered magnetization correlations have continuously varying exponents in the gapless regime, while the exponent for correlations between the two sectors is independent of $κ$. These results connect the competition between magnetic orders to a continuous family of critical theories and identify magnetic correlation signatures of the intervening gapless regime.
